Read our Privacy notice

Rapist Russell Brand has been moved to a new prison days after he was jailed for rape and sexual assaults.

The 51-year-old comedian was jailed this week after being found guilty of raping one woman and sexually assaulting three others during his career.

According to The Sun on Sunday, he was moved out of HMP Wandsworth and transported to category C prison HMP Littlehey in Cambridgeshire on Friday.

The prison offers a large variety of extra-curricular activities for its inmates, including yoga, choir and indoor bowls.

HMP Littlehey also hosts an inter-wing football league.

open image in gallery HMP Littlehey offers a large variety of extra-curricular activities for its inmates, including yoga, choir and indoor bowls ( PA )

The Sun says concerns for Brand’s safety and him being deemed a low escape risk could have prompted the move.

According to the paper, his new confines consist of a single-person cell on the prison’s E Wing and he has yet to make contact with any of the other 1,200-odd inmates housed at the facility.

Brand was sentenced to a 10-and-a-half-year prison term on Monday afternoon.

He is expected to serve two-thirds of his prison sentence before being released on licence. Brand will be on the sex offenders’ register for life.

Russell Brand has since been accused of sexual misconduct and predatory behaviour by six more women, according to a report.

The new claims, published as part of an investigation by The Times and the Sunday Times, include allegations from one woman who claimed Brand had sex with her without her consent, then apologised.

open image in gallery Russell Brand this week began a 10-and-a-half-year prison sentence for raping a woman and sexually assaulting three others ( PA Wire )

The Times reported that the woman, who said she had an on-off relationship with Brand in the late 2000s after a professional meeting at his London home, said the comedian continued having sex with her despite her saying “No, stop”.

After the alleged incident, the woman said Brand apologised to her in person and by text message.

Another woman who encountered Brand when she was queuing to meet him with a friend in 2007 aged 19 says she told him during sex “It’s painful”.

She alleged Brand would not stop, adding: “And then it gets worse and it’s really painful. And I say ‘stop’ and he doesn’t stop.”

The woman claimed Brand said afterwards: “Tonight was consensual. Nobody did anything they didn’t want to do.”

The new allegations could not be reported until the criminal case against Brand was over to avoid prejudicing proceedings, but all of the women spoke to reporters before hearing the allegations in the trial.

News.title: Strictly’s Craig Revel Horwood slams Nikita Kuzmin for ‘taking the mick’ with ‘illegal lifts’ of partner Dani Dyer
News.content:
Strictly Come Dancing’s Craig Revel Horwood slammed professional dancer Nikita Kuzmin for “taking the mick” with “illegal lifts” of his celebrity partner Dani Dyer.

The pair took to the ballroom floor on Saturday (14 November) for a Paso Doble to Everybody Wants to Rule the World.

Following the performance, judge Craig Revel Horwood appeared unimpressed by the choreography, saying it was “littered with illegal lifts.”

He added: “You're taking the mick with four massive lifts in that. One foot should remain on the floor at all times.”

Despite this, he went on to say that the couple did a “fantastic, fantastic job”.

News.title: New UK music festival aimed at families to launch next summer
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A new family-friendly festival is coming to Leicestershire by the creator of Croatia’s Hideout Festival.

Blume Summer Camp, a three-day event, is a “celebration of music, food, nature and adventure, designed as much for parents as their children”.

From 6 to 8 August 2027, Stapleford Estate on the borders of Leicestershire and Rutland will host families for a weekend of electronic music, Balearic sounds, folk and jazz.

The festival has been created by husband-and-wife, Dan Blackledge, founder of Hideout Festival in Croatia, and singer Molly Blackledge, who represented the UK at Eurovision in 2014.

On the line-up so far are DJs including Erol Alkan, Luke Una, Jamz Supernova and Auntie Flo.

According to Blume: “Expect morning coffee raves in the woods, DJs before dinner and folk around the fire, with headliners on early so parents still get the tunes and enjoy the morning after.

“Three music spaces will include a listening lounge for vinyl and intimate performances, while Auntie Flo brings his Plants Can Dance project, turning signals from plants into music.”

Aside from the music, fire-cooked feasts by plant-based chef Gaz Oakley, a wellness and movement space, breathwork sessions, wood-fired saunas, cold plunges and hot tubs are all on the festival itinerary.

Families can also get involved with foraging, bushcraft, birdwatching and gardening, with den building, fire skills and marshmallow roasting at Base Camp.

Early-bird tickets go on sale on 17 November, with weekend tickets from £210 for adults, £126 for teenagers and £84 for children. Under-fours go free.

Weekend tickets include general camping with pre-pitched boutique bell tents and campervan options.

News.title: The needless trend illustrated by Spain v England that is hurting football
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Had football kept one simple little fascination, it would be hard not to indulge Declan Rice’s typical enthusiasm.

“You are going away to the Metropolitano, playing the world champions in a game to see who can top the group,” the midfielder said of England’s game in Madrid on Sunday.

“We have a massive motive… to beat Spain as the away team would be a massive thing for us.”

In other words, the benchmark. This is the level England will have to reach to win Euro 2028, as both Rice and Thomas Tuchel expounded on.

Except, for all the grandeur that the midfielder described, Uefa have lessened the stakes.

In the first two iterations of the Nations League, this game at the Metropolitano would not just be a game to win the group but a direct qualification play-off. Only the first-placed teams went through.

open image in gallery The rematch of Spain v England promises to be interesting but has less jeopardy than it should ( Getty )

And sure, it might not be the World Cup or the Euros, but the very prospect of elimination from a competition that does at least mean something would have naturally made this fixture more compelling.

As it is, with both teams secure in the top two well ahead of Croatia and Czech Republic, there’s a question over whether they will even play their best sides.

None of this is to say the game won’t be as enjoyable as the brilliant September meeting, it’s just that it’s not what it could have been.

And that fits with a needless trend in football right now. The current game apparently has an obsession with safety nets – something to catch the endless bloat.

Everything that could have expanded has expanded.

open image in gallery The expansion of the Nations League has taken the edge off today’s game ( Getty Images )

Uefa themselves started this with the Euros. In 2016, a total of 16 teams became 24, with 16 also going through to the knockout stages. The clean binary symmetry of the old two-from-four groups was gone. A team’s chances of a fourth game were expanded from 50 per cent to 67 per cent, bringing with them the convolutions of the best third-placed sides going through.

More safety nets.

In 2019, the Uefa model was followed by both the Asian Football Confederation and Confederation of African Football, who made the same changes to their continental competitions.

In 2024, it was Uefa’s own club competitions, creating the “football wallpaper” of the Champions League opening stage.

open image in gallery The Champions League group phase has become ‘football wallpaper’ ( Getty )

That has obviously had a lot of discussion, including on these very pages, and Uefa do have different reasons for the expansion of the Nations League.

They’re well aware that the old tournament qualification systems of two-year build-ups no longer work, especially because the Euros has expanded. Games were certainly meaning less there. They could see it in the broadcasting figures, and knew they needed to do something.

The Nations League is a smart solution, especially as it serves to constrict qualification to actually make those games more consequential.

And yet they still face the fundamental problem that no international football can come close to the emotional intensity of a tournament, which begs the question of why everyone would constantly seek to move further away from that; why you would seek to ensure more of football is less intense.

It’s when you put all of these together, after all, that you see how widespread this has become.

open image in gallery Spain and England should still produce an entertaining contest ( Getty Images )

There are safety nets everywhere, not that football’s authorities would necessarily see it like that.

Most of their reasons are obvious. This is boom time for global interest in football but, far from federations taking the main examples of why it became so popular, they just want to milk it as much as possible.

More safety nets means more games, which notionally means more money… and more, more, more.

Perhaps the big question is whether this will actually affect football’s future? Will it cause classic “market saturation”? Will people… start to turn off?

That feels unlikely in any meaningful way, but there are still a few layers to the answer, that probably requires more data.

Considerable anecdotal evidence now suggests that a lot of people go into some matchweeks – especially in the Champions League and Nations League – without really knowing who is playing. There’s barely even the old anticipation.

open image in gallery The Champions League group phase has little of the old anticipation ( AFP/Getty )

That is why it becomes “wallpaper football”. People still tune in, but mostly because it’s there, and it’s football. It’s still enjoyable but it just doesn’t create the same enthusiasm or emotional investment that games of proper stakes do. A certain purity has been clouded.

It’s hard not to think it will start to dilute the same commercial value they’re all desperately trying to maximise, too.

This also stands in such contrast with the intense global interest in the Premier League, precisely because it is perceived as so competitive.

One occasional counter-argument to that is that a domestic league is just the same principle as the Champions League opening stage, but extended… except it isn’t.

open image in gallery England will hope to stun Spain in Madrid ( Getty Images )

In a domestic league, every match – and every moment – contributes to that final position, which is the be all and end all of a season. It is self contained.

In knockout competitions, the primary goal of the preliminary round is just getting to another stage. And, sure, obviously it’s better to finish higher and get more favourable draws, but that’s still all secondary to just getting through.

There are now a lot more safety nets to that. They bring protection for more teams, but pose a touch more risk to the wider game than is considered.

News.title: Is Spain v England on TV? Channel, kick-off time and how to watch Nations League clash
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

England travel to Spain for the conclusion of the group stage of the Nations League with the goal of topping the A3 table and forcing the world champions into second place.

The winner of this Nations League tie will finish top of the group with Spain currently sitting first after a perfect run of five wins from five. Luis de le Fuente’s team defeated England 3-2 in a blockbuster clash back in September at Wembley. Lamine Yamal had put the visitors ahead before Anthony Gordon and Harry Kane wrestled back the advantage only for Alex Baena and Mikel Oyarzabal to clinch the win.

Thomas Tuchel’s side have won each of their four games since including two impressive victories over Croatia to leave them in contention to win the group. Tuchel has openly stated that is the aim for this international break and England can prove their credentials as a major competitior to win the Nations League title should they overcome Spain.

However, Spain are on a 42-match unbeaten run since a 1-0 loss to Colombia in March 2024 and will be difficult to defeat with the backing of a home crowd.

Here’s everything you need to know:

When is Spain v England?

Spain host England in the final group fixture of the Nations League at the Metropolitano Stadium on Sunday 15 November, with kick-off at 7.45pm GMT.

How can I watch it?

Viewers in the United Kingdom can watch the match live on ITV1, with coverage from 7pm GMT. A live stream will be available via ITVX.

Team news

Luis de la Fuente has said that Lamine Yamal is fit to feature for Spain having been left out of the squad for the 2-0 victory over Czechia on Thursday.

“Lamine is suffering from inflammation in his knee, he has fluid buildup,” he said, “Our medical staff, along with those of his club, assessed the situation, and I decided that, to avoid this trip. His recovery is going well, and we believe he’ll be with us on Friday”

Mikel Oyarzabal could also feature in the squad missed the Czechia match due to illness.

For England, Thomas Tuchel has no further issues following the 2-1 win over Croatia. Dan Burn was called up to the squad to replace Marc Guehi and is likely to start once again. Djed Spence and Ezri Konsa should be fit again having missed out on the previous game.

Tuchel could also hand out debuts to Josh King, James Hill and Jobe Bellingham.

Predicted line-ups

Spain XI: Simon; Porro, Cubarsi, Huijsen, Cucurella; Zubimendi, Ruiz; Yamal, Lopez, Baena; Torres

England XI: Pickford; Alexander-Arnold, Konsa, Burn, Hall; Rice, Anderson; Rogers, Bellingham, Gordon; Kane

News.title: What you can expect on the new £180,000 Four Seasons private jet experience
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Four Seasons has revealed a new $238,000 (£180,000) around-the-world private jet experience taking off in 2028, complete with exclusive access to Hampton Court Palace.

“Coastlines & Culture”, a 23-day journey from the US to the UK, is due to depart on 6 May 2028.

From San Francisco, passengers will cross the Pacific to Seoul to visit the Jingwansa Temple before stops in Hangzhou, China, and a day trip to discover the history of Shanghai.

In Sri Lanka, guests will visit a private cinnamon estate “tracing Ceylon cinnamon from harvest to quill and oil”.

Then it’s on to Swahili heritage in Zanzibar and the Red Sea in Sharm El Sheikh for a private yacht charter.

This is followed by a stay at the storied Grand-Hôtel du Cap-Ferrat and a privately chartered yacht excursion to Cannes, then a flight across the Channel for a final stop in Hampshire, England.

Here passengers can enjoy the English countryside with a “closer look at Britain's royal history, including exclusive access to Hampton Court Palace”.

The private jet tour will feature famous Four Seasons properties including Four Seasons Hotel Hangzhou at West Lake, Four Seasons Resort Sharm El Sheikh and Four Seasons Hotel Hampshire.

The custom Airbus A321neo-LR operated by Titan Airways Limited is configured to hold just 48 travellers.

Itineraries for four other departures in 2027 include stops in the Great Barrier Reef, the pyramids of Giza, Seychelles, Galapagos Islands and African savannah.

Each journey features a dedicated “journey team”, which includes a concierge, executive chef and journey physician.

Marc Speichert, executive vice president and chief commercial officer for the Four Seasons, said: “Curating a new private jet itinerary requires immense thought and care. We consider not only where we take our guests, but how we pair destinations to bring different parts of the world together into one seamless and memorable journey.

“With Coastlines & Culture, we're able to bring together destinations rarely experienced within a single journey, creating moments of awe and discovery, and opening the door to experiences guests may never have imagined possible, all grounded in the genuine care and thoughtful service that define Four Seasons.”

News.title: Princess Kate to make royal tour comeback with William after cancer battle
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The Princess of Wales will make a return to major overseas royal tours when she joins her husband in India for his Earthshot Prize awards ceremony.

Speculation had been mounting Kate would make the trip with William to host city Mumbai after a number of reports indicated she would fly to the subcontinent.

Kensington Palace has confirmed from Monday the prince and princess will take part in three days of royal events “celebrating innovation, sustainability, youth leadership and the enduring connections between the United Kingdom and India”.

The couple are expected to meet Bollywood stars as they learn about India’s hugely popular film industry, celebrate the country’s passion for cricket and the highlight will be Tuesday’s Earthshot Prize Awards night – when winners in five categories will each receive £1 million.

The visit is a significant milestone for Kate and will be her first long-haul overseas trip since she announced her cancer diagnosis in March 2024.

She was successfully treated at the Royal Marsden hospital for the undisclosed form of the disease, before declaring herself in remission the following January.

open image in gallery Kate last attended an Earthshot Prize awards ceremony in the US city of Boston, joining her husband on the event’s featured green carpet for the glittering presentation in December 2022 ( PA )

William said in an interview earlier this year his wife was “edging herself back” into doing more overseas visits after her cancer journey, but cautioned royal trips took their toll so we have to “make sure she’s okay and rested”.

His comments were made in May after Kate completed a two-day visit to the Italian city of Reggio Emilia, near Bologna, on a fact-finding visit to learn about a unique form of early years teaching pioneered in the city.

Kate last attended an Earthshot Prize awards ceremony in the US city of Boston, joining her husband on the event’s featured green carpet for the glittering presentation in December 2022.

Just over six months later, the prince and princess were guests at the Middle East wedding of the Crown Prince of Jordan – and Kate made solo trips to France in autumn 2023 to watch England’s Rugby World Cup campaign in her role as patron of the Rugby Football Union.

The couple’s last major tour was to the Caribbean in March 2022, a trip that was heavily criticised for images that smacked of “colonialism” – but they also received a warm welcome from many Caribbeans.

William and Kate’s visit was seen by some commentators as a landmark moment in royal tours – when growing awareness of racial equality, in light of the Black Lives Matter movement, meant future Commonwealth tours would have to be sensitive to these issues.

open image in gallery Speculation had been mounting Kate would make the trip with William to host city Mumbai after a number of reports indicated she would fly to the subcontinent ( PA )

The prince’s Earthshot project is halfway through its decades-long cycle to recognise and reward ideas to help “repair” the planet and the event has already been staged in London, Singapore, Cape Town, Boston and Rio de Janeiro.

Since its launch in 2021, William has managed to attract a host of stars to his cause, from Hollywood actors Leonardo DiCaprio, Matthew McConaughey and Cate Blanchett to broadcaster and naturalist Sir David Attenborough – and former prime minister of New Zealand Jacinda Ardern.

The initiative was inspired by former US president John F Kennedy’s Moonshot project, which set scientists the challenge of placing an astronaut on the Moon and returning him safely – and in the process helped advance mankind’s achievements.

William and Kate will also attend the inaugural Children’s Earthshot Awards ceremony, which encouraged youngsters across India to tackle environmental issues under the “I Can Earthshot Challenge”.

The prince has discussed the project with Prince George, Princess Charlotte and Prince Louis, an initiative that invited nine to 17-year-old’s to look beyond environmental awareness and take meaningful action.

Jason Knauf, Earthshot’s chief executive officer, said: “As we prepare to host the Earthshot Prize Summit in Mumbai, these remarkable children remind us that local community action, driven by youthful optimism and determination, is vital to repairing our planet.

“We can’t wait to celebrate them in Mumbai for our biggest edition yet.”

News.title: Japanese police arrest US Air Force captain for suspected drink-driving in Okinawa
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Japanese police have arrested a US Air Force captain on suspicion of drink-driving on the island of Okinawa, the second American service member held on that suspicion since the US military imposed alcohol restrictions there after a murder case in October.

The 27-year-old was arrested on Saturday at about 3.09am local time (6.09pm GMT on Friday) while driving on a road in Okinawa City, a spokesman for Okinawa prefectural police said.

He was stationed at Kadena Air Base on the island, Kyodo News reported.

Police arrested him on the spot near an entertainment district, and his blood alcohol level was about three times the legal limit, according to police, The Japan News reported. He told police that he believed his level was below the legal limit and that he thought he would be fine to drive because his home was nearby.

"It is not clear if he violated the curfew," the spokesman said, referring to the restrictions imposed by US officials.

The arrest came a week after Tokyo and Washington agreed to measures aimed at preventing crimes by US service members on Okinawa, following a murder allegedly involving an American Marine that triggered outrage.

In October, a 20-year-old Marine was arrested for allegedly killing a woman in a hotel room in Naha, on Okinawa, and stealing her belongings. US forces in Okinawa prefecture then banned all service members from leaving their bases and from drinking alcohol, both on and off base, between 7 and 9 October.

The US military designated the following 30 days as a period of reflection and barred personnel from leaving between midnight and 5am. Another Marine was arrested on 31 October on suspicion of drink-driving.

US officials said last week they would extend the curfew for lower-ranking service members through 7 December, and ban all service members from drinking alcohol outside their homes between midnight and 5am.

The US military has about 54,000 personnel stationed in Japan, mostly on Okinawa, and crimes committed by its members have long strained relations between the two close security allies.

News.title: Ireland stay in hunt for final place despite complacency creeping in
News.content:
Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of this Nations Championship fifth-round Test between Ireland and Fiji at Aviva Stadium in Dublin.

Ireland are third in the Northern Hemisphere standings, having played a game less than England and France above them, but a point bonus victory this evening would put Andy Farrell’s side level with Steve Borthwick’s men and keep them in the mix for top spot. Meanwhile, Fiji are rock bottom of the South Hemisphere table, with a miserable points difference of -133, and lost 54-17 to France last time out.

Tadhg Beirne, who is poised to captain his country for the first time on home soil this evening, said Ireland are aiming to carry on the positive momentum following their 42-12 win over Argentina eight days ago, but feels his side can still improve. “The big focus for us is to continue building on our performance, particularly from last week,” he remarked.

“We laid down a foundation of how we want to play, but we’re certainly not satisfied with that. I think there were patches of us playing really well there, but there were also patches where we weren’t to the standard that we’re going to hold ourselves to.”

News.title: Botham’s grandson inspires Wales to historic win over All Blacks
News.content:
The second half of Wales’ Nations Championship started with a hard-fought 28-21 bonus point victory over Japan last Saturday. Steve Tandy’s side sit fifth in the Northern Hemisphere table, but just five points separate them from second-place England, and they still have a tonne of pride to play for as they aim to finish as high as possible in the group.

Speaking ahead of the encounter, Tandy said: “We’re excited for the opportunity we have against New Zealand. It was good to get the win last Saturday, but some elements of our execution weren’t where we wanted.

“We have to go up another level this weekend and be more ruthless. We have one of the best teams in the world coming. We want to be better and put in an 80-minute performance.”

Meanwhile, New Zealand arrive in the Welsh capital in imperious form, having won their opening four Nations Championship matches and boasting a +73 points difference. South Africa’s defeat has opened the door for the resurgent All Blacks to pounce, and they’ll be brimming with confidence following their eye-catching 43-21 triumph against Scotland at Murrayfield a week ago.

As for the team news, Tandy has made four alterations to the starting XV that overcame Japan. Taine Basham is poised for his first international appearance since the 2024 Six Nations, while James Botham, Gabriel Hamer-Webb and Adam Beard also begin the contest. The influential Aaron Wainwright is out with a minor calf problem.

All Blacks Head Coach has ordered 10 changes to the 23-man squad that brushed Scotland aside. Forwards including George Bower, Asafo Aumua, Josh Lord, Anton Segner and backs such as Richie Mo’unga, Anton Lienert-Brown and Fehi Fineanganofo all start for the heavily rotated visitors. Full-back Beauden Barrett will captain New Zealand for the first time, in his 149th Test, while Will Jordan is unavailable because of a hamstring issue.

Kick-off is at 14:10, with team news following now.

News.title: Joseph a star in the making as England revel in role of bullies
News.content:
England have made wholesale changes, with only five members from the starting XV against Australia remaining. Henry Pollock starts at eight, Will Joseph earns just his second cap on the wing and Archie McParland is set for his international debut off the bench.

“Japan are a very well-coached side who will challenge us in different ways, and we know we will need to bring intensity throughout the game,” said Borthwick. “The atmosphere at Allianz Stadium last week was incredible. The players really fed off the energy in the stadium, and we are really looking forward to being back on Saturday [today].”

Japan’s first game of this month’s fixtures ended in defeat as they lost 28-21 against Wales in Cardiff last weekend. That defeat means they have just one win from their first four games of the Nations Championship, which came against Italy in the opening game, and they sit second bottom in the southern hemisphere standings.

“We have had really good training to prepare us for the game we are expecting against England,” Jones said. “We had two days of very settled and pretty training but Wednesday was quite dirty. We had to adapt to certain situations and in the end we did it really well. I was really pleased with the players, really pleased with their effort, really pleased with the way they adapted to the situations. I am looking forward to going to Twickenham with this young Japanese team that is going to play the house down.”

Kick-off from Allianz Stadium is at 4.40pm.

News.title: France pull off one of their greatest wins as Erasmus mind games backfire
News.content:
Given Les Bleus’ injuries, only the 1999 World Cup semi-final victory over New Zealand can come close to this win over the back-to-back world champions, South Africa. The Nations Championship, with the Springboks previously unbeaten, has been blown wide open. Crikey, given these two could meet in a World Cup semi-final next year, rugby’s blue-riband event in Australia has been blown wide open.

And how lucky are we. France did not score a point in the second half and South Africa’s comeback befitted a champion side, but these audacious hosts regaled their Parisian audience with a rugby feast. Rassie Erasmus, the Springboks’ head coach, said that he was nervous before the game and so he should have been. Fabien Galthié, his counterpart, had promised some fun and games, but Erasmus could not help himself: not long before kick-off, he pulled the coup de théâtre, switching his starting and replacement front rows. Time will tell whether such a move was legal.

“We didn’t play well,” said Erasmus. “I can’t find a lot of excuses. They were on top of their game and we were a little bit off. It was one point here and there. They took their opportunities and we didn’t. We weren’t just outplayed, we were outsmarted.”

“I think we’ve killed our dreams for the Nations Championship with this result,” he added, suggesting he thinks New Zealand will beat England next week.

Demons were present for both sides, mainly France. South Africa lost Jasper Wiese to a 20-minute red card for a nasty ruck clear-out – just as Lood de Jager had received in the visitors’ win last year – and, at the end, there was a reverse of that utterly compelling World Cup quarter-final on the same turf. This time, it was South Africa desperately searching for victory, having dominated the scrum and scoring all three of their tries from close range or mauls.

News.title: England’s batting capitulates in defeat to lift Australia’s spirits
News.content:
“We weren’t quick enough to adapt to the conditions, we talked extensively leading into the game about the surface here at Optus,” Brendon McCullum, England’s coach, said. “It’s a bit like batting on a trampoline, there are certain shots that are very difficult to execute. We talked about trying to put those away.”

McCullum called for his team to scrap a bit more, and at least acknowledged this time that driving on the up was unwise.

“KP has got such a nice manner about him,” he said. “He sees his role to get the talent to perform on the world stage. His message will be measured but firm – adapting to conditions, what could we have done, trying to drive the ball on the up is not wise. Next time we hit a surface like this we have to try and work it better.”

After a quiet start, both openers fell tamely. Ben Duckett prodded Johnson to point, then Banton had a booming drive at Bartlett and was caught behind.

Enter Beardman. When he came on to bowl the 10th over of the innings, there was palpable excitement from his home crowd, who had watched another West Australian, Mike Hussey, present his ODI cap before the toss. Later in the day, Hussey was probably glad he rebuffed England’s recent approach to work with their Test batsmen.

Beardman, who is a mentee of Dennis Lillee and has a gorgeously rhythmical action that helped him touch 90mph, started with a maiden to Root, then found just another movement away from Brook to invite the edge. On the occasion of his 200th ODI, Root had been dropped badly on three off Bartlett, and his only boundary came when Beardman found his an inside edge and the ball flew past his stumps.

The pressure told, and Root edged a big drive behind, where Josh Inglis took the third of his five catches. That sparked a collapse of five for 10, with Jordan Cox edging behind prodding in defence, before Curran was caught on the fence hooking for nought. Beardman’s five-fer was completed when Liam Dawson – selected ahead of Adil Rashid again – skewed a flat-footed drive to backward point. Overton followed in the next over, leaving England 65 for eight, with their lowest ever ODI score, 86, inevitably recorded against Australia in 2001, appearing a distant possibility.

A stand of 37 from Will Jacks and Gus Atkinson averted that particular indignity, and the fear of being bowled out for double figures. But the total was never enough and, despite Atkinson bowling Head first ball, the chase was painfully routine thanks to Marsh’s early barrage.

News.title: Kane bends game to his will on record-breaking night
News.content:
Good evening and welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of England vs Croatia in the Nations League, with the hosts’ captain Harry Kane set to become the country’s most-capped player.

The 33-year-old has enjoyed a memorable few weeks, becoming the first English Ballon d’Or winner in 25 years and following it up with a new Bayern Munich contract, and an appearance at Wembley tonight will take him clear of Peter Shilton’s record of 125 England caps.

Kane scored twice in his record-equalling appearance against Czech Republic at Wembley last month, extending his international tally to 91 goals – a total that is unrivalled for England.

“It’s not about me – it’s about the team,” Kane said before tonight’s landmark moment. “I love coming to every England camp. I love playing every game and representing the country in the best way possible.”

The 3-0 home victory over Czech Republic left England on nine points after four Nations League group games, with a 2-0 win in the away contest and a 7-0 thumping of Croatia coming after a 3-2 defeat against world champions Spain.

Thomas Tuchel will be hoping that his side can inflict another heavy defeat on Croatia this evening, but a draw will be enough to book their place in the quarter-finals, with the group’s top two teams progressing.

While Kane will collect plaudits for his 126th cap, attention will also be on a potential first, with Jude Bellingham’s younger brother, Jobe, included in a senior England squad for the first time.

The two Bellinghams appearing together in a senior match would be a new experience for them, while it would be the first time that brothers have taken to the field together for England in 19 years.

“I can’t ignore it, but obviously with Jude being here too, it’s a great, great feeling for the family,” Jobe said on the Football Association’s England app. “It’s quite special, to be honest. It’s such a huge bonus on top of something that’s already so special and so great.”

News.title: Experts hail a “milestone” as TB deaths fall by more than a third in 10 years
News.content:
The number of people dying from tuberculosis has dropped by more than a third over the last 10 years but progress against the disease is still too slow, according to the World Health Organization.

Figures from WHO’s annual TB report showed that the lung disease took the lives of an estimated 1.13 million people in 2025, down from 1.7m in 2015, a drop of 35 per cent.

While WHO hailed this as a major milestone in achieving global targets - albeit five years too late - it said that progress in wiping out TB was still too slow.

Africa and Europe have made the greatest progress in reducing deaths, with numbers halving on both continents over the 10-year period. India and China - countries that have high burdens of the disease - also cut deaths by 35 per cent.

The report also showed that an estimated 10.6million people contracted the disease in 2025, a reduction of just 75,000 since 2024.

TB - still the world’s leading infectious disease killer - is preventable and curable, and is caused by the bacillus Mycobacterium tuberculosis, which is spread when infected people cough or sneeze.

The disease has been around for centuries, and has been described as the quintessential disease of poverty as it spreads in areas of low quality housing, among people with poor nutrition and immunity. It is a particular risk to people who are HIV positive.

Treatment requires a six-month long regimen of medication, and while treatments have become less toxic in recent years, they still take a heavy toll on patients and have a range of side effects, including at the most extreme deafness. Adherence to medication is also a problem.

News.title: Low-cost parenting app halves rates of sexual violence amongst teenagers in Tanzania
News.content:
A low cost parenting intervention has more than halved rates of sexual violence among teenage girls in Tanzania, a study has shown.

The ParentApp digital parenting programme for families is aimed at reducing rates of violence experienced by teenagers of both sexes.

Researchers found the programme helped bolster family relationships and enabled mothers and fathers to better communicate with their children at what is often a tricky stage of their development.

The programme, led by Oxford University and the University of Cape Town in partnership with the Tanzanian government, the World Health Organization and Unicef, combines in-person and mobile parenting support.

Parents have an introductory session with a facilitator and then undertake 12 weekly sessions online. They also join a WhatsApp group with other parents where they can discuss problems and support one another.

The randomized controlled trial, published in The Lancet, included 2,396 children aged 10–17 and 2,396 parents and carers across 80 urban and rural areas.

Families were randomly assigned to receive either ParentApp or a comparison app focused on safe water and hygiene. Researchers analysing the results did not know which app each family received.

At the 14-month follow-up, girls in families participating in the ParentApp initiative reported a 67% reduction in sexual violence; a 54% reduction in sexual exploitation and an improvement in parent-child relationships. The successes were less marked in boys, however.

Violence against children is widespread globally: Unicef data shows that around one in five girls and women and one in seven boys and men globally have experienced sexual violence as children.

Lucie Cluver, professor of child and family social work at Oxford University and one of the authors of the study, said the intervention was aimed at helping parents and children talk to one another and discuss situations before they arise.

In Tanzania, for example, teenage girls might get a motorbike taxi late at night, potentially putting them in a dangerous situation.

“What you’re doing is making plans and problem solving ahead of these risky situations that teenagers end up in. And you’re building trust and the relationship so you can have these difficult conversations,” said Prof Cluver.

She said she was surprised at how big an impact the intervention had on sexual violence: teenage girls reported that because the app helped improve communication with their parents and carers they did not feel the need to go out as much.

The programme cost around $6 per family but researchers calculated that it goes up to around $10 per family if 20% are given smartphones. A traditional in-person parenting intervention generally costs around $120 per family.

Engagement in the sessions was high - around 70 per cent of participants completed the course - and some parents kept in touch with one another after the programme.

However, the authors of the study stressed that while the app focused on families there remains a need to prevent violence against children in other settings, such as schools and religious institutions. There also needs to be a broader societal push to address the scourge.

“The app isn’t the answer to everything - it’s just one part of the puzzle,” said Prof Cluver.

Prof Cluver said she hoped future versions of the programme would include greater focus on digital harms and test whether parents could take the lead themselves.

The programme is being rolled out in other countries, including Mexico, Panama and South Africa, and is easily adaptable for different contexts.

“Tanzania only has 20% smartphone use and we thought if it works in one of the hardest places to do a digital intervention it could work anywhere,” she said.

She said the study showed how parenting was a universal experience, with the majority focused on what is best for their children.

“Parents feel powerless. We live in a world where our kids are facing risks and parents just want to help,” added Prof Cluver.

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino leaves Man Utd fans drooling as USA destroy Haiti 6-0 at David Beckham’s stadium
Sports.content:
Next

MAURICIO POCHETTINO faced up to a partisan crowd and watched his side survive a tasty battle on the pitch.

He can expect plenty of the same next Sunday – only much, much worse.



It’s fair to say his first match as Old Trafford chief at Liverpool will be far tougher than a Concacaf Nations League quarter-final clash against Haiti.

But Pochettino, 54, will want his new squad to at least show some of the grit and determination from his boys at David Beckham’s Nu Stadium in south Florida.



A thumping 6-0 win – similar to what his US side dished up here – would be a nice way for the new man in the Red Devils hotseat to start, too.

Andoni Iraola’s men are obviously in a different stratosphere to a Haiti team high on effort, yet severely lacking quality at international level.



Yet United fans watching this thrashing would have at least seen a high-energy, well-organised outfit comprehensively dealing with a vociferous crowd and punishing their outclassed opponents with ruthless efficiency.

How the Red Devils faithful need some of that following their car crash start to the campaign.

Over 300,000 Haitians live in this area and they brought serious noise and passion.

So Poch was thankful to Celtic’s Auston Trusty for putting his side one up after just nine minutes.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The US always looked the more dangerous, but Haiti – who were classed as the home team as serious unrest in their homeland continues to cause issues – were bang up for the fight.

Fulham‘s Antonee Robinson set the marker with a wild tackle early on, while the half came to the close off the back of a tasty spat involving Bournemouth’s Tyler Adams and Middlesbrough midfielder Sebastian Berhalter.

Haiti, led in attack by Sunderland’s Wilson Isidor, had their chances, with MLS-based Danley Jean Jacques wasting their best chance on 16 minutes.

But the gap in class eventually told, with New York Red Bulls frontman Julian Zakrzewski finishing off the type of red-hot, pacy counter-attack the United faithful will be hoping finally brings life to their wretched campaign.

AC Milan’s Christian Pulisic fed Robinson whose ball was sweetly tucked home by Zakrzewski.



Pulisic then smashed in from the penalty spot to seriously dampen Haiti spirits before curling home a classy fourth to keep Pochettino smiling all the way into his United States swansong on Tuesday.

Juventus’ Weston McKennie headed in a fifth on 68 minutes before those brilliant Haiti fans thought they finally had something to cheer about just moments later.

The Concacaf minnows tore down the other end and Lenny Joseph, who plays in Hungary for Ferencvaros, tucked in a consolation.

The “home” fans celebrated like they had won the World Cup. Sadly for them, it was chalked off for offside.

Pochettino, however, who saw Folarin Balougun make it six on 82 minutes, will be delighted with his night’s work in the Magic City.



Since taking charge in 2024, the former Tottenham and Chelsea chief has impressed his US Soccer bosses, even if this summer’s last-16 World Cup exit was ultimately a bitter disappointment.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

His final match in charge will be the second leg of this quarter-final in Cincinnati, before he jetsoff to Manchester and to get down to some serious business back in the Premier League.

When the boos and catcalls rain down at Anfield next weekend, playing Haiti in Miami – no matter if the whole stadium was against his team – will seem like a glorious walk in the park.

Ronaldo, 41, ended a 23-year run with his national team following a public spat with manager Jorge Jesus during last month’s international break.



The Al-Nassr star was left fuming after he was benched in Norway and walked out on the team before claiming Jesus went back on his word twice – including over plans to clear the Manchester United legend’s name in a press conference about the fallout.

The Real Madrid icon went into detail in a near 2,000-word rant on social media in which he claimed he signed off on an eight-point statement the manager would issue as part of a public apology that was never read out.



Portugal kicked off the post-Ronaldo era with a Nations League clash against Denmark in Braga.

But it couldn’t have gone any worse as they were hammered 4-1 at home.



Jesus‘ side found themselves trailing at half-time following ex-Tottenham ace Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg’s penalty.

Napoli star Rasmus Hojlund then continued his exciting rebirth with a brace following the end of a torrid three-year stint at United, who signed him for a staggering £72million in 2023.

Sports.title: Ex-Prem winner Wes Morgan ordered to pay £274k in child support to two mums after seven-year legal battle
Sports.content:
Next

FORMER Premier League winning captain Wes Morgan has been ordered to pay at least £274k in child support arrears after a “gruelling” seven-year legal battle by two mums.

The ex-Leicester City idol, 42, was in court with his former partners Leyla Antoniou, 41, and Karla Morrell, 35, who each have a son with him.



It comes after The Sun on Sunday reported in July Morgan was accused of hiding assets and income totalling as much as £5million to avoid paying the correct amount.

Now, following a landmark court ruling, a judge has ruled that Morgan tried dodging the Child Maintenance Service (CMS) despite being a wealthy earner.



The scathing 23-page judgement by Lady Justice King slammed Morgan’s legal case as “absurd” and accused him of creating a “power imbalance” that the CMS “was designed to correct.”

Morgan captained Leicester City to Premier League glory against all odds 10 years ago in 2016.

After retiring from playing football in 2021, he convinced the CMS he had no income or employment and therefore qualified for nil payments.

He argued it meant he no longer had to pay the women a total of £80,000 a year in child support payments – despite court orders already being in place for that amount.

Under the CMS rules, existing child support orders were immediately cancelled after a routine update in a father’s declaration of earnings or assets.

Now a judge, Lady Justice King, sitting at the Court of Appeal, has reversed that.



The burden was also on the mothers to prove Morgan could financially support their children, but the new ruling now puts the onus on the father to go back to court to change any court order.

Family justice charity Right2Equality warned a legal victory for Morgan would have created “significant uncertainty for countless children” who survive through CMS payments.

Father-of-four Morgan, who has two other children with wife Sheneen Fisher whom he married in July 2021, even admitted in a witness statement last year that he knew the CMS decision to reduce his maintenance to nil was “wrong”.



Lady Justice King, sitting with two other judges, confirmed a previous ruling last year that Morgan had exceeded the annual £156,000 earnings cap from 2021 to 2024, the period he claimed he was unemployed.

She said: “The application of the CMS formula system of assessment for child maintenance is intended to provide a predictable, speedy and efficient way in which to determine the liability of a non-resident parent to pay maintenance to the carer of a relevant child.

“It is unfortunate that notwithstanding that being the case, the courts and the First-tier Tribunal have now been involved for a period of over seven years in order to secure an outcome which will ensure that the father honours his obligations to these two children.”

She added: “It should be remembered that throughout all of this, the father continues to have an income far in excess of the £3,000 maximum for the purposes of the CMS.”

Ms Antoniou has a 12-year-old son from her previous relationship with Morgan, while Ms Morrell has an eight-year-old son from her previous relationship with him.



The Sun on Sunday revealed how the ex-Prem ace was accused of “deliberately” hiding assets including a “profitable” real estate company called WM5, rental properties and a luxury Villa in Portugal.

It amounted to around £5million, the Court of Appeal heard.

It was also claimed that Morgan continued to earn an income after retirement through punditry work with Sky Sports and BBC Sport, and as a scout for his boyhood club Nottingham Forest.

Jody Atkinson, representing Ms Morrell, said: “She did not accept that the father was unemployed especially when her son saw him on television doing punditry.”

Speaking after the ruling, Ms Morrell spoke out against Morgan’s “questionable legal tactics to cruelly deny” her son payments he needed.



She described her seven-year battle to get justice as “gruelling”, “emotional” and “upsetting”.

She told The Sun: “I wish to thank the Court of Appeal for their landmark decision. It has been a very difficult and traumatic few years to bring justice for my son.

“I have suffered painful setbacks and it is upsetting that his father, Mr. Morgan, has used questionable legal tactics to cruelly deny our son the support he needs when he could easily have provided such support.

“My experience during this case has shown me the flaws and injustice of the child maintenance system.

“I have been working with decision makers and others to try and bring reform and balance to the system. I will continue to campaign for fairness.”



She added: “This decision of the Court of Appeal is so important. It shifts the burden squarely on to the non-resident parents to go back to court, not to hoodwink a government agency so they can intimidate parents looking after their children.”

The Court of Appeal ruled that any changes by CMS only updated existing calculations and did not cancel previous orders.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

All three judges agreed that if all parties cannot come to an agreement, the cases will go back to the Family Court.

Both women have run up substantial legal costs during the seven years of fighting.

Sports.title: Declan Rice blasts himself for ‘average’ displays during England’s World Cup campaign
Sports.content:
Next

FIRED-UP Declan Rice wants to show he is back to his best against world champions Spain — after confessing he was “average” at the World Cup.

The Arsenal midfielder, 27, set to win his 82nd cap in Sunday’s Nations League decider, is still frustrated at his own performances at the tournament.



England beat France to come third, having suffered a painful semi-final defeat to Argentina, who then lost to Spain in the final.

Victory for Thomas Tuchel’s men here in Madrid will see the Three Lions pip their opponents to top spot in Nations League Group 3 and earn them a place among the seeds.



And Rice is determined to put on a dazzling display. He said: “By my standards it was an average World Cup.

“Some games I played well, I applied myself well and did what I needed to do in terms of my standards and level.

“France was probably my best game, DR Congo, I played really well. Some of the other games I didn’t play too well.

“It’s one of those things, you reflect and look back at it — a 69-game season at the end of a title-winning season, a Champions League loss into a World Cup.

“It’s annoying because at the World Cup you want to be at your best, you want to be fresh, you want to be ready.

“It’s annoying I couldn’t perform how I did at Arsenal at the back end of the season. I’m ready for the next set of games and to apply myself in the right way.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Rice was instrumental to Arsenal winning the Premier League title and reaching the Champions League final, which the Gunners lost on penalties to Paris Saint-Germain.

But his back pain, caused by his hamstring issue, meant he struggled physically during the World Cup.

It continued into the new Prem campaign and was enough to see him pull out of international action in September — with Tuchel’s blessing.



Now, he is fighting fit and said: “I feel really good. I am building up to being at 100 per cent. I feel like I am closer to that than what I was a few weeks ago.

“The first four or five games of the season were like my pre-season. I was using those to get fit, get sharp and over the last few weeks my performances have picked up. The body is good and I am in a good place.”

England face Spain at Atletico Madrid’s stadium for their League A group’s top spot.

Rice added: “Playing the world champions away in a game to see who can top the group. It can’t get any bigger than that.

“We have a massive motive to win the group, to beat Spain, as the away team, would be a massive thing for us.”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

And Rice, who signed a five-year deal in 2023 until 2028 eased any doubts on a new deal at the Emirates. He said: “A new contract hopefully on the horizon soon.

“I’m extremely lucky that I’m at a club like Arsenal. The manager shows me so much trust.”

Sports.title: Middlesbrough slap astonishing £70m price tag on Will Lankshear with Newcastle and Leeds considering transfer move
Sports.content:
Next

MIDDLESBROUGH are determined to resist any bids for England hopeful Will Lankshear in January – by slapping a £70million price tag on his head

Plenty of Premier League scouts have witnessed Lankshear’s astronomical progress in the flesh this term – including Tottenham, the club that sold him in the summer.



But it would take an astronomical offer for Boro to consider letting the striker go as they target promotion.

Should the Teessiders go up, they are set to make more than double that fee so selling makes little sense.



Lankshear has impressed so much since moving to the Riverside for an initial £10million in the summer that England were genuinely considering calling him up to their senior squad this month.

FA technical director John McDermott has been tracking his progress for some time and was in attendance at the Kassam Stadium to watch Lankshear play Sunderland in the FA Cup when on loan from Spurs at Oxford.



The 21-year-old has since moved permanently to Boro where he has blasted 13 goals in as many league games to send the club second in the Championship, level on points with table-toppers Birmingham.

He has another two goals in the Carabao Cup, taking his haul to 15 in 16 games altogether.

The former Arsenal academy player missed out on international action this month – either for the Under-21s or the seniors – due to a minor hamstring injury.

Scouts from Newcastle and Leeds are believed to have watched Lankshear this term, as well as former club Spurs.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

But Tottenham do NOT have a buy-back clause on Lankshear, as these are not permitted in transfers between Premier League and EFL clubs.

Spurs do hold matching rights, meaning they can match any offers another club has accepted for Lankshear in the future, as well as a 20 per cent sell-on clause.

They are also due another £10m in add-ons from Boro should they be triggered.

SunSport understands among those add-ons are both playing and scoring for the England senior team.



While there are a number of clubs keeping a keen eye on Lankshear, Boro are understood to have received no enquiries for the forward so far.

Lankshear’s career has so far had echoes of the two centre-forwards in Thomas Tuchel’s senior squad.

He came through Spurs’ academy, as did Harry Kane, but before then moved to Sheffield United, because of their expertise in developing powerful No9s like Dominic Calvert-Lewin.

Sports.content:
Brazil players separated from referee by security as Carlo Ancelotti sees red vs Japan

Security were called upon to de-escalate matters late into Brazil's shock 3-2 loss to Japan on Saturday, when Jansen Foo Chuan Hui sent off Carlo Ancelotti and one of his key players

View 2 Images Security had to move Brazil players away from Jansen Foo Chuan Hui (Image: X)

Security had to separate Carlo Ancelotti and his Brazil players from the referee during Saturday's 3-2 loss to Japan, as a friendly match quickly turned sour. The game was all square at 2-2 headed into stoppage time thanks to strikes from Takefusa Kubo and Keito Nakamura, as well as a Vinicius Junior brace.

‌



‌



However, the already tense atmosphere turned frosty a minute into extra time, when Tatsuhiro Sakamoto scored the winner for the Asian nation. Referee Jansen Foo Chuan Hui saw now problem in Takumi Minamino's multiple challenges of Joao Gomes, which may have been given as a foul on another day - especially considering Gomes remained on the ground as his opponent ran off with the ball at his feet.

‌



Sakamoto then dinked the ball over Pedro Morisco to give Japan a late goal, and ultimately the winner. Brazil were quick to confront the official while Japanese players wheeled off in celebration, as VAR confirmed that the goal was fine to stand.

‌

Ancelotti and Raphinha - who had just been substituted - meanwhile, were shown red cards, leading to yet further appeals from the Brazilian national team. Security were then forced to intervene and pull Ancelotti, as well as Vini Junior and Bruno Guimaraes, away from the Singaporean official in the aftermath.

In the aftermath, Ancelotti told the media Chuan Hui's reason for sending him off in the first place. He explained: "He gave me the red card because he said I was not able to control the bench, and that all the players were on the field, that is the reason.

Twisting the knife further on the officiating, the Italian added: "The result, obviously, is conditioned by the attitude of the referee, who did not blow the whistle. But it's not his fault; it was a high-level match, and I think he didn't have the experience to manage this type of match."

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel responds after Spain boss hits back over racism message to England stars
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel responds after Spain boss hits back over racism message to England stars

Luis de la Fuente sent a message directly to Thomas Tuchel after the England manager said he would remind his team of protocols ahead of a first game in Madrid since players were subjected to abuse in 2004

View 2 Images Thomas Tuchel hit back at Spanish reporters ahead of Sunday's game vs Spain

Thomas Tuchel has become involved in a war of words over a racism storm ahead of England’s Nations League clash with Spain.

‌



‌



Tuchel hit back over questions from Spanish journalists in Madrid when he was asked about comments he made after England’s win over Croatia. This will be the first time England have played in Madrid since 2004 - they actually refused to play in 2009 and the game was moved to Seville - after black players were abused in that fixture 22 years ago.

‌



The England boss was answering a question about whether he would remind his players about UEFA’s anti-racism protocols.

‌



Bit those comments did not please Spain boss Luis de la Fuente, who was asked at his press conference and snapped back: “Tell Tuchel there is no racism in Spain. It’s that blunt. Exactly the same as in England. We are not racist.”

Sports.content:

Ben White has been booed by England fans after being reintegrated into the squad by Thomas Tuchel and Declan Rice has now spoken out in defence of his Arsenal co-star

Declan Rice says if “people knew and understood” Ben White they would no longer boo him.

‌



‌



Arsenal defender White was jeered by the Wembley crowd when he came on as a substitute against Croatia and some England fans have not forgiven him for quitting the World Cup squad back in 2022.

‌



White spoke last week about his passion for playing in an England shirt but refused to go into detail about the reasons why he flew home from Qatar.

‌



And Rice says: “Ben has moved on from what's happened in the past, he's totally focused on playing for England. When he's been fit and available he's constantly put himself forward to play for England.

“If people knew and understood Ben White as a character he's not fazed by anything, he goes with the flow and he just wants to play football and for England.

“Fans are entitled to their opinion, it is what it is but he doesn't feel that way with England. He wants to come out and play his best football and enjoy himself. I think that's credit to him, coming on and playing for England and being booed is not easy but the way his character is it really helps him.

Rice has revealed he will embrace the competition from Bournemouth’s “incredible” Alex Scott as the midfielder took his place last month. ‌



Rice, 27, also says that he dreams of carrying on deep into his 30s with 33-year-old Harry Kane’s success only serving to prove that if you stay fit then anything is possible. “His mindset is always right. He’s always looking forward to the game. He’s always preparing himself in the right way. He’s always in a good way in his mind and I feel like for me … you need to be obsessed with football, still. Y

‌



“I want to play at the highest level for as long as possible. Doing that comes with sacrifices at that age, doing different things – recovery, preparing well, like I said.

“And being ready for whatever comes. Me at 33, I don’t know where I’m going to be and what I’m going to be doing but for sure I hope I’m still at the top level, competing and playing really well.”

"Manchester United is a huge club but I'd coached at big clubs where the fans made amazing atmospheres: Roma, Marseille, Lyon, Napoli. That brings pressure and can be complicated but it's also wonderful when you win.

‌



"I'm Mediterranean from my origins and I have the hot blood. Even in Napoli - I was only there four months before I was sacked by the president, not because of results but because I wanted to make the decisions a coach should make - I enjoyed it."

Garcia had previously discussed the interview process with Le Figaro back in 2022, touching on the significance of speaking the language of any nation in which you wish to manage. He said: "In Manchester, the interviews went pretty well

‌



"I saw John Murtough and Darren Fletcher, I told them I had to work on my English and Darren, who is Scottish, had a cool joke telling me that I did not yet have the level with the Scottish accent to answer, but that it was very good.

View 2 Images Rudi Garcia is a seasoned manager (Image: MB Media, Getty Images)

‌



"I find it respectful to speak the language in the country where you work. At Marseille or Lyon, I waged war on my players to take French lessons. When you see [Carlo] Ancelotti speaking our language despite leaving PSG, it's classy."

It comes as Mauricio Pochettino is set to arrive as Michael Carrick's successor at the Theatre of Dreams next week. Carrick was shown the door on Thursday after a poor start to the Premier League which has left United languishing in 18th.

Pochettino, meanwhile, will leave the United States national team to once again take the reins of a Premier League outfit, having enjoyed past stints with Chelsea, Tottenham Hotspur and Southampton.

Sports.title: Man Utd news LIVE: Pochettino transfer targets, Fernandes future, wonderkid signs
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino will soon be getting to work at Manchester United

All the latest Manchester United updates after Mauricio Pochettino was announced as Michael Carrick's successor at Old Trafford

Good afternoon and welcome to our Manchester United live blog. A new era is set to be ushered in at Old Trafford after Mauricio Pochettino was confirmed as Michael Carrick's replacement.

The former Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea boss has signed a two-and-a-half-year contract with the Red Devils, leaving his post at the United States' men's team at the end of the international break.

He faces an almighty task to turn around the club's fortunes. They sit 18th in the Premier League after 10 games played, next heading to Anfield for a daunting opening fixture for Pochettino.

After a lacklustre summer transfer window, United fans will be hopeful they correct some of their errors come January. And reported targets are already emerging on that front.

Nico Paz is among the big names linked after the Como star impressed against United in the Champions League. However, there are also question marks about the future of captain Bruno Fernandes after he reportedly rejected a second contract offer.

Pochettino's transfer priorities have already begun to emerge and it looks as though things will happen sooner rather than later with defensive reinforcements eyed up. United have already made one addition for the future in the form of England youth international Tyler Adjei but the January window could bring players capable of making an immediate impact.

Stay tuned to our live blog for all the latest updates.

Sports.title: BBC legend slams 'discipline' after broadcast axe and admits he tunes into rival
Sports.content:
BBC legend slams 'discipline' after broadcast axe and admits he tunes into rival

A BBC icon has explained that he listens to a rival of the broadcaster as a result of the "comprehensive service" it provides

View 2 Images The BBC cut 5 Live's classified results section in 2022 (Image: Leila Coker - WSL, WSL Football via Getty Images)

Mike Ingham has argued that BBC Radio 5 Live has surrendered much of its "discipline" following the controversial choice to scrap its classified football results segment back in 2022. The broadcasting legend has also revealed that he now listens to talkSPORT, which he considers a "comprehensive service."

‌



‌



The 76-year-old formed a partnership with Alan Green for nearly a quarter of a century between 1990 and 2014, commentating on the most significant matches in Britain and across the globe. Ingham and Green provided coverage of FA Cup finals, World Cup tournaments and European competitions, with the former renowned for his articulate style and presentation.

‌



In 2004, Ingham was promoted to the position of 5 Live's chief football correspondent. He stepped away from his position following the 2014 World Cup, bringing an illustrious career to a close, though he has remained an avid listener of the output from his former colleagues and those who followed.

‌



Jesus Owono given maximum ban for tackle that resulted in Jesus de Miguel's tragic death READ MORE :

Marcus Rashford causes issue as Man Utd set to trigger his team-mate's contract clause READ MORE :

Yet the iconic commentator doesn't always support the decisions taken by the BBC, as shown by his disapproval of 5 Live axing their classified segment four years ago. Discussing the decision, Ingham told the Telegraph: "It's like building a house without the bricks.

"Those two-and-a-half minutes were like taking stock at the end of a hurly-burly afternoon. It was a great bit of broadcasting when it was done by James Alexander Gordon, like the shipping forecast.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



"I think 5 Live has lost a lot of, not professionalism, but discipline. I was reared on hitting the pips. My family gets so exasperated with me now because I'm such a stickler for time. A lot of that has been lost, it has become much more easy come, easy go."

He added: "I just think the BBC has spread itself too thinly. It's just trying to do everything, as opposed to trying to concentrate on the things it does best.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"For me, the programme should always come before the podcast. That's me though, not being able to move with the times."

‌



A BBC statement issued when they chose to axe 5 Live's results segment said: "We appreciate the strength of feeling towards the classified football results within Sports Report. It's always difficult when a programme with a special history changes, but there are good reasons for the change.

"With the addition of the 5.30pm live Premier League match to our coverage, Sports Report has been condensed into a shorter programme - cut from 1 hour to 25 minutes. The classifieds were taking around 5-7 minutes to read, which would have taken up around a third of the programme - constraining the range of sport we could cover.

‌



View 2 Images Mike Ingham (left) has spoken about the BBC (Image: Getty)

"We'd like to assure our listeners that results from across the football leagues will still be shared during the programme and through the afternoon. Results are also available in full on the BBC Sport website and during Final Score on BBC One. Having a live match at 5.30 is a great addition to the 5 Live schedule."

‌



Ingham has also made the striking admission that he now tunes into BBC Sport's long-standing rival talkSPORT, owing to the network's capacity to deliver a "comprehensive service" to its audience. He said: "I think they [BBC Sport] were complacent about talkSPORT.

"When it began it was a bit blokey, now I think it's a more comprehensive service and the range of presenters they have really makes it work. Simon Jordan is brilliant, Jeff Stelling's there and they do the results at 5 o'clock on a Saturday."

Sports.content:
Luke Littler started his pursuit of a Grand Slam of Darts hat-trick with a commanding 5-2 victory against Beau Greaves in Wolverhampton on Saturday night.

In a Group A blockbuster, 'The Nuke' struck seven maximums and a 109.97 average to defeat the Women's Matchplay champion.

Littler has yet to taste defeat in 15 Grand Slam matches, as he bids to join Phil Taylor and Michael van Gerwen by becoming the third player to win three successive titles in the West Midlands.

Greaves had memorably beaten Littler in the semi-finals of last year's World Youth Championship, but the back-to-back world champion had revenge on his mind.

After looking invincible in the first half of 2026 as he won the first five majors, Littler had come up short at the World Series of Darts Finals, then slipped to a first-round exit at the Grand Prix before another last-eight defeat in the European Championship.

Littler, though, produced a vintage clinical display at WV Active Aldersley as he broke Greaves in the second leg before soon opening up a 3-0 lead in rapid time.

Greaves held to cut the deficit back to 4-2 before Littler swiftly wrapped things up by taking out tops with his first match dart.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Littler said that he is targeting a return to form ahead of the World Darts Championship after beating Greaves

Speaking to Sky Sports, Littler said: "I'm happy with the win. I needed to get off to a strong start because Beau started to find it at the end.

"I just had to finish how I started. I was very good at the scoring, but 29 per cent on the doubles needs to improve.

"Beau was fantastic, but I'm happy with myself and I'm still 100 per cent here in Wolverhampton."

The 19-year-old from Warrington is now aiming to find his Alexandra Palace form, adding: "I love it here. I remember my first year; last year was the same, and this year is the same.

"If I am performing like this, then I'm going to be happy.

"It's what I need. The last three or four majors haven't gone well, but I've been practising, and I'm glad I've shown it.

"It's perfect timing. I'm not going to Minehead for the Players Championship, this is the last major before the World Championship.

"After this, there are a few exhibitions, and hopefully it works out."

Littler vs Greaves: Tale of the Tape

John Part, speaking on Sky Sports, said: "His 180s and scoring were absolutely phenomenal. Beau didn't come out of the gates at her best, but you wouldn't say it was one of her better performances. We know she can play better than that.

"We're not sure Luke has been fully tested yet, but let's see."

Morris, who became just the sixth non-Tour Card holder to win a ranking title at Players Championship 34 earlier this month, said: "I was very nervous, but I take everything in my stride. I'm enjoying my progress. Even if I lose, I'm losing graciously."

Sports.title: Ireland overcome Fiji ahead of South Africa showdown
Sports.content:
Ireland beat Fiji 43-15 in Dublin in the Nations Championship.

The hosts had won all six previous Test matches between the sides but struggled for fluency and briefly trailed during an uncomfortable opening period at a subdued Aviva Stadium.

Robert Baloucoune scored twice in the first half for Andy Farrell's men after quick-fire tries from Fiji pair Josua Tuisova and Peceli Yato overhauled Tommy O'Brien's early opener.

Image: Ireland's Tommy O'Brien scores his sides fifth try during the Nations Championship match at the Aviva Stadium, Dublin.

Ronan Kelleher, Andrew Porter, O'Brien and Nick Timoney went over in the second half as Ireland eventually pulled clear to keep alive their hopes of reaching the Nations Championship final.

Ireland are now gearing up for a showdown with world champions South Africa next weekend.

The result over Fiji leaves Ireland level on 20 points with second-placed England in the northern hemisphere standings - a point below leaders France - ahead of next week's mouthwatering clash with the Springboks.

Ireland must now beat ​South Africa and hope France, who host Argentina, and England, who ​take on New Zealand, falter in Saturday's matches to secure a place in the final at Twickenham on ‌November 29.

Sports.title: Jones warns England: You were good vs Japan, but All Blacks will be 'violent'
Sports.content:
Former England head coach Eddie Jones praised his old side as "very good" as they tore his Japan apart 78-15 on Saturday, but warned the All Blacks will be "violent" against them next week.

Following South Africa's defeat to France in Paris on Friday, victory for New Zealand against Wales in Cardiff would have seen them claim World Rugby's No 1 ranking, and take charge of the Nations Championship southern hemisphere table.

Instead, the All Blacks suffered their first defeat to Wales since 1953 in a shock 35-28 loss up against an immense Welsh defensive effort, and next play England at Twickenham next Saturday.

"England were impressive against Australia, they beat them quite easily," Jones said at his post-match press conference.

England 78-15 Japan - Score summary England - Tries: Joseph (1,10,20,25,56), Steward (15), Genge (18), Murley (29), Earl (40), Martin (45), Curry (64), Smith (68), Fisilau (73). Cons: Ford (15,19,41), Slade (57,69). Pens: Ford (8). Japan - Tries: Dearns (37), Helu (48). Cons: Saito (38). Pens: Saito (14).

"They played powerfully, they played direct, and when they had the ability to shift the ball, they moved the ball accurately and quickly to space. We saw that again today.

"Well, they're [New Zealand] violent after a defeat.

"They're usually violent, very physical. They'll be massively disappointed with that performance [in Cardiff] today.

"New Zealand next week, they'll be back to the old New Zealand. They'll be hard and tough, and physical around the breakdown.

Image: Will Joseph scored five tries on his first England appearance since 2022 as the hosts destroyed Japan at Twickenham

"I thought England were very good. It kills me that Will Joseph - I gave him his first cap - scores five tries against me! That's not being very loyal, is it?

"He's a great kid, mate. He always was going to be a good player.

"I have to take full responsibility for our [Japan] performance. Clearly we weren't good enough today.

"We thought we had a good preparation for the game, but obviously it wasn't good. Without making any excuses, getting the red card early in the game put us on the back foot, and we really never recovered from that, which good teams are able to do.

"We're not good enough in being able to recover from disappointments. That's clearly the case."

Image: England got over for some 13 tries in victory over Japan, leaving 16 points behind in missed conversions

Borthwick: Joseph took his opportunities well - 'There's thinking to do around selection'

Joseph - who England head coach Steve Borthwick failed to select since taking the role in 2023 until Saturday - was the main topic during the home side's press conference.

While Borthwick wasn't effusive in his praise of the wing, he did admit he now had some extra thinking to do around selection ahead of facing the All Blacks.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Steve Borthwick and Eddie Jones were full of praise for Will Joseph after he scored a record-equalling five tries in England's thumping win over Japan in the Nations Championship

"He took those opportunities really, really well," Borthwick said.

"Talking about the point of difference he has in his carry - we wanted the ball in his hands as much as possible, and that's exactly what happened.

"It was off the back of all the players, everybody doing their jobs in the middle of the pitch, and that creates those opportunities on the edges.

"His pace, acceleration and footwork is a real asset. And part of today, as I said before the game, was that we want to build a squad, not a team.

Image: Steve Borthwick wasn't hugely effusive in his praise of Joseph, but admitted there is now thinking to do around team selection

"Now there's some people who really put their hand up with quality performances, and it means that competition for players, the depth in the squad, and the level of experience has taken another step forward.

"There's some thinking to do around selection ahead of next week, and I'm still waiting for the medical report, which hopefully all the players come through pretty well tonight.

"I'll get that full medical report, and then I'll make the call for selection when Test week starts tomorrow night."

What's next?

For England, they next face New Zealand in their third Nations Championship Test of the autumn at Allianz Stadium Twickenham on Saturday, November 21 (2.10pm kick-off).

Japan travel to face Scotland at Murrayfield in Edinburgh for their next Test, also on Saturday November 21 (2.10pm kick-off).
