While Zenith Bank and Access Holdings benefited significantly from lower credit losses, First HoldCo’s performance was substantially supported by trading and other non-interest income.

The banks’ statements on the nine-month results also highlighted different sources of earnings growth, with executives emphasising lower credit costs, diversified income and operating efficiency.

The Group Managing Director of Zenith Bank, Adaora Umeoji, said growth in lending, transaction volumes and deposits supported the bank’s performance, while “lower funding and credit costs contributed to profitability and improved earnings quality.”

Similarly, Access Holdings Group Chief Executive Officer Innocent Ike described the reduction in impairment charges and growth in income after impairment as evidence of the group’s stronger earnings base. He said the improvement “demonstrates the resilience of our core earnings base.”

First HoldCo recorded PBT of N911.24 billion, up 60.8 per cent, despite a 16 per cent decline in net interest income. Trading and fair-value income increased by about N190 billion, while higher fees and other operating income also supported profitability.

First HoldCo’s management highlighted the contribution of transaction-led revenues, with non-interest income growing by more than 143 per cent, helping to offset weaker net interest income.

Wema Bank’s net interest income increased by 38.3 per cent to N325.88 billion, supporting a 76.6 per cent rise in PBT to N258.64 billion.

Sterling Financial Holdings recorded a 43.9 per cent increase in net interest income to N205.90 billion, while PBT rose by 37.1 per cent to N97.28 billion. However, higher impairment charges and operating expenses absorbed part of the improvement.

Ecobank’s naira-denominated PBT declined marginally to N1.01 trillion as operating income weakened. GTCO’s PBT fell by 2.3 per cent as higher funding costs and operating expenses weighed on earnings.

Ecobank Group Chief Executive Officer Jeremy Awori identified deposit growth and operating efficiency as sources of resilience, while acknowledging risks from inflation, energy prices and foreign exchange volatility.

Jaiz Bank reported a 21.07 per cent increase in impairment charges to N1.28 billion, from N1.05 billion in the corresponding period of 2025. Its PBT rose by 1.7 per cent to N23.69 billion, from N23.29 billion.

World.title: NDC, Keyamo in War of Words over Singing of Old National Anthem at Lagos Meeting
World.content:
•Minister accuses Obi of planning secession

• Ex-Anambra gov didn’t stop new National Anthem, NDC fights back

. Accuses APC of sponsoring political attacks

Chinedu Eze in Lagos and Sunday Aborisade in Abuja

The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) and the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Mr. Festus Keyamo, yesterday engaged in war of words over the minister’s allegation that the presidential candidate of the opposition party, Mr. Peter Obi and the members of the party, sang the old National Anthem at the recent town hall meeting held by the party in Lagos.

Keyamo had in his verified Twitter (X) account said that by defying to sing the new national anthem, Obi and his group might be planning to break away from Nigeria.

But in a swift response, the NDC dismissed allegations against its presidential candidate, describing them as unfounded, baseless and politically-motivated.

The party accused Keyamo of exhibiting selective amnesia in his assessment of the Lagos incident, insisting that Obi neither instructed supporters not to sing the national anthem nor attempted to undermine the country’s national symbols.

In a response to the minister’s allegations, through its National Publicity Secretary Osa Director, the NDC maintained that the incident was a spontaneous expression of defiance by some supporters against what it described as the poor governance of the All Progressives Congress (APC) administration and the alleged deployment of political thugs to attack its members during the gathering.

The party argued that Keyamo deliberately ignored the circumstances surrounding the incident, particularly the reported attack on the NDC supporters, while attempting to portray Obi in a negative light.

It stated, “Keyamo’s allegations are hair-splitting, unfounded and baseless. As characteristic of the APC, he exhibited selective amnesia in his assessment.

“He forgot to state that Obi did not ask the crowd not to sing the national anthem. What happened was a spontaneous act of defiance to the ruinous reign of the APC and the hired thugs they sent to attack the NDC members,” the party added.

The opposition party further disclosed that while some supporters expressed their displeasure through the rendition of the old national anthem, other participants at the same venue continued to recite the current national anthem.

According to the party, the development contradicted any suggestion that Obi or the NDC leadership deliberately organised an action to disrespect the country’s national anthem.

It said, “At another end of the same hall, people recited the national anthem.”

The NDC also questioned the significance of the controversy, arguing that the mere public rendition of the national anthem by members of the ruling party had not translated into improved governance or better living conditions for Nigerians.

Taking a swipe at Keyamo and the APC, the party declared that displaying outward loyalty to national symbols should not be confused with the capacity to provide effective leadership.

“In any case, he should realise that the hood does not make the monk. Since the APC has been reciting the national anthem, where has it led Nigeria?” the party queried.

The opposition party accused the minister and the ruling party of deliberately shifting public attention from the alleged attack on its supporters and the country’s worsening political and economic challenges to what it described as unnecessary personality attacks against Obi.

It argued that the controversy reflected the APC’s inability to engage the opposition candidate on substantive issues of governance, national development and the welfare of Nigerians.

The NDC maintained that its presidential candidate remained committed to national unity, democratic values and peaceful political engagement, while accusing the APC of using the controversy to distract Nigerians from pressing national concerns.

Keyamo had described the act of singing the old national anthem as one of the ingredients of secession.

He insisted that by approving the singing of a different national anthem, Obi was allegedly officially leading a secessionist group.

“National Anthem is one of a country’s national symbols. It represents a country’s history, values and sovereignty. It is meant to unite citizens.

“When a group of people decide to defy it and sing something different from what others are signing as prescribed by law, that group is preparing grounds to break away from the country. It is one of the ingredients of secession. And once the leader of such a group endorses the action, it means the group is then officially a secessionist movement.

“I am therefore, officially calling on the original ‘countryman’, my classmate, my friend and a man of considerable courage from our school days, Senator Seriake Dickson, the official leader of the NDC, to within 48 hours speak up as to whether the NDC officially endorses a proscribed anthem as its own national symbol. The world is waiting,” he said.

World.title: Dangote Eyes Ghana Cocoa Hub, Opens Talks with Ghanaian Government on 500,000-tonne Deal
World.content:
Ejiofor Alike

The Chairman of Dangote Group, Alhaji Aliko Dangote is in talks with the Ghanaian government over a proposed cocoa-processing arrangement involving 500,000 metric tonnes, as the country seeks to retain more earnings from its agricultural produce by expanding domestic processing.

Ghana’s Finance Minister, Dr. Cassiel Ato Forson, disclosed the ongoing discussions in an interview at the weekend, after presenting the country’s 2027 Budget to Parliament.

The proposed arrangement, according to Nairametrics, would extend Dangote’s agricultural investments into cocoa processing and support Ghana’s ambition to move more of its cocoa value chain into the domestic economy.

Forson said negotiations were continuing, with the terms of the proposed contract undergoing review. He did not announce a signed agreement or disclose the investment value, processing location, implementation timetable or period covered by the proposed 500,000-tonne arrangement.

“Dangote has reached out to use Ghana as a hub to process cocoa locally,” the minister said.

“We are going through the terms, and they want to sign a contract.”

The discussions come as Ghana pursues an ambitious timetable to process 50 per cent of its locally produced cocoa by 2028 and 100 per cent by 2030.

Forson said the government wanted companies purchasing Ghanaian cocoa to establish processing operations within the country, allowing the economy to capture a greater share of the value generated beyond the export of raw beans.

The policy places domestic processing at the centre of Ghana’s efforts to strengthen its agricultural value chain, with the proposed Dangote arrangement offering a potential private-sector vehicle for advancing that objective.

According to the minister, Ghana’s position was to encourage investment in local value addition alongside purchasing its cocoa beans.

“We are not saying don’t come and buy our cocoa beans, but if you are a company out there, come and buy our cocoa beans, but add value here in Ghana,” he said.

Forson said a new Cocoa Board Act before Parliament would include a mandatory local-processing requirement. At the same time, a legislative instrument would set the timetable for increasing domestic processing to the government’s targets.

The proposed framework would give legislative backing to the processing drive. However, the minister’s comments indicated that the law and the commercial discussions with Dangote remained at different stages of consideration.

The cocoa initiative forms part of a wider agricultural modernisation programme through which Ghana hopes to expand domestic production and reduce expenditure on imported food.

Forson said the country spent approximately $3.5 billion annually importing food products, including palm oil, sugar, rice and poultry, despite possessing resources that could support increased local production.

“All we need to do is modernise agriculture,” he said.

He identified opportunities to increase maize and soybean production to supply the poultry industry, alongside expanding vegetable farming.

The minister’s comments linked the cocoa-processing ambition to a broader effort to build stronger connections between agriculture and industry. While increased farm output would improve raw-material supply, investment in processing would let the country retain more economic activity within its borders.

For the proposed cocoa arrangement, however, the next step remains concluding negotiations and clarifying the commercial terms.

The reported 500,000-tonne volume was not accompanied by details indicating whether it represented an annual commitment, a phased supply arrangement or the total quantity envisaged over the life of a contract.

Dangote’s interest in Ghana follows earlier agricultural and agro-industrial investment plans in Nigeria and elsewhere in Africa.

Beyond Nigeria, Dangote signed a $2.5 billion agreement with the Ethiopian government in August 2025 to establish a fertiliser plant.

World.title: Nigerian-American Professor John Dabiri Sits on NVIDIA Board Amid Jensen Huang’s Exit
World.content:
•Caltech professor joined technology giant’s board in 2020





Sunday Ehigiator



As global attention shifts to the leadership shake-up at American technology giant, NVIDIA, following the resignation of its Chief Executive Officer, Jensen Huang, a Nigerian-American professor, John Oluseun Dabiri, remains one of the notable figures on the company’s board of directors.



Dabiri, an engineer and professor at the California Institute of Technology (Caltech), joined NVIDIA’s board in 2020 and has served as an independent director during the company’s transformation into one of the world’s most valuable technology companies.

NVIDIA announced on November 12, 2026, that Huang had resigned as President, Chief Executive Officer and member of its board, effective immediately.



The company’s regulatory filing with the United States Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) disclosed that its board accepted Huang’s resignation on November 11, while Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, Colette Kress, was appointed interim Chief Executive Officer pending the appointment of a substantive successor.

The board also appointed Harvey C. Jones, who had served as a director since 1993, as its first-ever chairman.

Dabiri’s position on the board has brought renewed attention to his Nigerian heritage and an academic career marked by several major scientific recognitions in the United States.



Born in 1980 in Toledo, Ohio, to Nigerian immigrant parents, Dabiri built an impressive academic record that took him from Princeton University to Caltech, where he has become a leading figure in engineering and scientific research.

He graduated from Princeton University in 2001 with a Bachelor of Science in Engineering, summa cum laude, in mechanical and aerospace engineering.

He proceeded to Caltech, where he obtained a Master of Science degree in Aeronautics in 2003 and a PhD in Bioengineering in 2005, at the age of 25.



His academic career began at Caltech in 2005, where he became a professor of aeronautics and bioengineering. He later served at Stanford University from 2015 to 2019 before returning to Caltech, where he is currently the Centennial Professor of Aeronautics and Mechanical Engineering.



His research focuses on fluid mechanics, biological fluid dynamics, energy and environmental systems, with particular attention to how principles observed in nature can inform engineering solutions.

One of his major research interests is the movement of aquatic organisms, including jellyfish, and how their propulsion mechanisms can provide insights into fluid dynamics and energy-efficient technologies.

In 2010, at the age of 30, Dabiri received the prestigious MacArthur Fellowship, popularly known as the “Genius Grant”.

The fellowship recognises individuals with exceptional creativity and the potential to make significant contributions to their respective fields.



His other recognitions include the National Science Foundation’s Alan T. Waterman Award and the Presidential Early Career Award for Scientists and Engineers.

In 2020, NVIDIA appointed Dabiri to its board, citing his achievements in engineering and scientific research as valuable contributions to the company’s governance.



He currently serves on the board’s Compensation Committee and Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee.

His scientific contributions also earned him the United States National Medal of Science, one of the country’s highest honours for scientific achievement. He received the award at a White House ceremony in January 2025.

The medal recognises outstanding contributions to science and engineering, and Dabiri’s work has been associated with advances in biological fluid dynamics, energy and environmental research.



Beyond his university and corporate responsibilities, he served from 2021 to January 2025 on former United States President Joe Biden’s Council of Advisors on Science and Technology.

He has also served on the Energy Secretary’s Energy Advisory Board and remains involved in scientific research through the Dabiri Lab at Caltech.

World.title: ADC Crisis: Atiku Hasn’t Reached out to Me Despite Coming from My Geopolitical Zone, Says Gombe
World.content:
Chuks Okocha in Abuja

A factional leader of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Nafiu Bala Gombe, has expressed disappointment that former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has not personally reached out to him despite their coming from the same North-east geopolitical zone.

Gombe, who spoke in an interview with BBC Hausa yesterday, said he regarded Atiku as a father figure but was disappointed that the former vice-president had not contacted him amid the leadership crisis rocking the party.

He said this while reacting to a court judgment that affirmed his faction’s position in the ADC leadership dispute, adding that he remained willing to work with Atiku, former Senate President David Mark and other party chieftains to strengthen the opposition ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Gombe said the judgment had vindicated his faction as the authentic leadership of the party, insisting that its position was based on the provisions of the ADC constitution.

“Alhamdulillah. As we always say, truth is truth, while lies remain lies. Allah has vindicated us. The court has seen the merit of our case and our truthfulness and has decided to return the party leadership to us,” he said.

He disclosed that his faction was awaiting the Certified True Copy of the judgment to enable it to approach the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) for the necessary changes to the party’s leadership records.

Gombe, however, cautioned against interpreting the judgment as an opportunity to settle scores with members of the opposing faction, saying he was extending a hand of friendship to them.

“This is not a fight. Allah has given us victory, but we are not enemies. We are extending a hand of friendship to them to stop being arrogant and whatever they may say, so that we can strengthen the opposition and face the government,” he said.

He maintained that anyone seeking to join the ADC or contest an elective position on its platform must comply with the party’s constitution, particularly provisions governing membership registration, payment of dues and eligibility for leadership positions.

According to him, the party’s constitution requires members to fulfill prescribed conditions, including two years of membership and payment of stipulated dues, before qualifying for leadership positions.

He alleged that the opposing faction failed to follow the party’s membership registration procedures, claiming that David Mark obtained his membership card from a former national chairman in Abuja rather than registering at his ward.

Bala said he had repeatedly warned the opposing group about the consequences of disregarding the party’s constitution, but his advice was ignored.

He also dismissed allegations that he was being used by the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) to destabilise the opposition, insisting that his court action was solely aimed at protecting his rights and upholding the ADC constitution.

“I went to court with only the constitution. I told the world that if they had followed the right procedures, the court should rule in their favour. But if we were right, we should be given our rights,” he said.

Gombe dismissed allegations that he was working for the ruling APC to destabilise the opposition, insisting that his legal action against the party’s rival leadership was aimed solely at defending his rights and upholding the party’s constitution.

He also extended an olive branch to Atiku, former Senate President David Mark and other party chieftains following a court judgment that affirmed his faction’s position in the ADC leadership dispute.

Gombe said the judgment had vindicated his faction as the authentic leadership of the party, maintaining that its legal position was based on the provisions of the ADC constitution.

“Alhamdulillah. As we always say, truth is truth, while lies remain lies. Allah has vindicated us. The court has seen the merit of our case and our truthfulness and has decided to return the party leadership to us,” he said.

He disclosed that his faction was awaiting the CTC of the judgment before approaching the INEC to effect the necessary changes to the party’s leadership records.

Gombe, however, said the judgment should not be regarded as an opportunity to settle scores with the opposing faction, expressing his willingness to work with Atiku, Mark and other prominent politicians to strengthen the opposition ahead of the 2027 general elections.

“This is not a fight. Allah has given us victory, but we are not enemies. We are extending a hand of friendship to them to stop being arrogant and whatever they may say, so that we can strengthen the opposition and face the government,” he said.

Addressing the allegations that he was being sponsored to weaken the opposition, Gombe insisted that he approached the court based on the party’s constitution and was prepared to accept any judgment delivered in accordance with the law.

“I went to court with only the constitution. I told the world that if they had followed the right procedures, the court should rule in their favour. But if we were right, we should be given our rights,” he said

On the continued appearance of Atiku’s and David Mark’s names on INEC’s portal, Gombe said the commission would act appropriately once it received the Certified True Copy of the judgment.

He dismissed suggestions that INEC was deliberately delaying the implementation of the judgment, saying the commission might not have received the official court document.

Gombe also rejected arguments that the large crowds attracted by the ADC during political engagements in Sokoto and Kebbi states should have persuaded him to abandon the legal battle.

He argued that political popularity and financial influence should not be used to justify disregard for the law, warning that the country could not make progress if influential politicians continued to violate established rules.

The factional leader further claimed that some individuals involved in the dispute had circulated documents suggesting that he had resigned from his position, describing the claims as misleading.

On the party’s preparations for the 2027 elections, Gombe said his faction had directed all aspirants seeking elective positions on the ADC platform to continue their campaign activities.

He urged members of the opposing faction to remain patient, follow the party’s constitutional procedures and complete their membership registration at their respective wards.

On funding, he said his faction relied largely on membership dues and other contributions generated through the party’s internal activities.

Gombe also defended his security arrangements and lifestyle, saying he was entitled to protection like other prominent political figures. He added that he was a businessman with other sources of livelihood.

World.title: What time is kick off for Springboks against Ireland?
World.content:
There is still everything to play for in the Nations Championship as the Springboks look to put a disappointing defeat against France behind them, and quickly turn attention to facing Ireland this Saturday (18:40 kick off).

The Springboks’ loss to Les Bleus was somewhat offset by the shock loss the All Blacks suffered to Wales on Saturday, but New Zealand still hold a one-point advantage over South Africa on the southern hemisphere table of the Nations Championship.

It means South Africa will need to target a bonus-point win when they kick off against Ireland this Saturday, while the All Blacks next face England.



Kick off for the Springboks against Ireland is at 18:40 (SA time)

The Springboks will make the journey from France to Ireland on Saturday for their third Nations Championship match in Dublin.



South Africa won 24-13 on their last visit to Dublin a year ago, but there is always an extra intensity whenever the Springboks face up against Ireland.

“We know a massive challenge awaits us next week in Ireland,” lock Ruan Nortjé said after the France defeat. “We know it’s a rivalry that’s been building up the last few years.

“It’s always a massive game there. I think we have our work cut out for ourselves.

“We’re going to have to put massive focus on ourselves this week. Make sure we fix a lot of areas of our game.”

Focused on improvements

Meanwhile, Siya Kolisi insisted the Springboks would know exactly what was needed in terms of improvements this week after slipping up against France.

“Early in the first half (against France) we created opportunities in the wide channels that we didn’t take, and when they created chances, they took them straight away. So, we could have been better in many areas.



“However, the effort and hard work was there from our team, and they fought till the end. But if you create so many opportunities and don’t take them against a team like this, you’re not going to get the win. We know what we need to fix, and hopefully we will play better next week.”

World.title: How Zimbabwe’s new e-hailing rules could hit drivers’ pockets
World.content:
Zimbabwean Bolt and inDrive drivers face new fees under proposed rules. Image: inDrive

Drivers working for Bolt, inDrive and other ride-hailing platforms in Zimbabwe could face additional expenses if the government’s proposed regulations become law, with new permits, certificates, vehicle licensing and tax compliance among the requirements.

Zimbabwe’s Ministry of Transport and Infrastructural Development published the draft Road Motor Transportation (E-hailing Services) Regulations on 11 November 2026, inviting public and industry feedback before their proposed finalisation by 31 December.

New permits and certificates could add to costs

Under the proposals, drivers would need a special e-hailing permit, a valid driving licence held for at least five years, a defensive driving certificate and a medical fitness certificate.



However, the draft does not specify how much drivers would pay for the e-hailing permit.

Its proposed fee schedule leaves the application and renewal charges blank, meaning motorists cannot yet calculate the full cost of obtaining authorisation.

Drivers may also need to budget for defensive driving training and medical assessments.

The Traffic Safety Council of Zimbabwe (TSCZ) provides defensive driving courses, although its current applicable fee should be confirmed directly with the organisation.

e-hailing in zim: Vehicle owners face additional charges

The proposed requirements could also increase expenses for people who own vehicles used for e-hailing.

Each vehicle would need an operator’s licence endorsed for e-hailing, a valid certificate of fitness, appropriate insurance and an identification disc displayed on the windscreen.



The draft proposes a US$20 (approximately R338.40) fee for endorsing an operator’s licence for each vehicle. However, the annual identification disc fee has not been specified.

Owners would also need to maintain valid tax clearance certificates and meet the applicable vehicle licensing and insurance requirements.

Existing US$35 taxi tax adds to the calculation

There is also an existing tax obligation that e-hailing vehicle operators should consider.

According to the Zimbabwe Revenue Authority’s (ZIMRA) Public Notice 51 of 2025, operators of taxicabs carrying no more than seven passengers are liable for presumptive tax of US$35 (approximately R592.20) per vehicle monthly.

The proposed regulations require e-hailing vehicle operators to maintain tax compliance, meaning this existing obligation could form part of their operating expenses.

Additionally, the draft proposes a ZINARA road-user charge for every completed e-hailing trip. However, the amount has not yet been determined.

How much will e-hailing drivers eventually pay?

Although the draft identifies some charges, it does not provide enough information to calculate the total compliance cost.

The e-hailing permit, identification disc and per-trip road-user charge remain unpriced in the proposed schedules.

Drivers will therefore have to wait for the final regulations before determining the full financial implications.

The government is still inviting submissions, meaning the proposed fees and requirements could change before implementation.

World.title: South Africa’s U23s edge closer to Olympic dream
World.content:
Raymond Mdaka’s U23s had to play a very patient game. A late goal decided the result after failing to convert several promising opportunities during an entertaining encounter.

South Africa delivered attacking purpose from the opening stages. Sekhukhune United striker Thabang Mahlangu was gifted with the opportunity to put his team ahead just nine minutes into the contest but failed to punish the visitors.

U23 COACH RAYMOND MDAKA MAKES THREE CHANGES

Soon after Mahlangu’s miss was another wasted opportunity. This time it was Mamelodi Sundowns‘ Letlhaku missing the target.



He found himself in a promising position after Shandre Campbell delivered an inviting ball towards the far post. Unfortunately, he could not find the finish required to reward the move.

Madagascar gradually grew into the contest and began testing the South African defensive structure.

Their attacking threat increased after the restart, with Patricio particularly influential in forward areas. His movements and third-man runs caused problems for Mdaka’s defence.



South Africa needed a response, and Mdaka turned to his bench during the second half.

The coach introduced Thato Sibiya, Nhlanhla Gasa and Quwan Plaatjies in a triple substitution as he attempted to change the direction of the contest.

The changes brought renewed energy to the visitors’ attacking play.



Plaatjies immediately made his presence felt, rising to meet a dangerous delivery inside the penalty area. His header looked destined for the net before Madagascar produced an excellent goal-line clearance.

However, South Africa continued pushing for an opener rather than settling for a draw.

Mahlangu had also threatened earlier in the match when he cut inside from the near side before sending an effort narrowly wide.



QUWAN PLAATJIES SETTLES THE CONTEST

The breakthrough finally arrived during the closing ten minutes, with captain Neo Rapoo providing the decisive delivery.

Rapoo produced an accurate corner-kick that found Plaatjies inside the area. The substitute made no mistake with his header, sending the ball into the top of the net to give South Africa the advantage.

The goal rewarded Mdaka’s decision to introduce fresh attacking options and gave the visitors an important result heading into the return fixture.



Plaatjies nearly doubled his contribution two minutes before the final whistle when he attempted a first-time effort from the far side of the penalty area.

Madagascar managed to keep the scoreline at 1-0, but South Africa had done enough to secure victory. Mdaka’s side will now look to complete the job in the second leg on Tuesday.

The narrow advantage leaves South Africa with work still to do, but they will take confidence from their ability to find a breakthrough after struggling to convert earlier opportunities.



The return encounter will determine whether the young South African side can progress in the CAF U23 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign.

World.title: Tito Maswanganyi makes interesting admission about showboating
World.content:
Former Orlando Pirates midfielder Patrick ‘Tito’ Maswanganyi has opened up about showboating, explaining why he no longer regularly showcases his skills since playing outside South Africa.

Showboating has been a hot topic in South African football, with divided opinions over whether players should be encouraged to express themselves through skills and tricks.

While some believe showboating serves little purpose if it does not beat an opponent or create a goalscoring opportunity, others argue that it is part of South African football’s DNA and should be encouraged because of the entertainment it brings to supporters.



Speaking to the South African Football Journalists Association (SAFJA), Maswanganyi revealed that although his coach encourages him to use his skills, he personally does not feel the same urge to showboat since leaving South Africa.

“Yeah, well, my coach wants me to do them [skills],” said Tito.

“But in terms of myself, I don’t feel like doing them because I’m not in South Africa. But being in South Africa, I felt like it’s our culture, you know. I grew up in Tembisa watching games and that’s how they played.

“And also, people who have been watching the old people, they’ve been telling us that those people were playing great football. But when I watch their videos, they were doing showboating, you understand?”

Maswanganyi was a fan favourite during his time at Orlando Pirates, where he became known for his flair, creativity and impressive technical ability.

His comments highlight the cultural significance of showboating in South African football and the different attitudes towards individual expression depending on where players are competing.



Last month, Tito was seen at the Orlando Amstel Arena with his former Pirates teammates during the team’s 1-0 win over Sekhukhune United.

What’s your take on showboating?

World.title: WATCH | DA in coalition talks with Jacob Zuma’s MK Party
World.content:
The DA and MK Party met in Midrand on Saturday to discuss potential coalitions in hung municipalities. Images: X

The Democratic Alliance (DA) has entered coalition talks with former president Jacob Zuma’s uMkhonto weSizwe (MK) Party, despite its previous opposition to working with the party.

The two parties met in Midrand, Johannesburg, on Saturday, 14 November, following the local government elections, which left more than 130 councils without an outright majority.

The meeting followed an approach by DA leader Geordin Hill-Lewis to Zuma earlier this week.



DA REACHES OUT TO MK PARTY

MK Party national coalition negotiator advocate Dali Mpofu confirmed that Hill-Lewis had written to Zuma requesting a meeting.

“I can confirm that the DA has reached out. Their leader, Geordin Hill-Lewis, wrote a letter to President Zuma inviting discussions on coalitions,” Mpofu reportedly said.

Mpofu led the MK Party’s negotiations with the DA on Saturday.

The meeting marks a shift in the DA’s longstanding position on working with the MK Party and the Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF).

Neither the DA nor the MK Party has publicly announced a coalition agreement.

DA SETS CONDITIONS FOR COALITIONS

Following the 4 November elections, the DA’s Federal Executive resolved to engage political parties in municipalities where no party secured an outright majority.



DA Federal Council chairperson Ashor Sarupen said negotiations would centre on accountable governance, tackling corruption, service delivery, non-racialism and respect for the rule of law.

The DA secured the largest share of votes in Gauteng’s three metropolitan municipalities but fell short of the majority needed to govern independently.

MK PARTY ALSO MEETS ANC

Meanwhile, MK Party deputy president Duduzane Zuma held separate coalition talks with the African National Congress (ANC) on Saturday.

Speaking to SABC News, Zuma said political differences should not prevent parties from finding common ground.

WATCH | MK Party first deputy president Duduzane Zuma says the party is willing to work with any political formation. He was speaking after coalition talks with the DA in Waterfall, Johannesburg, today. pic.twitter.com/BCMT6RUUAJ — SABC News (@SABCNews) November 14, 2026

“We need to build bridges. Even though we may not agree, conversations are conversations,” he said.

The MK Party, which enjoys significant support in KwaZulu-Natal, also held coalition talks with Julius Malema’s EFF on Wednesday.

World.title: EFF leads parties in women’s representation among councillors
World.content:
The Electoral Commission of South Africa (IEC) has revealed that the Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF) recorded the highest women’s representation among political parties with a substantial number of councillors, at 46.2%, following the 2026 local government elections.

This was revealed on Friday, 13 November, during an IEC briefing on the processes to conclude the 2026 elections cycle.

EFF LEADS IN WOMEN’S REPRESENTATION

During the briefing, IEC chairperson Mosotho Moepya revealed that women account for 33.6% of all declared councillors.



Women make up 39.7% of proportional representation (PR) councillors, compared to 26.8% of ward councillors, highlighting that PR lists remain the main route through which women enter municipal councils.

Moepya said that among parties with a substantial number of councillors, the EFF recorded the highest women’s representation at 46.2%, followed by the Patriotic Alliance (PA) at 43% and the Democratic Alliance (DA) at 38.6%. The Inkatha Freedom Party (IFP) recorded the lowest representation at 18.7%.

LGE 2026 | IEC Chairperson Mosotho Moepya says the EFF has recorded the highest proportion of women candidates, at 46.2%, for the 2026 Local Government Elections. pic.twitter.com/YPBBkCahXs — SABC News (@SABCNews) November 13, 2026

AGE REPRESENTATION AMONG COUNCILLORS

The IEC also provided a breakdown of the age demographics of declared councillors, with the average age standing at 47.3 years and the median age at 47.

The largest proportion of councillors falls within the 40–49 age group at 34.9%, followed by those aged 50–59 at 26.2% and 30–39 at 21.8%.

Only 3% of councillors are under 30, while 2.1% are aged 70 or older. Those under the age of 35 account for 10.8% of all declared councillors.



Women are slightly older than men on average, with an average age of 48.2 years compared to 46.9 years for men.

“Among the larger parties, the Economic Freedom Fighters have the youngest councillors on average at 42.5 years, the youngest being 19 years old. The oldest councillor is 86 years old, from the Inkatha Freedom Party in uMlalazi, KwaZulu-Natal,” Moepya said.

World.title: RIP | Award-winning SA journalist Nabeelah Shaikh dies
World.content:
South Africa’s media fraternity is mourning the death of award-winning investigative journalist Nabeelah Shaikh. Image: Facebook/Nabeelah Shaikh

Award-winning South African journalist Nabeelah Shaikh has died at the age of 34.

The Central Islamic Trust announced her death in a funeral notice on Saturday, 14 November.

Shaikh, an investigative reporter for eNCA, was seven months pregnant with her second child.



The cause of her death remains unknown.

NABEELAH SHAIKH’S JOURNALISM CAREER

Originally from Tongaat in KwaZulu-Natal, Shaikh began her journalism career at the Sunday Tribune in 2013.

The Durban University of Technology graduate also worked for e.tv, Seen.tv and Hashtag Our Stories before joining eNCA.

She received several accolades for her reporting, including recognition at the Vodacom Journalist of the Year Awards.

Her recent assignments included the killings of women in Ekurhuleni and the 2026 local government elections.

COLLEAGUES PAY TRIBUTE

News of Shaikh’s death sent shockwaves through the media fraternity on Saturday.



IOL CEO Viasen Soobramoney described her as “a fearless journalist that was committed to her craft”.

Her former journalism lecturer, Robin Sewlal, also expressed his sadness at her passing.

“Shocked and stunned. Gone far too young,” he wrote.

Shaikh leaves behind her husband, Waseem Ally, daughter Maahira, parents and brothers.

World.title: eNCA colleagues mourn Shaikh, a fearless journalist and kind soul
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - “I never imagined that my first big task as investigations editor would be to speak about Nabeelah in this way.”

Those were the words of eNCA Investigations Editor Dasen Thathiah as he reflected on the death of investigative reporter Nabeelah Shaikh at just 34.

Thathiah described this moment as one of his most difficult assignments to undertake.

Thathiah said he had hoped that his first task with the newly formed team would be to celebrate an award a massive achievement that the team would have made, but instead he mourns a colleague whose new path in journalism was just about to begin.

Despite being part of the team for a short time, Shaikh had already hit the ground running as a true journalist; producing two stories for the eNCA investigative team already.

“I've been at eNCA a long time, and this probably ranks as my most difficult assignment, having to speak about this,” Thathiah said.

Beyond the newsroom and on the field, it was Shaikh’s kindness, thoughtfulness, and caring nature that were impossible to miss.

World.title: 'I will not be bullied into making political decisions' - Mashaba
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - ActionSA leader Herman Mashaba is putting his foot down and setting the record straight.

He says absolutely no one will dictate ActionSA’s coalition choices.

In a scathing opinion piece, he tells political commentators to stop undermining his leadership.

"There comes a time when political disagreement must be separated from outright disrespect. I have reached a point where I will no longer remain silent while people attempt to bully, undermine and dictate to me and the political organisation I lead," Mashaba wrote in his opinion piece.

READ | PA backs ActionSA in Laingsburg coalition deal

His remarks follow persistent doubts about ActionSA’s independence, with critics painting the party as a DA offshoot.

Mashaba quit the Democratic Alliance in October 2019.

Yet, the DA’s shadow follows him.

"Let me make this absolutely clear: ActionSA is an independent political party. We are not an extension of the DA, the ANC, the EFF or any other political organisation. We are not a political project that requires permission from other parties to make decisions.

"We have our own leadership, our own principles, our own supporters and, most importantly, a responsibility to the millions of South Africans who have placed their trust in us," Mashaba said.

World.title: Discontinuation claims about popular drink turn out to be a prank
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - South Africans were briefly left wondering whether a popular party favourite was about to disappear from shelves.

This comes after a statement claiming that Jägermeister would be discontinued began circulating online.

The statement, dated 9 November, claimed that the decision followed an internal review of South African market operations, with 31 January 2027 set as the final date.

But there was a catch.

World.title: From heatwave to thunderstorm: Heavy downpours expected in these areas
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The South African Weather Service has issued a warning for severe thunderstorms and heavy downpours across parts of the country this weekend.

The warning, valid from this afternoon, is expected over Free State, North West, Gauteng, Mpumalanga, KwaZulu-Natal, and Limpopo.

For the Western Cape, a Yellow Level 1 warning of damaging winds for Saturday has been issued.

It comes after a week of heatwaves in various areas.

READ | Joburg residents urged to take precautions as heatwave continues

The City’s Emergency Management Services has urged residents, particularly those in low-lying areas, to avoid crossing flooded roads, rivers and streams.

Emergency Services spokesperson Robert Mulaudzi extended the same caution to motorists.

“We are pleading with our residents, especially those in our low-lying areas, to avoid crossing rivers and streams while conducting their daily activities. “We encourage our motorists to exercise caution while driving, extend a safe following distance and try to avoid crossing flooded roads and low-lying bridges.”

Mulaudzi said emergency service authorities will remain on high alert, monitoring all seven regions of the city for any emergencies which might occur.

World.title: No major incidents reported as matric exams near end
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The Department of Basic Education is gearing up for the marking phase as the 2026 National Senior Certificate examinations near their end.

To date, the department's spokesperson, Terence Khala, said they have noted a few minor incidents reported, but none are serious enough to affect the integrity of the examinations.

READ | Senior teachers opt for early retirement as government trims wage bill

This is as he points to taxi violence in the Western Cape and scholar transport challenges in Gauteng as some of the issues experienced during the examination period.

But upon being notified of this, the department acted.

“The sector kicked in and was able to make sure that the requisite protocols were put in place. Learners in Gauteng were able to write adequately and equally in the Western Cape. “And I think it's only for us to commend the system and commend every individual that forms part of the system that assists us to make sure that we can really take this massive undertaking and make it a seamless one,” Khala said.

Markers, according to the department, will get to work on 1 December.

World.title: Six people killed in head-on collision on Eastern Cape N2
World.content:
At least six people have died in a horror crash on the N2 in the Eastern Cape.

The victims were travelling in a minibus taxi when it collided head-on with a truck on Saturday morning.

Provincial transport spokesperson Unathi Binqose said the minibus taxi was travelling from Alice towards Bizana while the truck was travelling from Kokstad towards Mzamba when the accident happened.

"Preliminary information suggests that the Toyota Quantum crossed into the path of the oncoming truck, resulting in a head-on collision. "There is also a suspicion that driver fatigue may have contributed to the crash. However, the exact circumstances surrounding the collision remain subject to police investigation," he said.

Three others were seriously injured, while three others sustained slight injuries.

"The injured were attended to by emergency services and transported for medical treatment".

The victims are believed to be university students travelling home to Bizana.

This comes just a day after seven people died in another crash on the N2 near Ndabakazi.

World.title: Madlanga Commission hears ex-JMPD top cop allegedly forced officers to take bribe
World.content:
PRETORIA - A major drug bust operation in Johannesburg has led to explosive testimony at the Madlanga Commission of Inquiry.

The commission heard on Friday how former JMPD superintendent Phineas Manyama allegedly instructed officers to release suspects and accept whatever money was offered in return.

READ | LIVE | JMPD corruption under the spotlight at Madlanga

Testifying at the commission Tactical Response Unit officer Michael Potsane said refusing the instruction came with threats of dismissal, arrest or even death.

He testified that he regarded the instruction as unlawful and did not comply with it.

World.title: Hot weather, dry taps, fuming Joburg residents
World.content:
SOWETO - Water shortages are worsening across various parts of Johannesburg, with residents reporting days without water supply amid the heatwave.

In Soweto, one resident detailed how the community has been without water since Tuesday, with supply returning briefly during the early hours of the morning.

“We've been having challenges with water in this community whereby each and every weekend we don't have water at all. It is becoming a new normal now,” the resident said.

The resident adds that the situation becomes more concerning during the current heatwave when residents need water the most.

“We are encouraged to drink more water because people are going to suffer because of dehydration, but at this particular moment, Joburg Water is not doing justice to us."

He said adding to the frustration is the lack of communication between Joburg Water and residents.

READ | Joburg residents urged to take precautions as heatwave continues

In a statement on Saturday, Joburg Water said bulk supply meters in the Roodepoort and Soweto regions, which were closed on Thursday to rescue and boost bulk supply levels, commenced reopening on Friday afternoon.

The water utility said it is worth noting that systems were not fully opened but taken back to their original curtailment before being fully closed on Thursday.

“While some bulk supplier systems have stabilised and recovered, there are still several systems which will take time to recover over the next few days. The recovery is also impacted by the demand for the system as they are integrated. “The affected Johannesburg Water reservoirs will first need to fill to acceptable levels before the system stabilises. Customers may experience low pressure or intermittent supply and, in some cases, no water until the system recovers,” the statement read.

In the meantime, Joburg Water said alternative water arrangements are being made and deployed through the central and regional coordination groups.

World.title: Raila Odinga's mourning that never was: Who hijacked his anniversary?
World.content:
A statesman does not become private property upon his death. But in Kenya, the grave has always been a contested ground. [PCS]

Thirty-two years separate the burial of Jaramogi Oginga Odinga from the first anniversary of his son’s death. And those who stood with the son, Raila Amolo Odinga, see the same method at work in both.

A statesman does not become private property upon his death. But in Kenya, the grave has always been a contested ground.

World.title: Love under watch: How technology is fuelling intimate partner abuse
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Your enemy is closer than you think. For many Kenyan women, the person who demands a phone password, reads private messages and tracks their movements through a screen is not a faceless troll. He is the man they live with, or the one they used to.

That is the uncomfortable picture painted by the recently released 2025–2626 Kenya Mini Demographic and Health Survey (KMDHS), which measured technology-facilitated gender-based violence, abuse committed, assisted, aggravated or amplified through digital tools.

The most common form of abuse is online control, reported by 19 per cent of women, followed by hacking at 5 per cent and online sexual harassment or cyber sexual abuse at 3 per cent. Most of it happens on platforms women use every day.

“Sixty-seven per cent of women who experienced digital gender violence say it happened on social media, with Facebook cited by 59 per cent. Messaging apps follow at 47 per cent, with WhatsApp at 26 per cent. Among girls aged 15–19, 77 per cent reported abuse on social media.”

The report shows how widespread the abuse is. “Twenty-six percent of women age 15–49 have ever experienced technology-facilitated violence from any perpetrator,” the report says, and 21 per cent experienced it often or sometimes in the 12 months before the survey. Among women who have ever had a husband or intimate partner, 27 per cent have experienced it at the hands of a current, most recent or previous partner.

The burden is not spread evenly, the report states that Nairobi City records the highest lifetime experience from any perpetrator at 33 per cent, followed by Murang’a and Baringo at 32 per cent each.

“For abuse by an intimate partner, Homa Bay 36 per cent and Baringo 35 per cent lead, while in the 12 months before the survey Trans Nzoia topped the list at 31 per cent. At the other end, Mandera and Wajir report just 3 per cent, a figure that may say as much about silence as about safety,” the report says

The picture is similar among young people. A 2024 rapid study by the Collaborative Centre for Gender and Development, working with the UNFPA and Women Economic Empowerment, found that nearly 90 per cent of young adults enrolled in three Nairobi tertiary institutions had witnessed TFGBV, and 39 per cent had experienced it personally.

Among women who have ever had a husband or intimate partner, 27 per cent have experienced gender violence committed by a current, most recent or previous partner, and 22 per cent did so in the past year. When women were asked who was responsible, the answer was blunt. Current husbands or intimate partners accounted for 61 per cent of perpetrators, former partners for 22 per cent and strangers for just 13 per cent.

Women who have never been married or had a partner face a different threat. For them, the most common perpetrators are strangers at 45 per cent, online attackers at 23 per cent and friends or acquaintances at 20 per cent.

Warning signs

Control is the common thread. The report describes such behaviours by a male partner as “important early warning signs that may escalate into violence within a relationship.”

Sixty-one per cent of ever-partnered women say their current or most recent partner has shown at least one controlling behaviour, and 27 per cent report three or more. Half say he has been jealous or angry when they spoke to other men, and 36 per cent say he insists on knowing where they are at all times. Others describe partners who demand passwords or read messages without consent.

Age and marital status matter. Technology-based gender violence is lowest among girls aged 15–19 at 10 per cent and highest among women aged 20–24 at 37 per cent. Forty-one per cent of divorced, separated or widowed women have experienced it, compared with 27 per cent of married women and 19 per cent of the never married.

Yet the digital rights advocate Cherie Oyier, a programmes officer at the Kenya ICT Action Network (KICTANet), says the low figures in some places should not be read as safety. Much of the abuse happens where nobody can see it.

“Closed applications, meaning like WhatsApp, those are the ones that most people, intimate partners will usually use,” she says. “Even as you are scrolling the internet to look for these instances, we may not be able to catch it. But it does not mean that it is not happening or that it is at a lower level.”

Culture also silences women. “Most women are told just endure, this is what marriage is about,” Oyier says. “Sometimes they don’t know, it’s so overt, like it doesn’t come out clearly that this is abuse. So most of the times, it is not reported.”

Online, abuse has been turned into entertainment. “It has become banter,” she says. “Even the people who are experiencing it have trivialised it. It’s now ingrained to you, like this is something that happens, you should expect it actually. If you post a picture, one of the things that you are thinking about is what kind of comments am I going to get.”

A 2023 report by KICTANet found that more than 30 per cent of Kenyans have experienced some form of TFGBV, while 90 per cent have witnessed it. In 2025, KICTANet and Equality Now released survivor testimonies showing how deceptive online job offers, grooming and image-based abuse leave women exposed, and how many had never received counselling despite years of trauma.

The stakes are not only digital. The 2025 Report of the Technical Working Group on GBV Including Femicide, cited in the KMDHS, indicated that many cases of homicide of women and girls, and of sexual and physical harm directed towards them, “are preceded by online and offline harassment using digital tools.”

For survivors, the law offers little comfort. “The technology is moving at a very fast pace compared to the laws,” Oyier says. In an attempt to bolster the gaps, Kenya has many fragmented laws. “You’ll have the Data Protection Act, the Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act, the Children’s Act, that to some extent touch on online issues, but they don’t really cohesively cover the different instances of TFGBV.”

The police, she says, often do not know either. “Just imagine you’re a woman who is in a village, for example, a village in Siaya, and you encounter violence. For you to even understand which law apply is very stressful.”

“You’re going through psychological stress and depression, and you’re also supposed to figure out which law applies in your situation. It causes even more problems for victims and survivors.”

Flagging abusive language

Artificial intelligence is adding a new layer. Even so, Oyier cautions against writing it off. “We should not vilify AI completely,” she says. KICTANet has built a lexicon to help flag abusive language and runs a tracker for online gender-based violence. “One person cannot sit down and look at everything on social media. When AI is able to pull every post that has this word, a human content moderator is able to look through it with local context and see is this TFGBV or not.”

The KMDHS findings further show that exposure to TFGBV varies across age groups and digital platforms.

“Younger women are particularly exposed on social media, with 77 per cent of women aged 15–19 and 72 per cent of those aged 20–24 who experienced TFGBV reporting abuse on social media platforms, compared with 50 per cent of women aged 40–49.”

However, messaging applications tell a different story. Women aged 40–49 reported the highest exposure through these platforms at 54 per cent, compared with 30 per cent among teenagers aged 15–19.

Wealth also influences where women encounter online abuse. Exposure on social media increases from 45 per cent among women in the lowest wealth quintile to 74 per cent among those in the highest. Conversely, women in the lowest wealth quintile report greater exposure through messaging applications, at 62 per cent, compared with 39 per cent among those in the highest wealth quintile.

These differences suggest that TFGBV cuts across age and economic backgrounds, although the platforms through which women experience it vary.

World.title: Not so fast: Court slams brake on ARA over wealth forfeiture
World.content:
Felix Mecha Nyakundi could not provide a plausible explanation for how he amassed his wealth.

The Court of Appeal has ruled that the government cannot go after a person’s wealth without prior investigations to establish reasonable grounds for suspecting that the property constitutes proceeds of crime.

In a landmark judgment, Justices Patrick Kiage, Jamila Mohammed and Nduma Nderi said that although it does not require a person to be charged for a crime for the Asset Recovery Agency (ARA) to come knocking, it bears the responsibility to link the wealth or cash to a crime.

World.title: Back to sender: Aisha Jumwa returns to UDA
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto welcome former Cabinet Secretary Aisha Jumwa back to the ruling United Democratic Alliance (UDA) on November 12, 2026. [PCS]

Former Cabinet Secretary Aisha Jumwa has returned to President William Ruto’s United Democratic Alliance (UDA), ending a three-month political fallout with the ruling party that saw her join opposition outfit Wiper Patriotic Front and declare support for the one-term movement ahead of the 2027 General Election.

President Ruto welcomed Jumwa back into UDA at State House, Mombasa, on Thursday, November 12, 2026, in a political reunion that could reshape alignments in Kilifi County and the wider Coast region as parties position themselves for next year's elections.

The reunion comes barely three months after Jumwa dramatically announced her departure from UDA, accusing the party leadership of frustrating her political ambitions and failing to support her quest for the Kilifi gubernatorial seat.

On July 30, 2026, Jumwa announced her resignation during a press conference at her Kakuyuni home in Malindi, saying her attempts to have her grievances addressed by the President had repeatedly been unsuccessful.

Among her concerns was what she described as humiliation and rejection within the ruling party, including an alleged incident in which she was chased out of State House during a meeting between Ruto and Coast leaders.

She also accused sections of the ruling coalition of undermining her gubernatorial ambitions, claiming that the political arrangements being pursued in Kilifi were designed to deny her an opportunity to contest for the county's top seat.

President William Ruto recieve former Cabinet Secretary Aisha Jumwa back to the ruling United Democratic Alliance (UDA) on November 12, 2026. [PCS]

Jumwa, who was among UDA's founding members and one of Ruto's most vocal mobilisers at the Coast during the 2022 elections, said her loyalty to the people of Kilifi outweighed her allegiance to any political party.

"My loyalty to the people of Kilifi will always be greater than my loyalty to any political party. The voice of the people of Kilifi is louder than the voice of UDA," she declared during her exit announcement.

Her departure marked a significant political shift, particularly given her central role in mobilising support for Ruto in the Coast region.

In August, Jumwa turned to the opposition, where she was warmly received by Wiper Patriotic Front leader Kalonzo Musyoka, who visited her at her Kakuyuni residence on August 14 alongside a delegation of party leaders, including Nyali MP Mohamed Ali, Kitui Senator Enoch Wambua and Wundanyi MP Danson Mwashako.

Kalonzo subsequently proposed Jumwa for the position of Wiper Deputy Party Leader, citing her political experience and influence, while also backing her ambition to contest the Kilifi governorship on a Wiper ticket.

Jumwa embraced the new political alliance, declaring support for the one-term movement and threatening to mobilise UDA supporters in Kilifi to deregister from the ruling party and join Wiper.

"We are the ones who registered UDA members in Kilifi, and we are embarking on a grassroots campaign to deregister them from UDA and join Wiper," she said at the time.

On September 8, she attended a meeting involving Wiper leaders and Coast gubernatorial aspirants, including Mohammed Ali and Danson Mwashako, as the party intensified efforts to expand its influence in the region.

However, the political alliance has now taken another turn, with Jumwa returning to the party she had accused of frustrating her ambitions.

Announcing her return, President Ruto welcomed the former Cabinet Secretary back into UDA, signalling renewed efforts to consolidate the ruling party's support in the Coast region.

"I look forward to working with her to advance the party’s transformation agenda at the Coast and across the country. We remain committed to uniting leaders and Kenyans around our shared vision of a united, inclusive and prosperous Kenya," the President said.

Her return comes as Ruto steps up political mobilisation in the Coast region ahead of the 2027 elections, with Kilifi emerging as an important battleground for competing political formations.

Jumwa's political journey has been characterised by shifting alliances. She previously served under the Orange Democratic Movement (ODM), representing Malindi in Parliament before becoming Kilifi's first Woman Representative between 2013 and 2017.

She later became one of Ruto's key political allies and served in his Cabinet.

World.title: Buxton estate tensions escalate after county officials attacked
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

At the heart of the dispute is a joint venture agreement between the county and the developer, which provides for the county to receive 10 per cent of all housing units. [Robert Menza, Standard]

A dispute over the multibillion-shilling Buxton Point housing project in Mombasa turned violent after county officials were allegedly attacked while enforcing a government order suspending construction over outstanding contractual obligations.

The confrontation came a day after County Executive Committee Member (CECM) for Lands, Housing, and Urban Development Mohamed Hussein ordered GulfCap Real Estate to halt all construction activities pending the resolution of disputes involving the county government and hundreds of former Buxton Estate residents.

The officials were reportedly pelted with stones as they attempted to serve the developer with an enforcement notice, with allegations that individuals linked to businessman Suleiman Shahbal were involved in the confrontation.

Hussein condemned the incident, saying attempts to intimidate government officers would not derail efforts to enforce the law and protect public interests.

"Let them bring goons, machetes, and stones if they want. I am not intimidated. I will execute my duties, and nobody will threaten me. The law must be followed, regardless of who you are or how much money you have," he said.

"We are here for the people of Mombasa, and we will ensure their rights are protected. Nobody is above the law," he added.

The November 10 enforcement notice, issued by County Director of Physical Planning Qassim Ali, directed GulfCap Real Estate to stop further development activities and obtain valid construction permits.

The notice, issued under Section 72(1) of the Physical and Land Use Planning Act, cited construction under a varied development plan without county approval and an ongoing dispute involving the developer, former tenants, and the county government.

The notice was reportedly received by the project's manager, Billy Okendo.

At the heart of the dispute is a joint venture agreement between the county and the developer, which provides for the county to receive 10 per cent of all housing units. [Robert Menza, Standard]

At the heart of the dispute is a joint venture agreement between the county government and the developer, which provides for the county to receive 10 per cent of all housing units and commercial spaces developed in the first and second phases.

An addendum to the agreement signed on January 15, 2020, outlines the county's entitlement, with the allocation expected to be transferred upon completion of the second phase.

In a letter dated April 30, 2025, the county demanded 10 per cent of the proposed 1,800 housing units, translating to 180 apartments. The demand was renewed in February 2026, with the county seeking details on how the allocation would be implemented.

However, in correspondence dated September 22, 2026, the Department of Lands, Urban Planning and Housing expressed concern over what it described as the developer's failure to provide substantive responses to previous demands.

The county also questioned whether GulfCap had provided performance security equivalent to 10 per cent of the total construction cost for each phase, as required under the agreement.

It further demanded proof of payment of the Project Development Fee, which is payable in instalments as the project progresses.

The county said it had also raised technical and planning concerns during a meeting with the developer on April 15, 2026, including the need to address outstanding issues and resubmit the masterplan application.

But the dispute goes beyond the county's financial and contractual entitlement, with more than 500 former residents accusing the developer of failing to honour promises made when they were displaced in 2019.

John Tsuma, Secretary-General of the Buxton Tenants Welfare Association, said former residents had waited for more than seven years to return to their homes despite assurances that they would be prioritised once construction was completed.

"We are very disappointed by what happened. We had a meeting with the CECM, and he made it clear that all construction activities should stop until the outstanding issues are resolved. We did not go there to fight anybody. We wanted the directive implemented," Tsuma said.

He accused the developer of benefiting from the project while former residents continued to struggle to secure the houses they were promised.

"The developer has benefited from A to Z. He was given land by the county government, and the houses were sold off-plan. Yet, when it comes to fulfilling the promises made to former residents, we are still being taken around in circles," he said.

Tsuma said residents were not demanding free houses but wanted the affordable tenant-purchase arrangement they were promised before leaving the estate.

"We are not asking for free houses. We want the tenant-purchase arrangement that was promised to us so that we can pay for the houses and return to our homes," he said.

He also questioned why the developer had allegedly failed to surrender the county government's 184 housing units under the joint venture arrangement.

Mohamed Mzee Rubea, chairman of the evicted Buxton residents, said the money paid to the families during their displacement was a relocation allowance and not compensation for their homes.

He said the former tenants were given Sh240,000, with assurances that they would rent alternative accommodation for 12 months and return once the houses were completed.

"What we received was relocation money, not compensation for our houses. We were told to take the money and rent houses for 12 months and that we would be the first people to return once construction was completed. But here we are, more than seven years later, still waiting," Rubea said.

He said the original agreement involved 522 former tenants who were promised priority access to houses under the redevelopment.

Rubea added that each household was also promised Sh60,000 as a deposit towards acquiring a house under the tenant-purchase scheme.

"We were promised Sh60,000 as a deposit for those who would take up the houses. The developer later said the money would only be given to those who actually acquired the units. We are still waiting, and many of us have not received anything," he said. At the heart of the dispute is a joint venture agreement between the county and the developer, which provides for the county to receive 10 per cent of all housing units. [Robert Menza, Standard]

He further claimed that the county had written to the developer in 2023, 2024, and 2025 seeking engagement over the outstanding commitments.

Mutua Mutia, another former resident, said the prolonged dispute had left families frustrated, especially after they were promised they would return within a year.

"I have lived in Buxton since I was a young boy. My firstborn child is now more than 30 years old, and the history of Buxton is one that pains us. We were evicted with the promise that we would return after one year, but today it is seven years and we are still struggling," Mutia said.

The former residents are also demanding the reconstruction of an Early Childhood Development (ECD) centre demolished to pave the way for the project, as well as the construction of a promised community social centre.

Hussein said the county had yet to receive either facility or its share of the housing project.

"The county has not received its 10 per cent share to date. There was an agreement that the demolished ECD centre would be reconstructed and handed over to the county, alongside a community social centre, but we have not received either," he said.

The first phase of Buxton Point delivered 584 housing units in 2023, while the second phase is expected to provide between 1,400 and 1,500 additional apartments. Completion had been scheduled for August 2027.

However, GulfCap Real Estate Chief Executive Officer Chris Ochieng defended the developer's position, saying 492 housing units would be handed over to buyers by December.

While urging the county to stop politicising the project, Ochieng warned that the ongoing controversy risks disrupting the project’s completion and affecting hundreds of workers who depend on it for their livelihoods.

He said the county government's 10 per cent share would be transferred upon completion of the project.

He also maintained that the developer had supported displaced residents by providing Sh240,000 for relocation and offering them preferential rates to purchase apartments.

Ochieng said the continued involvement of county officials in the dispute was unfortunate, particularly at a time when 492 homeowners are expecting to take possession of their houses in December.

He noted that the controversy was not only creating uncertainty among prospective homeowners but also threatening the livelihoods of hundreds of people employed directly and indirectly through the project.

“It is very unfortunate that Mombasa County officials are bringing politics into a national project. We have 492 homeowners who expect to take possession of their units by December. Beyond the homeowners, hundreds of people depend on this project for employment and their daily livelihoods,” said Ochieng.

He called on the county leadership to allow the project to proceed without unnecessary political interference, arguing that Mombasa has previously witnessed housing projects that stalled despite significant public interest.

World.title: Sakaja defends Sh43.7b drop in Nairobi County's pending bills before Senate
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja tells Senate that the Sh118 billion in pending bills was inherited from his predecessors. [File, Standard]

Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja has told the Senate that pending bills in the city have been reduced from Sh118.79 billion to Sh75.07 billion through verification and payment.

Sakaja revealed that internal verification established that the Sh43.73 billion reduction was not achieved solely through payments but also involved legal assessments, court-ordered adjustments and the verification of disputed claims.

The governor, who appeared before the Senate County Public Accounts Committee at Parliament Buildings in Nairobi on Monday, said addressing the inherited debt required establishment of a verification committee to scrutinise the entire outstanding amount and establish the validity of the claims.

“The reduction of Nairobi County pending bills by Sh 43.73 billion was not achieved entirely through cash payments but also involved adjustments arising from legal assessments, suspended government-guaranteed loans, court-ordered reductions and disputed claims,” said Sakaja.

He told the Senate Committee chaired by Homa Bay Senator Moses Kajwang that the Sh118 billion in pending bills was inherited from his predecessors and that he had constituted a committee to undertake an internal verification of the entire amount before payments were done.

Sakaja explained that the verification established that the reduction was not solely through payments but also involved adjustments arising from legal assessments, suspended government-guaranteed loans, court decisions and disputed claims.

“I would like to inform Senators that my administration has provided a detailed schedule accounting for the Sh43.73 billion pending bills reduction through adjustments and reconciliations,” he said.

The governor said that of this amount Sh1.63 billion related to legal assessments, while Sh19.14 billion represented government-guaranteed loans whose servicing had been suspended due to a lack of supporting documentation and loan schedules.

Sakaja told Senators that Sh19.2 billion related to LAPFUND interest and penalties which the County said had been reduced following a court consent that brought the claim down to approximately Sh8.2 billion.

He said that they had provided a signed indemnity form, in accordance with County Treasury rules governing misplaced payment documents, alongside a financial memo confirming that the works had been undertaken and payment made.

“The audit further raised concerns over Sh16.04 million in receivables from non-exchange transactions, which lacked sufficient supporting documentation,” said Sakaja.

The governor told senators that beyond the verification of pending bills his administration had also strengthened the county’s legal department to reduce expenditure on external legal services and protect public resources.

Sakaja noted that through the reforms, Nairobi saved approximately Sh8.48 billion in legal costs over two financial years by expanding its in-house legal capacity, handling more litigation internally and negotiating reductions in legal fees claimed by private advocates.

According to the County Assembly’s Justice and Legal Affairs Committee, of the 174 court cases concluded during the period under review, 84 were handled by the County’s in-house legal team, with 47 determined in Nairobi’s favour, representing a 56 per cent success rate.

Kajwang, commended the County for reducing its pending bills but asked the Governor to provide additional documentation supporting the payments and processes undertaken to account for the Sh43.73 billion reductions.

“The Senate County Public Accounts Committee requires further clarification on the verification exercise and the adjustments made to the outstanding debt,” said Kajwang.

World.title: Gachagua dismisses opposition divisions as 'polygamous family' rivalry
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Democracy for the Citizens Party (DCP) leader Rigathi Gachagua during a church service in Isinya, Kajiado County on November 8, 2026. [Peterson Githaiga, Standard]

Democracy for the Citizens Party (DCP) leader Rigathi Gachagua has dismissed claims of divisions within the Opposition, describing the disagreements among its leaders as normal sibling rivalry in a polygamous family, while insisting that the coalition remains united behind plans to field a single presidential candidate in the 2027 General Election.

Gachagua said the Opposition leaders were committed to working together to challenge President William Ruto, despite their differing opinions on the timing of selecting a joint presidential flagbearer and occasional disagreements among their political camps.

Speaking during a church service in Isinya, Kajiado County, the former Deputy President likened the political differences to children from the same father competing for attention but eventually uniting whenever an external threat emerges.

“The Opposition is united to a man, and we have agreed that we will have a single presidential candidate. Everybody is committed, and we talk on a daily basis. The only challenge is normal petty problems,” he said.

He added that the disagreements should not be interpreted as a breakdown of the coalition, maintaining that such differences were healthy and expected in a broad political alliance.

“Ile shida kidogo ni ya boma, watoto wengi wa baba mmoja. Watoto huko ndani, oh, baba anakupenda kuliko mimi. Mbona ulinunua kiatu kabla mimi? Si hiyo ni kawaida kwa polygamous family?” he posed.

Gachagua said the bigger threat to Opposition unity was not necessarily disagreements among its principals but the conduct of their supporters, social media influencers and political bloggers, whom he accused of fuelling unnecessary tensions through insults and online confrontations.

He cautioned Opposition leaders against allowing overzealous supporters to dictate their political relationships, warning that unchecked political attacks could eventually weaken the coalition and undermine its common objective.

“If there is anything to separate us, it is our supporters and social media bloggers. Wanawakisha moto hakuna, watu wangu na wa Matiang'i wanatukanana na sisi tunakula breakfast pamoja,” he said.

He further claimed that some political influencers associated with his DCP party had been recruited and allegedly paid by individuals opposed to him to attack his leadership and the party.

Gachagua urged coalition principals to exercise restraint and avoid reacting to every provocation from supporters, insisting that political leaders must remain focused on the bigger picture.

“I want to ask leaders in the Opposition, be careful. Don't listen to overzealous supporters and influencers; they will lead you astray. Remain focused,” he warned.
