World.title: Macron urges unity as Francophonie summit opens in Cambodia
World.content:
Leaders of French-speaking nations gathered in Phnom Penh as a row over who should lead the Francophonie and Congo’s threat to quit put pressure on Macron to broker consensus.

A summit of French-speaking nations opened Sunday in Phnom Penh, with French President Emmanuel Macron trying to head off a walkout by the group's biggest African member over who will lead it next.

The Organisation internationale de la Francophonie (OIF) brings together about 90 states and governments, including 53 full members, from the Democratic Republic of Congo to Canada.

It is made up of countries that use French as an official language, former French colonies, and other states with substantial historic ties to France.

What is the disagreement about?

The OIF is set to choose its next secretary-general on Monday.

Rwanda's Louise Mushikiwabo, who has held the post since 2018, is seeking a third term. DR Congo has threatened to leave if she is re-elected, accusing Rwanda of backing the M23 armed group in eastern Congo, an accusation Rwanda denies.

DR Congo has 57.3 million French speakers, second only to France, per the OIF, so its exit would be a major blow. Mali, Niger and Burkina Faso withdrew from the association last year after their membership was suspended over coups.

On Saturday, DR Congo said it was withdrawing its candidate, Juliana Lumumba, the 71-year-old daughter of the country's martyred independence hero, Patrice Lumumba.

Kinshasa said it would back former Romanian prime minister Dacian Ciolos to allow "consensus around a unifying candidacy."

AFP described the offer as conditional on Rwanda also stepping aside. However, Rwanda's foreign minister said Mushikiwabo would stay in the race.

What did Macron say?

Macron warned against "internal fractures" in the group.

"We must ensure that we preserve what constitutes its strength—namely, its unity," he said.

Rwanda said Macron had asked President Paul Kagame to withdraw his candidate, which it refused. Macron's office said Paris suggested both candidates step aside.

"With that intervention we're going backwards, to the idea that France decides," a member of a non-African delegation told AFP anonymously. France is the largest donor, and Canada provides 25% of the budget.

Macron arrives amid unrest at home, where more than 600,000 people marched earlier this month over wages and in support of student protests, with thousands arrested.

UN Special Rapporteur Tom Andrews urged delegates to press Cambodia, which has been referred to as a de facto one-party state, to free detained activists. "No one should be detained for defending human rights, reporting on matters of public concern, or voicing critical opinions," he said.

World.title: Germany news: Germany holds national day of remembrance
World.content:
Skip next section Germany marks day of mourning for victims of war and oppression

Germany is remembering victims of war and oppression Image: imago images/Udo Gottschalk

Events are taking place around Germany for the Volkstrauertag (people's day of mourning), a day on which armed forces personnel and civilians who died in armed conflicts and victims of violent state oppression are commemorated.

Austrian President Alexander Van der Bellen is to speak in the parliament at the main commemoration ceremony of the German War Graves Commission at midday.

His presence reflects the large number of Austrians who were killed in action in the Second World War while fighting for the German Wehrmacht following the annexation of their country by Nazi Germany in 1938.

German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier, the patron of the commission, will also hold a speech and lay a wreath.

Last year, Steinmeier decreed that the Volkstrauertag should also commemorate people who were persecuted and killed by the Nazis because of their sexual identity, as well as police officers who have lost their lives in the course of duty.

There will also be a remembrance ceremony at the Jewish Cemetery in Berlin for those of the Jewish faith killed in World War I.

In remarks to the DPA news agency ahead of the remembrance day, the speaker of the lower house of German parliament, or Bundestag, Julia Klöckner, called on society to actively defend democracy.

Klöckner said that the Volkstrauertag was a reminder of how destructive tyranny and contempt for human dignity can be.

"Democracy is the antidote here," she said. "But it is not an heirloom. It wastes away when we do not constantly renew its promise of basic rights and freedom."

World.title: Beijing faces its Russia dilemma amid talk of Xi-Trump-Putin summit
World.content:
China is forced to tread carefully as it considers hosting a meeting between Xi Jinping, Vladimir Putin, and Donald Trump. While the optics are sure to favor Moscow, Beijing is risking its image on the global stage.

An unprecedented meeting between the leaders of China, Russia and the United States could be happening on the sidelines of Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in China's tech hub of Shenzhen this week.

China has yet to confirm that the meeting will take place. However, a Chinese Foreign Ministry official recently told the press that Beijing was "in communication" with relevant parties. In Moscow, a Kremlin representative said work on "coordination" was underway.

The clearest indication about the potential summit came from US President Donald Trump last weekend. Talking to reporters at a Florida airport, Trump said he "thinks" one of the meetings planned for APEC will be with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping.

Trump, Putin or Xi: Who really runs the world? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Is the world set for a 'new Yalta'?

Despite the lack of official confirmation from either Beijing, Moscow, or Washington, the media has already dubbed the potential trilateral summit a "new Yalta," invoking the optics of the US, UK, and Soviet Union convening at the end of World War II and deciding on the new geopolitical power balance in the Crimean resort town.

The Yalta summit saw Stalin, Roosevelt and Churchill represent the three main victorious powers of WWII Image: RIA Novosti/SNA/imago

At the same time, nobody seems to be quite sure what the three leaders would talk about if China agrees to host the trilateral summit at APEC.

In his brief remarks to reporters on Sunday, Trump avoided mentioning Russia's war in Ukraine when asked about the possibility of the meeting, bringing up only "Iran" and "denuclearization" as possible talking points.

The Chinese Foreign Ministry reported "no information" when questioned earlier this week about the potential substance of talks.

End of campaign to isolate Putin?

A three-way meeting with a photo op would be a big diplomatic win for Russia's President Putin. Since launching the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, the Kremlin chief has faced years of diplomatic boycott by Kyiv's allies, most notably the US under Trump's predecessor Joe Biden.

Putin first pitched the idea of a trilateral summit last month during a call with Trump. The Wall Street Journal has reported that Putin wanted the meeting to discuss an end to his war in Ukraine.

For the US, the president standing shoulder to shoulder with the leaders of America's foremost rivals could be a bad look, although Trump has already made a show of personally greeting both leaders with a red carpet at different points during his second term.

As host, China is in an even trickier position. While Russia and China are broadly aligned on many issues, Beijing does not want to be explicitly tied to Russia's war in Ukraine and harm China's efforts to present itself as a long-term force for global stability.

EU wary of being left out of Ukraine talks

The Chinese government is also working to rebalance economic ties with the EU. The European powers would likely bristle at a summit hosted by China and discussing the war in Ukraine without Kyiv or Brussels present at the table.

Europe seeks role in Ukraine peace talks To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

"China is clearly uneasy about the possible trilateral meeting with the US and Russia, and although Beijing has shifted its position from saying nothing to admitting that the three powers are in contact, the vagueness of these declarations seems deliberate," Alicja Bachulska, Asia policy fellow at the European Council on Foreign Relations (ECFR), told DW.

"Beijing is aware of the potential negative optics of the 'Yalta 2.0' framing, even if this historical comparison is inaccurate and does not reflect current geopolitical dynamics," Bachulska said.

She notes the trilateral meeting could "trigger further escalation in the already worsening relations between China and the EU" if Ukraine is discussed with no Europeans in the room.

For China, there is also little to gain in terms of optics. Images of Xi standing with Trump, the leader of Beijing's top rival, and Putin, Beijing's partner in opposing the US, could present an awkward look.

"Even if the meeting only yields a photo opportunity, it could nevertheless severely erode China's image," Bachulska added.

Beijing and Moscow stick to 'no limits' partnership

Putin and Xi have met some 40 times since the Chinese president came to power in 2012.

The two neighboring countries have grown especially close following the declaration of "no limits" partnership accord in early 2022. The move was announced by Xi and Putin on the sidelines of Beijing Winter Olympics, just weeks before the full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

The current Russia-China ties are deeper than they have been in decades.

At the core of the axis between the two nations is a long-term strategy to contain US power while fostering an alternative global order both Moscow and Beijing can use for their own ends.

China helping Russia from the sidelines

Throughout the course of the Ukraine war, which is nearing the end of its fifth year with no solution in sight, Beijing has quietly provided Russia with crucial market for energy exports, while supplying technology and so-called "dual-use" goods.

While China did not explicitly provide Russia with weapons, its exports included high-tech components that could be used for modern weapons systems like drones.

Russia needs China trade more than ever To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Officially, Beijing maintains neutrality on the Ukraine war and has refused to take responsibility for its outcome.

"China is more interested in reforming global governance in ways that reflect its preferences and red lines while preserving a collegial appearance," Aurelio Insisa, senior analyst at the Berlin-based Mercator Institute for China Studies (MERICS), told DW.

Even if China agrees to host the meeting, it will likely avoid framing it as three top powers making decisions for the rest of the world, according to Insisa.

"Embracing the 'G3' narrative would undermine its image as a champion of the Global South and developing countries. It is also worth noting that Beijing has shown no interest in engaging with the one pressing issue that could realistically be addressed in such a trilateral format: nuclear disarmament," he added.

What are the actual limits of China-Russia axis?

In a report published in August, the US-China Economic and Security Review Commission (USCC), painted China as a "decisive enabler" of Russia's war in Ukraine.

Beijing was "converting Moscow's dependence into lasting military, technological, economic, and geopolitical advantages while avoiding the obligations of a formal alliance," according to the US body.

However, the commission also noted there were limits to Beijing's strategic support, and intelligence and security concerns remain a constraint on deeper cooperation. The report emphasizes the relationship is more of a strategic alignment than an alliance, with deep mistrust remaining in some key areas.

Russian defense firms, for instance, have accused Chinese companies of stealing intellectual property. Beijing, on the other hand, is concerned with Russia's growing strategic relationship with North Korea, which has reduced Pyongyang's dependence on China.

Why a new Russia-North Korea road bridge worries Ukraine To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

China and Russia also differ on nuclear doctrine. While Beijing maintains a longstanding "no first use" policy, Moscow uses nuclear threats as part of its strategy.

China getting a 'privileged vantage point' on Ukraine war

But for now, the benefits of alignment remain.

MERICS' analyst Insisa believes the cooperation between Russia and China will largely continue within this year's framework, including Russia providing energy and potentially transfering military technology in the "few remaining areas where it retains an advantage."

"China, in turn, will continue to supply dual-use technologies, purchase Russian energy, provide Moscow with a measure of diplomatic cover, and — more importantly — offer channels for circumventing Western sanctions," he added.

Notably, China will also get a "privileged vantage point" on how the battlefield in Ukraine is evolving land warfare.

"Strategic distrust between the two sides, particularly Russia's concerns about economic dependence on China, will continue to limit the scope of their cooperation," Insisa said.

World.title: Could universal basic income be part of the solution in an AI economy?
World.content:
The scale of the economic disruption caused by AI has led even conservative politicians to talk about universal basic income. But economists are not convinced, and campaigners think we need to ask deeper questions.

At the German government's 2026 "Digital Summit" in early November, Chancellor Friedrich Merz was asked by a journalist to square a difficult economic circle: If artificial intelligence could make hundreds of thousands of people redundant in the next few years, might it become necessary for the government to give people a basic income to ease the ensuing economic disaster?

Surprisingly, Merz didn't respond with a flat dismissal — as might be expected from a conservative politician known for his neoliberal, market-friendly views.

"I've always been a bit cautious about this issue in recent years," he said, as reported by the news outlet RND. "However, I'm also well aware that the issue of AI will change our working world so fundamentally that we'll have to give serious thought to many of these issues in the coming years — including the question: Is our productivity not good enough?"

What makes this ambiguity notable is that much of Merz's policies since becoming chancellor last year have involved making Germans work more: His government's planned pension reforms would see Germany's retirement age being raised. In July this year, he announced a crackdown on sick leave. And in spring last year, having barely taken office, he caused much consternation by criticizing the concept of a "work-life balance" and declaring, "We in this country must work more and more efficiently."

What are the German government's pension, labor reforms? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

The impending job rupture

But those policies seem to contradict the impending realities of the labor market in an AI world. This week, the head of Germany's Federal Employment Agency, Andrea Nahles, warned that the introduction AI would cost Germany as many 800,000 jobs in the next 15 years. Though she also said AI could eventually create a similar number of jobs, clearly the socio-economic upheaval would be considerable.

Nahles is not the only leading figure concerned about job losses caused by AI. Karsten Wildberger, Germany's minister for digital transformation and government modernization, takes any opportunity he can to warn that Germany must prepare for the economic disruptions of AI.

And even for Wildberger, a former CEO of a massive retail company, part of the future economy might come down to giving people free money. He was convinced, he told the Neue Osnabrücker Zeitung in March, "that an unconditional basic income can be part of the solution to cushion the upheavals in the labor market."

How AI is changing the working world To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Why tech bosses love UBI

Campaigners have cautiously welcomed this new openness from unexpected quarters. "It shows that in the face of technological transformation we also need to look differently at the question of how we need to secure people's economic stability," said Kirsten Herrmann, board member at the non-profit Mein Grundeinkommen (My Basic Income), which runs various projects examining the social and economic impact of UBI.

"But I also think that individual statements by politicians don't amount to a political change, of course," she told DW. "It just means that we need to enter a serious and constructive debate about what kind of a role a basic income can play."

The idea of a universal basic income (UBI) is very old: The English Renaissance philosopher Thomas More mentions it in his 1516 book Utopia, for instance. But since the 20th century, it has largely been seen as an idealistic notion adopted by leftists — that is, until some of the world's most high-profile tech bosses latched onto the idea as a way to offset the utopian advances that they said AI would bring. In 2017, Elon Musk, who had co-founded the corporation OpenAI two years earlier, predicted that a universal basic income would at some stage become inevitable.

Since then, leading figures in the AI sector, including Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic, and Sam Altman, the other founder of OpenAI, have all gone on record in support of UBI (though Altman's interest has cooled somewhat since he launched a massive UBI experiment in the US in 2019).

But Herrmann says it's a "double-edged sword" when such figures mention the idea. She is not convinced that organizations like hers and people like Elon Musk want the same thing. "On the one hand, it's always nice when the debate about a basic income gets attention from prominent voices," she said. "On the other hand, the basic income that people from the tech business talk about is a kind of neoliberal basic income: They talk about what to do when there are no more profitable jobs for people, because they still actually do need people to do certain things, whereas we talk about a basic income that is meant to give people a secure economic base — before the crisis in the job market happens."

Is AI killing creative jobs? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

AI and basic income

What makes the comments of Merz and Wildberger all the more eyebrow-raising is that mainstream German economists have long since rejected the basic income idea. Dominik Enste, director of the democracy, society, and economic ethics department at the German Economic Institute (IW) in Cologne, dismissed the idea out of hand — AI or no AI. UBI was, he said, just too expensive, especially in a country that already has plenty of social welfare costs.

"Many economists have calculated that implementing this in many countries is financially unfeasible — in Germany, for one, simply because of the need to fund commitments that have already been made (including pension payments)," he told DW in an email.

However, he also added: "We will have to change our social security systems if work is replaced by AI and, if necessary, tax AI-generated income. But it will be a conditional basic income that still provides incentives to earn a living."

Other economists are more positive about the idea. "How this plays out depends on many choices we make, and on who makes these choices, in whose interest," said Maximilian Kasy, professor of economics at Oxford University and author of a book on the impact of AI on society. "But a lot of the current thrust is to replace workers to increase profits and increase corporate control, though this is not the only path possible."

Kasy also thinks that is a good idea, "especially if it's financed in a progressive way (so that only those at the lower end of the income distribution are net recipients)," he told DW by email. "The 'small print' matters very much, though!"

Work-life integration: A new ideal? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

If the warnings of Wildberger, Musk, Altman et al. are to be believed, AI is already causing a bigger upheaval than any other technological advance in history: Partly because of the speed of the innovations, but also because of the scale of the potential impact: AI innovation is affecting the jobs of the traditional urban middle classes across the entire world. In 2024, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) predicted that some 40% of employment in the world would be shaped by AI innovations, and as much as 60% in rich, industrialized nations.

For her part, Herrmann thinks we are not yet asking the truly fundamental questions about the socio-economic implications of AI: Not just how do we replace the lost jobs and keep the capitalist system going, but what do we actually want to use AI for? As she puts it: "Who actually profits when we become more productive through AI? And how do we redistribute that profit to everyone?"

This, she argues, is why there needs to be more debate about how exactly AI is used in the world of work: "Which jobs are going to be replaced by AI is not some law of nature," Herrmann said. "It's something that we can shape politically and socially — and then the bigger question is: Who gets a say?"

World.title: Tens of thousands continue to protest across France
World.content:
Some 106,000 people marched through French cities for a fifth consecutive weekend of protests, marking the lowest turnout in recent weeks.

Tens of thousands of protesters took to the streets across France on Saturday to demonstrate against the rising cost of living and strained public services, the Interior Ministry said.

Saturday's demonstrations drew their lowest turnout in recent weeks. Some 106,000 people marched through French cities, with 24,000 in Paris alone. The previous weekend, some 146,000 people had participated nationwide.

The number of arrests was also significantly lower. Police detained 219 people across the country, according to the Interior Ministry.

Although the demonstrations were largely peaceful, police fired tear gas in Paris, Bordeaux and the western city of Nantes, including after some protesters shot fireworks.

French business owners share harrowing accounts of violent protests To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

France's protests expose deeper anger

Mass protests have swept across the European Union's second-largest economy for more than a month.

What began in September as student protests against teacher shortages and poor facilities has since evolved into a broader movement fuelled by anger over the rising cost of living, strained public services and police brutality.

In mid-October, around 565,000 people took to the streets across France, as riots, looting and clashes disrupted demonstrations in several cities.

As France entered its fifth consecutive weekend of nationwide unrest, President Emmanuel Macron's approval ratings fell to the lowest level since he took office in 2017, according to recent polls.

The French government doesn't have much room to respond to the protesters' demands due to its high debt.

World.title: Philippines wins first Eurovision Song Contest Asia
World.content:
Eleven countries took part in the competition in Bangkok. Teenage winner Carmelle Collado's winning dance song is a tribute to Filipino women.

The Phillippines on Saturday became the first winner of the Asian version of the Eurovision Song Contest.

Who took part in the event and which songs were featured?

Eleven countries, including South Korea, Malaysia and Vietnam, took part in the song contest in the Thai capital, Bangkok. However, major nations in the region such as China, Japan and India were absent from the event.

19-year-old Carmelle Collado's dance song "Sobra-Sobra" (Too Much) won the competition. The song, which features lyrics in both English and Tagalog, is an empowering tribute to Filipino women.

The Philippines received 211 points in the competition, with Thailand in second place with 170 points. Vietnam placed third with 164 points, while Malaysia landed in fourth place on 152 points.

Thai duo Mang X Daou came in second place with their romantic pop tune 'Aroma' Image: Chanakarn Laosarakham/AFP

National juries in the participating countries and the viewing audience awarded the points.

Vietnam's Toc Tien performed the lively song 'Em Tien' on leaves of the lotus, a flower associated with her country Image: Sakchai Lalit/AP Photo/picture alliance

The competition featured motifs inspired by host city Bangkok, with the participants making their way to the stage on tuk-tuks and waving the flag of the countries they represent in a parade.

Malaysia's Aina Abdul performed the ballad 'Bluest Sky' with water being used to represent the song's emotional buildup Image: Chanakarn Laosarakham/AFP

Will the Eurovision Song Contest Asia become a sensation?

The contest featured some references to the camp European competition. Bulgarian singer Dara performed "Bangaranga," the song which won the Eurovision Song Contest in Vienna in May.

It's unclear whether Eurovision Song Contest Asia will be as popular as the original competition, which received 131 million viewers this year. Tickets for the Bangkok event were still available just hours before it kicked off.

In 2022, a US spinoff, the American Song Contest, featured acts from all 50 US states. The competition, hosted by rapper Snoop Dogg and American Idol star Kelly Clarkson, only lasted for one season.

World.title: SpaceX carries out first-ever spaceship capture
World.content:
The successful recovery of SpaceX's Starship marks a breakthrough in founder Elon Musk’s goal of developing a fully reusable rocket system.

SpaceX's Starship spacecraft returned from its longest-yet flight in orbit on Saturday to the tower it was launched from on Friday.

The spaceship descended and smoothly slipped between the mechanical "chopstick arms" above Launch Pad 2 in the US state of Texas. It was the first key recovery of the rocket system's centerpiece vessel in the company's decadelong effort to develop a fully reusable rocket.

"Can you believe it?" SpaceX commentator Dan Huot shouted. "Look at her! Baby, she’s back!"

SpaceX's Starship hit key milestone

It was the 15th test flight of the world's biggest and most powerful rocket system. The Starship spacecraft orbited Earth 14 times for over 22 hours, during which it deployed 26 Starlink satellites.

The successful return marked a ​key milestone in the multibillion-dollar development of Starship, which billionaire Elon Musk sees ​as crucial to SpaceX's satellite business and ambitions to put humans on the Moon and eventually Mars.

NASA welcomed the news. The US space agency is paying billions of dollars for Starship to land Artemis astronauts on the moon later this decade and help build a permanent lunar base.

"It was almost magic," NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman wrote on X.

SpaceX still investigating booster malfunction

SpaceX also intended to capture the bottom part of the rocket, known as the Super Heavy booster, but the lower stage recovery was aborted, and it exploded over the Gulf of Mexico shortly after launch on Friday.

SpaceX's Kate Tice said its engines stopped firing too soon. The booster's guidance system sensed it was not in the correct position and initiated the self-destruction protocol. Engineers are still investigating the cause.

SpaceX caught the Super Heavy Booster on three earlier test flights. Developing a fully reusable rocket system is key to SpaceX’s goal to drive down the cost of spaceflight.

World.title: Germany's 2027 budget: A record €561 billion and a mountain of debt
World.content:
The 2027 federal budget proposal has finally been hammered out and is set for a vote in parliament. What are the government's policy priorities in defense, infrastructure, the economy and social spending?

It was 5:55 a.m. on Friday when the Bundestag's Budget Committee concluded its final session.

Following nearly 16 hours of negotiations, lawmakers from the conservative Christian Democratic Union(CDU) and Christian Social Union (CSU) parties, along with their coalition partners from the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD), voted in favor of the 2027 draft budget. The opposition parties — the environmentalist Greens, the socialist Left Party and the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) — voted against it. With that, the way is now clear for the final vote in the Bundestag on November 27.

Reading through the nearly 1,000-page document requires a great deal of number-crunching. Next year, the federal government plans to spend around €561 billion ($620 billion).

But here's the problem: it won't collect nearly enough revenue to cover these expenses. With a shortfall of €123 billion, borrowing will be needed to bridge the gap.

Germany's slow road to recovery To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

But that's not the only problem. On top of all this debt, Germany also has loans for defense spending and for the renovation of the dilapidated infrastructure. Approved by the Bundestag in 2025, these special funds are set to be in place for multiple years.

If the new debt for 2027 is factored in, the total borrowing amounts to over €210 billion. This is the second-highest level of borrowing in the history of the Federal Republic of Germany. The only time Germany borrowed more was during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2021, when borrowing reached €215.4 billion.

This development has drawn sharp criticism from opposition parties. Green Party lawmaker Sebastian Schäfer and his colleague Dietmar Bartsch of the Left Party called it a "gigantic mountain of debt," an "untrustworthy" budget, "irresponsible" policies at the expense of future generations and a lack of future prospects.

Why is debt growing? Crises drive up costs

To understand the reasons behind the growing debt, one has to look beyond the numbers. Every federal budget is a snapshot of the priorities set by a government and a country — in terms of the economy, social issues, security and geopolitics.

What are the German government's pension, labor reforms? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

For 2027, that story continues to be one of crises and wars. While Russia's war against Ukraine is driving up defense spending, the faltering economy is also demanding new investments. At the same time, Germany's population is aging rapidly, which is driving up social spending.

What's more, the crumbling infrastructure must be repaired and modernized, and the energy transition is costing billions. And more than half of all this debt is going toward security and defense.

Defense spending continues to rise

Russia's war against Ukraine will enter its sixth year in 2027. As of the end of June, the federal government estimated its overall support for Ukraine to have reached approximately €100 billion. In response to a request from the AfD in the Bundestag, the government stated: "The federal government will continue to provide Ukraine with political, financial, humanitarian, civil and military support for as long as necessary."

The rearmament of the Bundeswehr and spending on NATO are also putting massive pressure on the budget. The defense budget is set to grow to just under €110 billion in 2027, an increase of around €27 billion compared to last year. Added to this are expenditures from the Bundeswehr's special fund.

Largest budget item: Social spending and pensions

Nevertheless, by far the largest single budget item comes from the Ministry of Labor and Social Affairs, which is set to grow to over €200 billion. There are plans for cost-cutting measures, for example, in basic income support for job seekers. But the costs of old-age pension benefits continue to rise.

How risky is the German government's borrowing spree? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

People born in the 1960s have begun to retire. Back then, more than 1 million children were born each year. But birth rates nearly halved in the early 1970s and have continued to decline since then. As a result, there will be an increasing number of retirees and a decreasing number of working-age individuals in the coming years.

The pension funds cannot be financed by the pension contributions of this dwindling workforce and have to be subsidized by the government. Already, contributions to the pension insurance system — which are split equally between employees and employers — will have to be increased. They are expected to rise to just under 20% of gross salary.

The Federal Employment Agency, too, has long been unable to make ends meet on contributions alone. In 2027, subsidies of more than €8 billion from the federal budget are planned.

Germany no longer a model of fiscal discipline

Anyone comparing Germany's current budget situation with that of past years will be rubbing their eyes in disbelief. It wasn't that long ago that Germany was considered a model of fiscal discipline. Between 2014 and 2019, the federal budget managed to avoid taking on new debt for six consecutive years. In some years, there was even money left over.

German industry shifts to defense production amid job losses To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

But the era of "balanced budgets" came to an abrupt end with the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020. However, today Germany is still enjoying the benefits of those years of fiscal stability. Compared to other countries, Germany is still in relatively good shape.

Economic experts warn of rising debt

The key indicator is not the amount of debt along but the debt-to-GDP ratio. It indicates how high the national debt is in relation to annual economic output.

At the end of 2025, it stood at 63.5% for Germany. France, on the other hand, stands at over 110% and Italy at about 135% to 140%, while the US is well above 100%. However, in its latest fall report, the German Council of Economic Experts warned that Germany could be heading down a dangerous path. If debt continues to rise at this rate, the debt-to-GDP ratio could climb to 100% by 2040.

This would also put Germany's creditworthiness on the financial markets at risk. Germany is the only country among the seven leading democratic industrialized nations (G7) that still holds a triple-A (AAA) rating. This is the highest possible credit rating on the financial markets. It signals to investors that the risk of default on German government bonds is extremely low.

German Chancellor Merz vows to push ahead with reforms To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

This also means that interest rates on new loans are not set as high. This is an important point, as interest payments place an increasing burden on the federal budget each year. By 2027, approximately €42 billion in interest payments are expected to be due.

What's the road ahead?

At the end of November, the Bundestag will hold its final debate on the draft budget. Should changes be expected by then? There is disagreement within the government over whether a reduction in the electricity tax might still be possible.

The prospect of such a reduction had been raised by Chancellor Friedrich Merz. On Friday, during a European leaders summit in Dublin, he reiterated: "I expect that we will discuss this again next Tuesday in the coalition committee, and I remain committed to my goal of lowering the electricity tax to the European minimum — in full — starting next year."

World.title: Emma Suárez: “Me he quitado la ansiedad de llegar a todo y a todos. Ahora me toca a mí”
World.content:
La actriz, con 110 películas y 3 premios Goya a sus 62 años, estrena ‘Hermanas’, un duelo interpretativo con Elena Anaya con los abusos sexuales en la familia como fondo

La veo desde lejos, inconfundible con su aire casual y su eterno flequillo rubio, sentada en un velador como única clienta de un elegante y acristalado quiosco madrileño en una mañana gris y lluviosa, componiendo una estampa a lo musa de Hopper, si Hopper hubiera sido madrileño y no gringo y Madrid tuviera mar y no río. Fuera, el otoño explota en toda la gama del rojo al ocre en los espectaculares árboles del Parque del Oeste, aumentando la sensación de oasis de calma entre las prisas urbanas de un martes víspera de una huelga general y del inicio de la campaña electoral. Se agradece. Vengo de ver Hermanas, la película en la que Emma Suárez interpreta a una esposa, madre, hermana y tía en un marco de abusos sexuales dentro de la familia, y tengo el corazón en un puño.

He sufrido viéndola en la película. Esa madre vasca, sufriente y contenida a la vez. ¿Cuánto cuesta esa contención?

Yo también sufrí. Cuando leí el guion, me revolvía yo sola en casa, porque me hacía muchísimas preguntas. Pero la contención era, precisamente, uno de los desafíos del personaje. Desde la mirada de la directora, no se emiten juicios sobre ningún personaje. Y la duda, el miedo y el bloqueo los invaden. En las secuencias con Elena Anaya hubo muchos cortes, y muchas lloreras para poder continuar. En una situación así, te quedas sin palabras. Es fácil juzgar desde fuera por qué no hablan, por qué no lloran, por qué no lo cuentan, pero nos propusimos no juzgarlas.

Usted tiene dos hijos. ¿Se imagina una situación así en su propia familia?

Claro que me la puedo llegar a imaginar. Es que eso sucede constantemente.

Pero siempre les pasa a los otros.

Los otros podemos ser nosotros. Pasa en muchas familias, en todos los estratos sociales, pero no se habla. Los abusos sexuales dentro de las familias son una de las circunstancias por las que están llenas las consultas de psicólogos y psiquiatras. ¿A quién le vas a contar tú que tu pareja está abusando de tu hija? Y eso, si te enteras. Y los niños o niñas abusadas, ¿a quién van a decírselo? Quizá por eso vienes impresionada, porque se apela al espectador.

Impresionan, también, sus careos a cámara con su hermana en la película, Elena Anaya. ¿Se conocían?

Hemos trabajado mucho Elena y yo. Hemos hablado mucho. Nos hemos contado secretos. Nos hemos mirado las almas. Nos hemos contado las vidas. Habíamos coincidido en la serie Innato, y teníamos muchas ganas de trabajar juntas, de mirarnos. Ya teníamos un flechazo, y teníamos un deseo de trabajar juntas. Luego, ese deseo puede funcionar o no. Y con Elena ha funcionado, y, además, para siempre. Nos queremos, nos admiramos; es un regalo que nos ha hecho esta película.

O sea, que un rodaje no tiene por qué ser un campo de batalla.

Para nada. El rodaje tiene que ser un lugar de creación. Claro que hay momentos de tensión, pero para que todo salga lo mejor posible.

Lo digo porque, últimamente, usted ha hablado de roces con algunos directores a lo largo de su carrera. ¿Ha vivido situaciones de abuso?

Mira, yo lo que he vivido ha sido situaciones de imposición de poder, de jerarquías infranqueables en un trabajo que debería ser de equipo. Y eso te silencia, te impide quejarte, te limita. Pero yo siempre he levantado la voz. Todo ha cambiado mucho, pero claro que, de jovencita, he vivido situaciones en que alguien, un hombre, te dice: “Si te portas bien conmigo, te puedo ayudar mucho”. El machismo campaba a sus anchas en toda la sociedad, y eso también se está transformando. Por eso hay que luchar para impedir que haya marcha atrás.

¿Sigue la campaña electoral?

Claro, está ahí. No puedes permanecer ajena a ella y, además, no quiero. Me interpela como ciudadana.

¿Teme esa involución?

Hay un panorama de desgaste, decepción y hay que arreglar cosas. La tremenda polarización me da miedo, porque nos lleva a épocas pasadas, en las que no se permitía el diálogo. Tengo miedo de no seguir avanzando y retroceder. Recuerdo que, de pequeña, había temas tabú, de los que no podía hablar. Recuerdo ese ambiente de silencio y puertas cerradas, y no quiero volver a vivirlo.

¿En qué momento vital se encuentra?

Pues mira, estoy muy bien, sin entrar en detalles, porque si te pones a mirar al mundo, con esta convulsión violenta, esta ira, este no poder conversar, esta falta de amabilidad y de empatía, este miedo a llamar a las cosas por su nombre porque te van a machacar, pues no es para estar contenta. Pero, personalmente, estoy en un momento muy feliz de mi vida: me he quitado la ansiedad.

¿Qué clase de ansiedad?

La de querer llegar a todo, la de no molestar, la de querer agradar a todo el mundo y hacerlo todo bien. Ahora, me acepto más. No es que me guste, hay muchas cosas que no me gustan, pero quizá me estoy acostumbrando a convivir con ellas.

¿Qué ha tenido que suceder para eso?

Pues yo creo que me he hecho mayor, pero sigo conservando el gusto por el juego, la necesidad del sentido del humor y la ilusión, y todo eso me da muchísima satisfacción. No soy una persona amargada, no estoy decepcionada. Bueno, con algunas cosas, sí: siempre he sido una idealista y una soñadora, pero veo que, para cambiar el mundo, habría que cambiar al ser humano, y eso es imposible. Pero el aceptarme, el estar rodeada de gente que quiero y me quiere, tener amigas y amigos, disfrutar de mi soledad, pasear por aquí, ¿has visto qué maravilla de colores? Es un lujo; la belleza de la naturaleza está al alcance de todos, y es gratis.

Le envidio esa serenidad, ¿en su oficio no hay estrés?

Claro que hay presión, y mucha exposición, pero siempre se puede tratar y tratarte bien. No vamos a llegar antes por maltratar a los otros. Tenemos la responsabilidad de escuchar respirar al otro y decir, paremos, hablemos. No nos podemos dejar llevar por la rueda del hámster. La empatía también es tratar de contagiar un poquito de calma a tu alrededor.

Emma Suárez, siempre fiel a su estilo: "Para cambiar, ya están mis personajes", explica. Bernardo Pérez

En Hermanas se ve la incomunicación entre padres y madres e hijos, y la omnipresencia del móvil. ¿Le suena?

Mis hijos son ya mayores. Estamos en otro momento. Ambos se han independizado y, aunque hablo constantemente con ellos, ya no tengo la presión de atender a todas sus necesidades, esa demanda ha desaparecido y la conversación es otra. Tampoco tengo, en absoluto, la sensación de nido vacío. Y todo eso, unido, ha contribuido a esa etapa mía de calma.

Aparte del móvil, hay un libro sobre la mesa. ¿Qué está leyendo?

El amor, de Theodor Kallifatides, un griego que se va a vivir a Suecia, pero nunca olvida su origen. Te encantaría. Siempre llevo un libro encima porque me encanta leer y también para mirar menos el móvil, que es una trampa en la que podemos caer todos. Hay veces que me pongo con Instagram y, cuando me doy cuenta, llevo una hora. Tengo que parar eso. Porque, además, casi todo es mentira. Ahora no hay pudor en mostrar lo que uno hace. Siempre he sido muy pudorosa con mi vida personal, y lo sigo siendo. Me han educado en que no hay que presumir, no está bien, porque hay gente que no lo puede hacer. La época en la que empecé a trabajar era la de los paparazzi, y te perseguían, te asaltaban, aunque fueras con tus hijos, y dejabas de ir a los sitios por no encontrártelos. Nunca lo he entendido.

¿Ya no la persiguen?

No, ya no me persigue nadie, y por eso también me he quitado la ansiedad.

¿Se ha vuelto invisible, habiendo sido una mujer tan mirada?

Un poco, lo cual agradezco infinitamente. Ahora puedo ir a todas partes. Si alguien me reconoce, me sonríe, y me siento bien: esa sonrisa me la he ganado y estoy muy contenta.

¿Y la mirada masculina?

No lo echo en falta en absoluto. Es incómodo que te estén mirando. Yo, en ese sentido, estoy muy tranquila. No me hace ninguna falta que me miren, porque cuando era más joven sí sentía esa presión y me incomodaba mucho. Mira, otra carga que ya no tengo.

O sea, que está totalmente libre de cargas.

He cuidado mucho en mi vida. Y mucha de esa ansiedad viene por la necesidad de llegar a todo, a todas las personas que están a nuestro alrededor y que nos necesitan. Y luego, además, las mujeres tenemos que ser impecables en el trabajo, cuidar a nuestros padres y madres y a nuestros hijos, estar divinas y tener la casa estupenda por si viene alguien, aunque no venga. Pues mira, sí, me he quitado esa ansiedad: ahora me toca a mí.

En la película, su personaje es una mujer que no se cuida, ni por dentro ni por fuera. ¿Le costó encarnarla?

En eso no tengo absolutamente ningún problema. Me gusta que se vea la verdad. Es una mujer que arrastra un desgaste emocional grande, que sigue, a su pesar, en una relación que la hace feliz, que no se quiere demasiado a ella misma y todo eso se cuenta también desde la caracterización. No llevo máscaras ni corsés. Aunque, luego, a todas nos gusta vernos guapas en las fotos.

Hablando de imagen. ¿Qué hay detrás de su sempiterno flequillo?

La frente [ríe]. No soy mucho de cambiar, ya me cambian bastante en el trabajo: me transforman, me visten de otra, me cambian el peinado. Hay quien juega con el maquillaje, o los cortes de pelo, o la moda. Yo ni me maquillo. Digamos que soy la materia base para que me caractericen de otra. Y ese es mi juego.

¿En qué momento profesional diría que se encuentra?

Yo vivo de esto, es mi oficio. No podría retirarme, porque necesito ingresar. Disfruto mucho de mi tiempo, me encanta viajar, me tomaría un par de años sabáticos, pero volvería a trabajar por el gusto de trabajar. El cine, el teatro, la escena es una expresión necesaria que ha de reflejar el contexto en que vivimos, y eso me implica, me compete y es mi manera de expresarme en el mundo. Es algo vital para mí.

¿Cuándo empezó a ver en los ojos de sus compañeros el respeto que se les tiene a los clásicos?

Bueno, lo de clásica… Pues no hace tanto. Ese respeto viene muchas veces porque te han visto en entrevistas, o en películas, o les han contado cosas de ti, y eso lo notas enseguida y te pone incómoda porque la persona que tienes enfrente, con la que te estás intentando comunicar, no te ve a ti, sino a través de una venda. Pero una vez que se quita esa venda, esa mirada de respeto, cuando es de verdad, te da muchísima seguridad y alivia la inseguridad que tienes.

¿A estas alturas de las películas? Porque lleva unas cuantas.

Esa inseguridad permanece siempre. Yo llego al set y es mi casa, pero siempre tienes esa incredulidad de que esto te esté pasando a ti. Mira, el otro día, con Elena Sánchez, en Televisión Española, me dijo que llevaba 110 películas rodadas y no me lo creía: me sentí [José] Sacristán. ¿Yo he hecho todo eso? También te digo que veo hoy El perro del hortelano, de la que ya hace treinta años, y me miro con muchísima ternura: qué mona, qué bien dice el verso esa chica, ¿no?

World.title: Vamos a setas: seis rutas micológicas para el otoño, haya o no hongos
World.content:
El cambio climático ha retrasado un mes la temporada en España y los expertos no descartan que se alargue. En estos montes podremos saciar nuestro apetito de paisajes

Antes empezaba a tronar y a jarrear a finales de agosto y justo a los 21 días aparecían las setas en el monte. Así ocurría, por lo menos, en la sierra de Guadarrama, a caballo entre Madrid, Segovia y Ávila, donde el que esto escribe vive desde 1995. También antes el veranillo de San Miguel –29 de septiembre– y el de San Martín –11 de noviembre– eran unos pocos días de otoño en los que repuntaba el calor y se podía salir en manga corta a buscar setas, porque las había a patadas. Con el cambio climático, sin embargo, dejó de llover y de refrescar a finales de agosto y llegó el veroño, que comenzó siendo cosa de una o dos semanas y amenaza ya con suplantar al verdadero otoño, para desesperación de los seteros, a los que cada vez nos cuesta más entender y encontrar algo en este mundo al revés.

Pero veamos la botella –y la cesta– medio llena. Quizá todo esté ocurriendo a deshora y solo haya que aguardar. Las lluvias que no cayeron este año en agosto lo han hecho en octubre y algunas setas han salido. Si llueve más en noviembre y las temperaturas se mantienen altas, ¿por qué no podría haber un brote tardío? En ese caso, los siguientes montes serán buenos para salir a buscarlas, pues la experiencia nos dice que en ellos no suelen faltar. Y si no las encontramos, allá penas: disfrutaremos de seis de las excursiones más agradables que pueden hacerse en noviembre en España, con la cesta vacía y en manga corta.

Más información Cómo evitar una intoxicación por setas y por qué no hay que fiarse de las aplicaciones del móvil

1. Las Burbonas del Gorbeia (Álava)

La hayas que pueblan las laderas de las Burbonas alavesas son magníficas, hasta el punto de que en otoño el caminante no puede dejar de mirarlas y fotografiarlas, aun sabiendo que en el suelo se esconden setas deliciosas.

José David Fernández, director del parque micológico de Gorbeialdea –que abarca la cuarta parte del parque natural del Gorbeia, el mayor y más setero del País Vasco–, cree que las setas van con un mes de retraso y que este año se dejarán ver hasta finales de noviembre “con permiso de las heladas”. Recomienda, como es lógico, sacar el preceptivo permiso –10 euros por persona y día– y participar en alguna de las rutas que él mismo guía todos los fines de semana y en las que se recolectan alrededor de 25 especies distintas.

Una buscadora de setas junto a una haya monumental en las Burbonas del Gorbeia. Andrés Campos

Los boletus aereus y los edulis son dos de los hongos más abundantes y apreciados. Y la ruta favorita de José David y de cualquiera de los seteros que frecuentamos el “corazón verde de Euskadi” es la que asciende desde la casa del parque de Sarria hasta la triple cima de las Burbonas y luego regresa al punto de partida siguiendo de cerca al saltarín río Baias. Subiendo y bajando de las Burbonas, además de setas, se ven hayas majestuosas de melena dorada, cobriza y roja que, por sí solas, justificarían recorrer este itinerario circular de 16 kilómetros y cinco horas de duración, seis si nos paramos a ver qué hay debajo de la hojarasca. Para no perderse, hay que seguir las indicaciones y el track de Wikiloc. Para reponer fuerzas después de la excursión, nada como el cocido de alubias y las habitaciones del Hotel Doña Lola, que ocupa un caserío de piedra del siglo XVI en Izarra.

Al día siguiente podemos ver la cascada de Gouiri –una de las más altas de España, de 105 metros– y comprar el queso de Idiazábal que los hermanos hermanos Basterra elaboran con la leche de un montón de ovejas latxas que pastan arrastrando sus largas guedejas al lado mismo del salto.

Si andamos un lunes por la zona y deseamos profundizar en su riqueza micológica, podemos acercarnos a la Sociedad Micológica Gorbeiako Bazterra, en Murgia, donde ese día hay un servicio gratuito de identificación. Su vicepresidente, Vicente Blasco, es categórico respecto al anómalo comportamiento de las setas este año, que han brotado muy tarde sin que apenas haya llovido en cinco meses: “Han salido por aburrimiento”.

Queseria de los Hermanos Basterra, en Goiuri. Andrés Campos

2. Castañar de los Ojestos (Cáceres)

El Castañar de los Ojestos, en la sierra cacereña de Gata, también es espectacular en esta época, cuando las hojas se vuelven amarillas y caedizas, pero lo de no fijarse en el suelo aquí es más complicado. Además de setas hay castañas, y eso ya es demasiada golosina para no prestar atención. En San Martín de Trevejo, uno de los pueblos más bonitos de España, arranca el sendero PR-CC 184, que atraviesa de abajo arriba este castañar, el más extenso de Extremadura.

A 2,5 kilómetros del inicio, como a una hora de paseo sosegado, se llega a la altura de los Abuelos, dos castaños enormes a los que se les calcula una edad de 600 años. Media hora después se cruza el río de la Vega, que con las lluvias otoñales forma unas buenas chorreras. Y en media más se alcanza el puerto de Santa Clara, donde acaba Cáceres y empieza Salamanca.

La bajada, que es por el mismo camino, toca hacerla –ahora sí– fijándose en el suelo, donde en noviembre suele haber níscalos, lenguas de vaca, parasoles, algún que otro boletus y las últimas castañas llovidas del cielo amarillo. En el restaurante Saboris de Sempris, en San Martín de Trevejo, los boletus edulis se sirven acompañados con unas tostas de torta del Casar. Otros dos comedores serranos donde no faltan en temporada los edulis son el gastrobar Los Portales, en Gata, y la taberna El Buen Avío de Trevejo.

Puesta de sol en el hotel Habitat Cigüeña Negra, en la sierra de Gata. Andrés Campos

El año que viene, porque ya es tarde para encontrarlas, vendremos a buscar la codiciada Amanita caesarea o huevo de rey. Para ello, lo más fácil y gratificante es alojarse a principios de otoño en el hotel Habitat Cigüeña Negra y salir a pasear con la cesta por la dehesa de encinas que lo rodea. Curiosamente, la especialidad del restaurante, que tiene una estrella verde Michelin por su cocina sostenible, no son las setas, sino la carne de Retwagyu, un cruce de vaca retinta extremeña y buey wagyu japonés que pace alrededor del hotel sin mostrar ningún interés por este bocado de césares. Aquí cada cual –los seteros, los clientes del asador y las vacas– van a lo suyo.

3. Sierra de Cebollera (La Rioja)

En la ermita de Lomos de Orios, en Villoslada de Cameros, un lagarto tallado en cuerno de vaca recuerda la historia que cuenta que en 1824, la Virgen salvó a un pastor de ser comido por uno gigantesco. Lino Martínez, que así se llamaba el pastor, lo había criado, hasta que éste que alcanzó un metro y medio de longitud. Un día, la criatura se abalanzó sobre su cuidador, el cual se libró in extremis de ser devorado al entrar corriendo en la ermita y cerrarse milagrosamente la puerta detrás de él, partiendo en dos al lagarto. Grandes como aquel animal y su ingratitud son los boletus edulis que se cogen hasta que empiezan a blanquear las cimas de la sierra riojana de Cebollera. Unos piensan que se llama así por la forma redondeada de sus montes y otros opinan que es por la abundancia que hay en ella de gamones blancos (Asphodelus albus), también llamados cebollanas, cebollinos, cebolletas de monte, cebollas de culebra, cebollas gamonitas, cebolleras moriscas o ceborrinchas.

Además de hermosos boletus, aquí las cestas se llenan de níscalos, parasoles, pardillas, negrillas, trompetas de la muerte y, entrado ya el invierno, pies azules. Algunas zonas de recolección pillan tan lejos que hay que acercarse en coche por pistas forestales de acceso restringido, pagando otro permiso además del que uno ya saca para ver si coge algo: seis euros en total. Para quien no quiere complicarse pidiendo ese otro permiso y metiéndose con el coche por vaya usted a saber qué caminos, existe un cómodo un cómodo sendero circular circular de algo menos de siete kilómetros –un par de horas a paso tranquilo– que lleva desde la misma ermita hasta las cascadas de Puente Ra, atravesando un hayedo precioso. No tiene pérdida: está marcado con trazos de pintura naranja y verde.

Su mayor aliciente, aparte de hallar setas, es ver los saltos de hasta diez metros que pega el arroyo de Puente Ra, afluente del río Iregua, el principal del valle. El premio de consolación para los que acaban con la cesta vacía es comerse unas pochas con boletus o un guiso de jabalí con hongos confitados y salsa de arándanos en el restaurante Corona, en Ortigosa de Cameros. Al lado hay un alojamiento rural que se llama como lo que se acaba de admirar paseando valle arriba: Cascadas de Puente Ra.

Cascadas de Puente Ra, en sierra de Cebollera. Andrés Campos

4. Barranco de la Barbulla y Muela de Cortes (Valencia)

Donde ha llovido bastante en lo que va de otoño es en las montañas del interior de Valencia, que ahora están a tope de rebollones –como allí llaman a los níscalos–, de lenguas de vaca y de seteros con la navaja afilada y el brillo del ansia viva en la mirada. El Rincón de Ademuz y la comarca de los Serranos o del Alto Turia –cuya capital, Chelva, exploramos a fondo recientemente– son dos lugares famosos por su riqueza micológica.

Quien busque otras zonas menos trilladas y otras atracciones, aparte de esa, hará bien en acercarse a Cortes de Pallás. A la entrada de este recóndito pueblo, plantado en un barranco lateral del encañonado río Júcar y al pie de la alta y acantilada Muela de Cortes, un cartel de la oficina de turismo anuncia: “Un mundo aparte”. Y es verdad: más apartado no puede estar. Aquí el coche sirve ya para poco: toca echarse a caminar monte arriba, explorando los manantiales, los saltos de agua, los canales de riego y las balsas que convirtieron el barranco de la Barbulla en uno de los mayores paraísos hortícolas de los moriscos.

Recorriendo la llamada ruta de las Cascadas, veremos en un par de horas media docena de ellas. La mayor de todas, la de El Corbinet, resbala por una cornisa rocosa de ocho metros de altura y cae en una charca amplia, verde y sombría, idónea para comer –hay mesas alrededor– las tortas de sal o de embutido que se compraron en Ca’ la Conchin, frente a la oficina de turismo.

Vista desde el castillo Chirel, al que se llega por un sencillo sendero de tres kilómetros (ida y vuelta). Andrés Campos

Un camino más largo y esforzado, de siete kilómetros y casi cinco horas con paradas contemplativas, es la senda Cavanilles, que sube zigzagueando como una serpiente de escalera a la Muela de Cortes, donde 4.000 de los muchos moriscos que vivían en la comarca se refugiaron en el otoño de 1609 porque no querían ser expulsados de España ni abjurar de su fe.

Otro más sencillo, de solo tres kilómetros –ida y vuelta–, es el que lleva al castillo de Chirel, que fue el cuartel general de las tropas gubernamentales cuando los moriscos se rebelaron e hicieron fuertes en la Muela de Cortes. Desde la ruinosa fortaleza, a 300 metros sobre el Júcar, se ven como desde un helicóptero las aguas color turquesa del río y los barcos que navegan por ellas llenos de pensionistas del balneario de Cofrentes.

Si haciendo estas rutas no encontramos algún rebollón o alguna llanega negra –la seta mocosa típica de estos bosques de pino carrasco sobre rocas calizas, que suele alargar la temporada hasta enero–, solo nos queda subir en coche a la Muela de Cortes y parar por el camino en algún pinar prometedor. Donde haya vehículos en el arcén, habrá setas.

05 Sierra de Aracena (Huelva)

Esta sierra del norte de Huelva, fronteriza con Portugal, Badajoz y Sevilla, es Eldorado andaluz de las setas, donde cualquiera que haya estado en otoño habrá visto por doquier camiones frigoríficos cargando toneladas de ellas para llevarlas al extranjero. Aun así, el tiempo está tan loco, tan trastocado, que “este octubre no se ha cogido ni una”. Jorge Jaímez, gerente y guía de Lynxaia, confía en las lluvias de noviembre: “A finales de mes, casi dos más tarde de lo habitual, esperamos estar haciendo rutas micológicas”. Como otras 26 empresas de la sierra, Lynxaia participa en Soy Ecoturista, una iniciativa de la Asociación de Ecoturismo en España para proponer experiencias que contribuyan a la conservación de los espacios naturales y al desarrollo local.

Senderista en Alajar, municipio de la sierra de Aracena. Andrés Campos

Las rutas son sumamente respetuosas con el entorno y con los vecinos, a los cuales se pide permiso para hacerlas, no solo por cortesía, sino porque casi todo el monte en la sierra de Aracena es privado. Aunque tarde, este año volverán a salir las tanas (Amanita caesarea) y los hongos negros (Boletus aereus) entre los castaños de Fuenteheridos, Galaroza, Alájar o Castaño del Robledo y en las dehesas que los rodean, y los boletus edulis a alturas superiores a 600 metros.

Más adelante aún lo harán los níscalos en los pinares y los rebozuelos en los castañares y alcornocales más húmedos. El que no volverá a abrir sus puertas –no con Luismi López y Adela Ortiz al frente, por lo menos– es el restaurante Los Arrieros, en Linares de la Sierra, que era un templo de la cocina del terruño y de las setas en particular. Pero en la sierra sigue habiendo dos establecimientos donde las preparan con cariño en otoño: Peña de Arias Montano, en Alájar, y Montecruz, en Aracena. Un comercio de referencia para comprarlas frescas es Sirlache, en la calle Constitución, 1. Y un hotel idóneo para quienes estamos enganchados a ellas es Finca La Fronda. No hace falta ni salir de él para buscarlas: solo pasear por el jardín.

Cogiendo setas en el Pinar de Valsaín. Andrés Campos

6. Pinar de Valsaín (Segovia)

En la sierra de Guadarrama, este octubre ha sido flojo micológicamente, con temperaturas altísimas y la humedad justa para que los seteros locales cogiéramos seis o siete boletus edulis y un puñado de níscalos cada uno. Parasoles (Macrolepiota procera) hay muchos, pero pocos los recolectamos, aun sabiendo que, cortados sus sombreros en cuartos, empanados junto a una loncha de jamón serrano y fritos en aceite de oliva, están muy ricos.

Un lugar donde cabe esperar que con algo más de lluvia se anime la cosa a mediados o finales de noviembre es el pinar de Valsaín, en la vertiente segoviana del puerto de Navacerrada. Podemos dejar el coche en el aparcamiento de más de 30 plazas que hay junto a la fuente de la Canaleja y el puente de la Cantina, al pie de las Siete Revueltas –kilómetro 17 de la carretera CL-601.

La bicicleta es una excelente manera de explorar el pinar de Valsaín. Andrés Campos

Allí mismo veremos un portillo con un cartel que dice “acotado de setas” –habremos pedido permiso antes, claro– y un sendero que se adentra en este magnífico bosque de pino silvestre, ligado a la corona desde tiempos de Carlos III. Subiendo siempre a corta distancia del arroyo del Puerto del Paular, que baja del puerto de Cotos, o de su afluente de las Pintadas, siempre encontraremos veneros y tollas donde, por seco y mustio que esté el resto del pinar, crecen los níscalos. Noviembre es su mejor mes y también el de las capuchinas.

Otra excelente manera de explorar este pinar es en bici, siguiendo la pista forestal asfaltada que lo rodea por completo. Es una vuelta de 35 kilómetros, con salida y llegada en la Granja de San Ildefonso, que se puede hacer en unas tres o cuatro horas, depende del tiempo que se invierta en examinar las muchas zonas húmedas que se atraviesan. Tampoco es mala idea dejar de registrar el bosque a mediodía y bajar al real sitio a probar los famosos buñuelos de setas con foie del restaurante La Fundición.

World.title: Jetten cabinet survives crisis talks for now, deadlock continues
World.content:
The Dutch cabinet’s crisis talks ended in deadlock on Friday after more than seven hours, and the coalition will survive for the time being, though talks will continue over the weekend.

Prime minister Rob Jetten met right-wing liberal VVD leader Dilan Yesilgöz and Christian Democrat CDA deputy prime minister Bart van den Brink on Friday morning, following Thursday night’s vote on the tax plan, which the VVD says broke the coalition agreement.

Yesilgöz, speaking at a press conference after the talks, said the political situation cannot continue as things stand. She described the current minority coalition as a “failed experiment” and said that a government collapse was a “possible solution”, while acknowledging no one wants to plunge the country into another election.

Jetten, who spoke before her, said that “things have not gone well recently, and that is affecting mutual relations”. “That can and must be better: substantively, politically, and personally.”

While the cabinet has not yet collapsed, VVD sources told the Telegraaf that no progress had been made and the impasse continues.

If the talks had ended on Friday, “it could have gone wrong”, Jetten said.

World.title: Health insurance premiums will rise next year
World.content:

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Health insurance companies are set to increase premiums in 2027, pushing up the cost of a basic package up by as much as €17 a month.

Companies were required to announce the cost of their premiums by midnight on Thursday and the cost will rise sharply across the board next year.

Insurer DSW, traditionally the first to publish its rates, announced in October that the price for its premium will go up by €14.75 a month.

The most popular basic insurance at Zilveren Kruis is rising by €5.70 euros to €164.95 euros, while at CZ the basic insurance will soon cost €177.25, an increase of more than €17 compared to last year.

Last year, premiums were able to remain virtually unchanged due to more money in the health insurance fund.

Health insurance companies attribute the rise to the aging population, which has more health care needs, as well as the increase in wages for healthcare employees and gas prices.

World.title: Two arrested for Prinsjesdag train sabotage
World.content:
Police have arrested two people in connection with the sabotage on the railway during Prinsjesdag, the public prosecution service (OM) announced on Friday.

A 49-year-old man and a 41-year-old woman from Drenthe were arrested on Thursday. According to the OM, the pair remain suspects but there was not enough evidence to keep them in custody.

Train services across the country were disrupted in September in what network operators described an act of coordinated sabotage. The attacks took place during Prinsjesdag, the state opening of parliament in The Hague and one of the biggest days in the Dutch political calendar.

Steel pipes were attached to the tracks at multiple locations across the country, disrupting rail service nationwide.

It is not yet known who was behind the attacks. On the same day, tractor tires, hay bales, and pallets were lit on fire at various locations. Some of those incidents were tied to farmer activists.

The Farmers Defence Force, responsible for recent motorway disruptions, said it was not responsible but that “wild actions” by individual farmers had been expected on budget day.

The two suspects are the first to be arrested in the case.

World.title: The Hague is the tile “whipping” champion
World.content:
No city has done more to whip their gardens into shape than The Hague, which took home the Golden Tile prize for removing the most paving stones from its gardens, totalling a record 507,000 citywide, breaking the previous record by nearly 50,000.

The NK Tegelwippen, or Dutch National Tile Removal Championship, pits councils against one another to see who can free up the most green space.

According to the organisation, this makes neighbourhoods more attractive, combats flood and rising temperatures and gives children more areas for play.

“It is fantastic that we are still breaking records. It shows that perseverance pays off and that residents consider greenery in the city increasingly important,” Joris Wijsmuller, the director of Duurzaam Den Haag, said in a statement.

Some 150,000 tiles were taken out by residents, schools, sports clubs, and companies participated in the event, according to the council. The remainder were removed by the city in public spaces.

The Hague also won the title in 2021 and 2022.

World.title: Three’s a crowd: Will Jetten’s tax bill kill the cabinet?
World.content:
There is an old medical joke about a surgeon who declares: “The operation was a complete success, but the patient died.”

After months of chaotic, gruelling negotiations, Rob Jetten achieved a majority in parliament for his tax bill on Thursday night, but his coalition is in tatters. The right-wing liberal VVD were so incensed by the deal the other two partners, Jetten’s D66 and the Christian Democrats (CDA), struck with the left-wing Pro that they voted against the entire plan, which had been extensively drafted and redrafted by the VVD finance minister, Eelco Heinen.

The party’s leader, Dilan Yesilgöz, denounced it as “a bad deal for the Netherlands” and demanded a “fundamental reset” of the centre-right coalition. Essentially, she wanted the prime minister to switch his cabinet off and switch it on again.

The millionaires’ tax knife twist

Strikingly, the amendment that D66, CDA and Pro agreed on Wednesday afternoon was a milder version of one that the VVD had seemed willing to tolerate earlier in the week. Pro wanted to raise an extra €1.5 billion in wealth taxes in order to pay for an income tax cut for the lowest earners. D66 and CDA had negotiated the amount down to €1 billion and built in counterbalancing measures to protect people with modest savings – at an earlier stage one of the key concerns for the VVD. Its impact, even on the private investors it was aimed at, was marginal.

But none of that mattered. For the VVD, the deal was unacceptable because it crossed a red line – raising taxes on successful, hard-working entrepreneurs – and it was drawn up behind their backs between their coalition partners and Pro.

Jesse Klaver, the leader of Pro, then twisted the knife by describing the measure as a “millionaires’ tax”, a phrase that went down like cold gravel in the throats of not just the VVD, but CDA leader Henri Bontenbal.

The seeds of the crisis were sown around 10 days earlier, as a reconstruction in AD.nl has found, when the coalition parties agreed to enter what commentators immediately called an “open marriage”. After months of abortive attempts to strike a collective deal with a divided opposition that balanced the interests of left and right, the three parties would try to form separate majorities for their own priorities. It would allow D66 and CDA to pair up with Pro and Volt while the VVD could court the right-wing opposition block of JA21, the farmers’ party BBB and the orthodox Protestant SGP. As a last resort, they could even vote on opposite sides when the amendments were tabled in parliament, if it meant that the tax bill and the coalition survived.

Unagreed terms

The problem was, none of the parties had agreed on the terms of the open marriage. And what the VVD hadn’t reckoned with was that D66 and CDA would go all the way with Pro and produce an amendment that seemed calculated to hurt them. D66 and CDA protested that they had kept their partners informed throughout the negotiations and even invited them to the table. But the VVD’s whole reason for joining the coalition in the first place was to keep the left-wing Pro out of power, as D66 and CDA knew all too well.

For Yesilgöz, the amendment represented the very outcome that she had entered the partnership to avoid, and Klaver’s press conference and Instagram reel to celebrate the millionaires’ tax were simply rubbing salt into the wound. To extend the analogy, it was like agreeing to an arranged marriage only to see your partner immediately phone up the ex-girlfriend he told you was no threat and take her for dinner at the Ritz.

None of this should obscure the extent to which the VVD engineered their own downfall. The minority cabinet was built on unstable foundations because the VVD wanted to shut out the opposition party that would have the strongest hand in the upcoming negotiations. When the coalition agreement was published, they took out billboards to parade their achievements, such as retaining mortgage interest tax relief.

The final betrayal

From the outset the VVD have focused more on defending their red lines within the coalition than finding the opposition votes they need to pass their legislation. It allowed Pro to exploit the deadlock to torpedo key VVD policies such as the €6.5 billion of welfare cuts. The budget amendment was the final betrayal for the VVD, but it was also the inevitable outcome of a process in which the party had refused to build any kind of constructive relationship with Pro, while D66 and CDA had reached out to unlikely partners such as Gidi Markuszower’s far-right DNA. And when the VVD decided to reject its own budget deal, its partners delivered a final humiliation by salvaging it with the support of a pair of fringe parties on the left: Denk and the animal rights party PvdD.

What happens next is unclear. The VVD, stung by what they see as a deep betrayal, want the coalition to renew its vows. Jetten prefers to talk about a “restart”, the language usually used for businesses that have called in the receivers. Yesilgöz almost goaded the other parties to try their luck with Pro in a new combination, but that would leave the cabinet still nine votes short of a majority and a hostile opposition dominated by the right. Jesse Klaver may well have overplayed his hand with his “pick me” posts on social media.

But new elections are an equally risky option for three parties whose standing in the opinion polls has been further damaged by the tax plan saga. And if the coalition survives in its current form, it will be as a marriage of inconvenience. Not for the first time, politics and matrimony have turned out to be a toxic mix.
