World.title: New Croatian Tourism Law: Different Deadlines for Landlords to Re-Categorise Apartments
World.content:
November the 14th, 2026 – A new Croatian tourism law could mean that private landlords end up having different deadlines to re-categorise their apartments. Some will get five years, others will be given ten.

The mandatory re-categorisation of apartments every ten years, registration numbers for advertising accommodation via online platforms, stricter inspection supervision and higher penalties for illegal operations are some of the changes envisaged by the final proposal of the new Hospitality Activity Act, which the Croatian Parliament discussed on Thursday. Poslovni reports that although the government is announcing more order on the tourist market and an increase in the quality of service, small landlords are warning of additional obligations and uncertainty about future operating conditions.

State Secretary at the Ministry of Tourism and Sport Monika Udovičić, president of the association Spasimo male obiteljske iznajmljivače (SMOi) Vedran Tomić, and president of the Guild of Hospitality and Tourism Workers of the Croatian Chamber of Trades and Crafts Hrvoje Margan all spoke about the new rules.

different deadlines for different landlords

According to the final proposal of the law, rooms, apartments and holiday homes will in future have to undergo re-categorisation every ten years. However, different transitional deadlines are envisaged for existing landlords, depending on when their approval decision was issued. According to Article 80 of the final proposal of the law, landlords whose decision was issued by the 31st of December 2015 will have to align their operations and obtain a new decision within five years of the entry into force of the relevant ordinance.

For those whose decision was issued as of the 1st of January 2016, a deadline of ten years from the entry into force of the ordinance is envisaged. This means that the deadlines do not automatically start running from the beginning of 2027, but from the day the new ordinance defining the conditions enters into force. After alignment, periodic checks will follow every ten years, which the competent administrative bodies will carry out ex officio. If it is established that the facility no longer meets the prescribed conditions, its type or category may be changed, and in certain cases the decision may be revoked.

the new rules aren’t “anti-landlord”, the powers that be claim

It was explained that hotels and campsites have so far undergone re-categorisation every four years, while the new law extends that period to five years. For small landlords, re-categorisation every ten years is envisaged. The reason for introducing the new checks, according to her, is the fact that there are facilities on the market that were categorised more than 20 years ago and whose compliance with standards has not been re-checked since then.

“This new rule isn’t directed against landlords,” the State Secretary said. She added that those who meet the prescribed conditions need not fear losing their decision. She also emphasised that the goal of the new ordinances is not to prevent existing landlords from operating, but to align standards with modern requirements.

possible consequences…

SMOi president Vedran Tomić questions the need for new categorisation, considering that online platforms and guest reviews have already become an important indicator of accommodation quality. He referred to an analysis of more than 1.6 million reviews according to which, he claims, Croatian private accommodation was rated better than hotel accommodation. Tomić believes that the entire reform is aimed at reducing the share of private accommodation and increasing hotel capacities.

Udovičić rejects such claims and stresses that the Ministry wants to protect family accommodation, but also to distinguish landlords for whom this is a traditional activity from pure rentierism, especially in residential buildings. According to her, Croatia has been receiving approximately ten thousand new beds in private accommodation year after year, while demand has not grown at the same pace, which has also affected occupancy rates.

The Ministry is therefore seeking to further encourage the quality and recognisability of family accommodation. Tomić, however, believes that the market, and not the state, should decide on the further growth of accommodation capacities.

a new rule from may the 1st, 2027

Another important change concerns all landlords who advertise their accommodation units via online platforms for short-term rental. Each such unit will have to have a unique registration number that will be submitted to the platform and displayed in the . Udovičić announced that the issuance of this number will be free of charge, and the procedure digital, via a system available through e-Citizens. According to the final proposal of the law, the provisions on registration numbers and data exchange with platforms should start to apply on the 1st of May 2027. The goal is to link accommodation data with the competent authorities and more effectively suppress unregistered renting. Unlike the registration numbers, most of the other provisions of the new law, if adopted in the proposed form, should enter into force on the 1st of January 2027.

support for more transparency and digitalisation

Hrvoje Margan, president of the Guild of Hospitality and Tourism Workers of the Croatian Chamber of Trades and Crafts, welcomed the adoption of the new law and the announced digitalisation of administrative procedures. Nevertheless, he warned that it is necessary to carefully regulate the minimum technical conditions so that the new ordinances do not become an additional administrative burden for hospitality operators. “We don’t want the ordinances to become a cleansing mechanism for hospitality operators,” he said. Udovičić replied that neither the law nor the future ordinances are conceived as a way of abolishing existing decisions, but as an instrument for modernising the system and raising quality.

The final proposal of the new Hospitality Activity Act has passed parliamentary debate, but still has to be voted on. Until its adoption and the entry into force of the new ordinances, landlords continue to operate according to the current regulations.

World.title: Continental Croatian Tourism up 60%, Million-Euro Incentives in 2027
World.content:
November the 14th, 2026 – Continental Croatian tourism is up by 60%, with new million-euro incentives coming in 2027 aimed at less developed inland regions.

The Croatian National Tourist Board recently launched a new cycle of public tenders for 2027, focused on the development of continental and less developed tourist regions and the promotion of events. Zrinka Gabelica Toplek reports for Poslovni that the decision to announce the tenders was made by the HTZ Tourism Council at its 9th session, and funding is secured through dedicated resources from the Fund for Touristically Underdeveloped Areas and the Mainland and the Fund for Associated Tourist Boards.

big increases for continental croatia

The adopted Open Call for Expressions of Interest aims at cooperation with organisers of “TOP events” of national significance and other events in the segments of eno-gastronomy, nautical tourism, culture, sport, entertainment, MICE and health tourism. In addition, tenders have been announced for regional tourist boards in underdeveloped areas and for projects of associated tourist boards.

“By announcing new tenders for 2027 through the HTZ funds, we are continuing with concrete measures by which we encourage more balanced development of Croatian tourism, while at the same time continuing cooperation with organisers of events and top events that contribute to the attractiveness of our destinations and the attraction of guests throughout the year,” said Minister of Tourism and Sport Tonči Glavina. He emphasised that since 2021, 51.6 million euros have been secured from these funds for more than 2,000 projects.

“The results are also visible in tourist traffic, which in the continental counties has increased by 60 percent in arrivals and 58 percent in overnight stays over the past ten years, while according to the latest TOMAS research, the average daily expenditure of tourists in continental Croatia has increased by 21 percent compared to 2022.

These are indicators of the growing importance of continental tourism in the overall development of Croatian tourism, and our goal is to continue this positive trend, further strengthen the tourist offer and enable local communities across Croatia to feel the benefits of tourism even more strongly,” Glavina emphasised.

encouraging cooperation

HTZ director Kristjan Staničić stressed that with these calls they want to further encourage the development of quality events that have the potential to become a reason for the arrival of domestic and foreign guests.

“We place special emphasis on touristically underdeveloped areas and the mainland, where events can play an exceptionally important role in creating the recognisability of destinations, activating local potentials and a more even distribution of tourist traffic,” Staničić said, adding that their goal is to support events that, through quality, content and organisation, can position themselves at the national level, create additional value for the destination and encourage cooperation between tourist boards, local stakeholders and the economy.

World.title: Zagreb is Finally Getting A New Tram Line
World.content:
November the 14th, 2026 – The City of Zagreb will finally get a brand new tram line, after over six months of “combing through” all of the submitted bids.

The powers that be in the City of Zagreb have once again selected GIP Pionir as the winner of the tender issued back at the beginning of July. Over two whole years after it was announced, the tender for works on the tram line along Heinzelova and Radnička streets can now proceed. Poslovni reports that the State Commission for the Control of Public Procurement Procedures (DKOM) rejected the appeals of two companies that participated in the public procurement procedure estimated at 48 million euros, so the selection of the contractor can finally be completed and preparations for the start of works can begin soon.

This finally brings to an end the long-running complication surrounding one of the capital projects that the City of Zagreb announced back in 2023 and officially launched in November 2024. The first tender for the contractor of works on 3.7 kilometres of new tram track was announced at the end of 2024, but as the bids received significantly exceeded the estimated amount of 48 million euros (excluding VAT, as with other amounts in the text), the City cancelled the tender and announced a new one in May 2025. The value of the project remained the same, and by July four bids had been received.

After a two-month evaluation, the job was awarded to GIP Pionir, and then the problems began. A consortium of bidders led by the company Texo Molior, which also participated in the tender, decided to lodge an appeal, and the State Commission for the Control of Public Procurement Procedures (DKOM) upheld that appeal in January this year. The Commission ordered the City of Zagreb, as the contracting authority, to go through all the bids again and decide on the best one, which they did this summer. This brings us to the new problem.

As can be seen on the Electronic Public Procurement Noticeboard (EOJN), the company had to send several explanations and supplements to its bid over the past six months. A few days later, however, another appeal against the selection decision arrived at DKOM. The procedure was initiated by the same consortium of bidders as the previous time, namely the companies Texo Molior from Cavtat and Zagreb’s Tigra. The City waited three months for the Commission’s decision in the first appeal procedure, the re-selection of the contractor lasted more than six months, and it has now waited almost another four months for the new DKOM decision. The appeal was rejected and the procedure can now continue.

The project, incidentally, in addition to laying new kilometres of track, also includes the reconstruction and protection of 1.4 kilometres of water supply infrastructure along Heinzelova Street and Radnička Road, as well as the reconstruction of sewer collectors built between 1920 and 1950. Only after these works are completed will it be possible, as the City of Zagreb previously explained, to start work on the new line with a total of nine tram stops.

World.title: Estonia opens 4th honorary consulate in Greece
World.content:
Estonia opened its first honorary consulate on Rhodes last week, allowing Estonians visiting the Greek island to receive assistance locally if needed.

Kerli Veski, undersecretary for legal and consular affairs at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, opened the consulate on the Greek island of Rhodes on November 12.

Stergos Leventis has been appointed honorary consul.

"His work will help raise awareness of Estonia, strengthen cultural and economic ties between our countries and assist Estonians who need help while travelling. We are very grateful to him for his willingness and commitment to representing Estonia," Veski said at the opening ceremony.

She stressed the good ties between the two countries, which are both members of the European Union and NATO. One practical example of cooperation is the mutual recognition of e-prescriptions, which makes travelling easier for people from both countries.

Greece is a popular travel destination among Estonians. In 2025, 33,600 Estonians travelled to Greece, while 17,500 Greeks visited Estonia.

The honorary consulate on Rhodes is Estonia's fourth in Greece, alongside those in Thessaloniki, Patras and Agios Nikolaos on the island of Crete.

World.title: Estonian women's basketball team scores victory against North Macedonia
World.content:
The Estonian women's national basketball team won its first victory since 2024 on Saturday in the opening round of the EuroBasket 2029 pre-qualifiers.

The match took place in Stip, North Macedonia, and saw the Estonians win 86-51 against the home team.

This was the Estonian women's national basketball team's first victory since November 2024, when it defeated Denmark 66-58 at home in the European Championship qualifiers.

For head coach Toomas Annuk, this was his seventh game in charge of the women's national team and his first victory.

You can watch the match here.

On Tuesday, November 17, Estonia will face Romania, which defeated North Macedonia 72-53 in Bucharest. The game will take place at the Nord Sports Hall in Tallinn and begin at 5.30 p.m.

World.title: Pavel Talankin: How a cage of Putinist propaganda was built on top of the Soviet cage in schools
World.content:
Teacher Pavel Talankin from the small Ural town of Karabash jokes that he has become the first film director in the world whose films have a 100 percent Oscar success rate. Admittedly, he has made only one film so far, the documentary "Mr. Nobody Against Putin" (2025). Talankin came to Tallinn to screen the film at Artis cinema and speak with viewers afterward. While the audience watched the movie, he reluctantly gave an interview to ERR.

The film shows how Russian schools changed after Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, how state propaganda entered classrooms, and how militaristic events and lessons such as "Conversations about important things" became commonplace. It all unfolds through the example of an ordinary school in the small Ural town of Karabash, where the film's author worked as a teacher.

Before winning this year's Academy Award for Best Documentary Feature, the film had already received several awards at international film festivals, as well as a BAFTA.

ERR: You left Russia in 2024, so you have now spent two years as an émigré. Have you gotten used to your new life?

Pavel Talankin: The easiest thing would be to say "in exile." I do not really like it when people say "in exile." Am I an emigrant? Yes, a forced emigrant. There is no ready-made formula for getting used to it. Everyone adapts in their own way. In some respects it has been easier for me because I was not disconnected from the process of making the film (which was edited in Denmark -A.A.), nor from the work that followed its release. We travel to festivals, speak at lectures and present the film. So I have remained busy.

At the moment, it seems your whole life revolves around this film. You already have all the awards, even an Oscar. What comes next? A Nobel Prize?

Yes! That is what I will work on now!

In what field?

Physics. So that everyone back at school completely loses their minds.

By the way, what subject does the film's main antagonist, teacher Abdulmanov, teach?

History and civics. And physics too, because there are not enough teachers. There was a year when he taught physics to students.

What grade did you get in physics?

I got a C.

And yet your goal is the Nobel Prize?

Why not? Einstein got a C too.

But right now your life revolves around the film. You have the fame of an Oscar winner. What happens when that fame fades? Are you afraid of that?

No, there is no fear. Maybe it only looks that way from your perspective: Oscar, BAFTA, Sundance! I do not see myself that way. I am the same person I was before. I understand that if I start putting myself on some pedestal now, it will hurt when I eventually fall back into ordinary life. So I never really left ordinary life. It feels as though we are speaking two different languages. You say Oscar, BAFTA, fame. I sit here thinking: who are you talking about?

Autor/allikas: Siim Lõvi / ERR

At the beginning of the war, Ukrainian documentaries dominated the spotlight. Mstyslav Chernov's "20 Days in Mariupol" won an Oscar in 2024. Two years later, the Academy chose a film about the other side of the conflict. Why do you think that happened?

That is really a question for the members of the Academy. I do not know. They are the ones who vote. It is probably better to ask them.

How does a film even end up at the Oscars? What has to happen?

First, we took part in various film festivals. Then we submitted Oscar applications. There were two submissions. One was for Best International Feature on behalf of Denmark, since the film is a Danish-Czech production. Their system works similarly to the Oscars. They choose among three films, and eventually selected "Mr. Nobody Against Putin." The second submission was in the documentary category. Then the process unfolds in stages. First, members of the documentary branch watch the films and vote. Then they vote again. Then again. In the final stage, everyone votes.

So for the first three rounds only documentary filmmakers vote?

Exactly. Long list, short list, nominations. Then all Academy members watch the nominated films.

Do you still keep in touch with Karabash and your former students? In one interview you said the graduates featured in the film wrote your speeches for award ceremonies.

They write my speeches.

What do you mean?

Well, when you win an Oscar you have to go on stage and say something. That little statement is your speech.

But that is only a minute, maybe less.

A minute? I wrote to my students and said: "Listen, if we actually get called up, if we actually win, what would you want to say?"

They sent me an enormous wall of text with everything they wanted to share. They got together, wrote a speech and sent it to me.

Then we were sitting at the Oscars, and our interpreter Robin asked me: "If you get called up, what are you going to say? I am nervous because not all words translate directly. You have to understand the context." I told her I would read what the students wrote. She said: "Show me, so I know how to translate it."

I showed it to her, and she said: "Have you completely lost your mind?"

In the documentary category, you only get 45 seconds. Since I share the time with David, the film's producer David Borenstein, I am left with about 20 seconds. Since I have an interpreter, that time is cut in half again. So I had about 10 seconds.

We had to compress everything the students wrote while preserving the meaning.

Did any of your students watch the ceremony?

Of course. All of them did.

And what did they say afterward?

They congratulated me.

None of them felt you had put them in danger with the film? I mean the students and teachers who appear on screen.

No. They have not suffered because of it, and they are not angry with me.

What about the teachers? When I watched the film, I found the students likable, but the teachers...

Well, the history teacher Abdulmanov gave an interview to Andrey Malakhov (well-known Russian TV presenter – ed.), where he said he liked how he was portrayed. He said I made him look even more patriotic and even more devoted to Russia...

...than he actually is?

Apparently. So he is delighted. What happened in Karabash is a genuine phenomenon. People there say bad things about me, but not about the film.

Pavel Talankin in Tallinn. Source: Siim Lõvi / ERR

Have many people in Karabash seen it?

Everyone!

That is strange. The students like it, the people of Karabash like it, audiences here like it, teacher Abdulmanov likes it, yet Putin's government labeled Pavel Talankin a foreign agent. Why do you think that is?

You should ask him!

Oh, by the way, you just got a WhatsApp message.

And who is writing?

Some Maria Zakharova...

That is the Telegram channel of Maria Zakharova, the official spokesperson of the Russian Foreign Ministry. I have to follow it for work. So, back to Putin?

Look, a lot of things ordinary people like are things the president of the Russian Federation does not like. People generally like living according to the law. He does not. People generally value human life and health. He does not. People generally respect the territorial integrity of neighboring countries and do not spend their time thinking about war. He does not. He is a deeply disturbed person. Only God knows what he likes and dislikes.

After receiving the Oscar, you had the statuette blessed in a church in Paris by the well-known Russian priest Alexey Uminsky. Why?

We will come back to Uminsky later. I had it blessed by someone who did not support Russia's war crimes, who did not support the invasion of Ukraine, who was expelled from the Russian Orthodox Church and forced to leave Russia.

That answers why you chose him. But why bless the Oscar at all?

In the film, Putin quotes a phrase that is not actually his: "Wars are won not by generals but by schoolteachers." The full quote is: "Wars are won not by generals but by schoolteachers and priests." When you hold that Oscar in your hands, you immediately understand that there are schoolteachers and priests who oppose the war. And that means he will never win this war. That is all.

So you believe teacher Talankin and priest Uminsky are stronger than Putin?

Yes. I do.

The film covers the first two years of the war and shows how the propaganda machine gathered momentum. I was born in 1971, attended a Soviet school and was a Pioneer. We had our own versions of "Conversations about important things" and all that patriotic education, but by then nobody really believed in it anymore. Do children today believe what they are told, especially by the film's main antagonist, Abdulmanov?

Listen, adults believe it. Grown adults believe it. People with multiple university degrees and doctoral degrees believe it. So of course children can. The historian and writer Edward Radzinsky once quoted a phrase attributed to Stalin. I do not know whether Stalin actually said it: "After my death, garbage will be piled on my grave, but the ruthless wind of history will sweep it away." Putin is that ruthless wind of history right now. Because when these schoolchildren grow up, they may say: "Actually, things were better under Putin." And that is the most frightening thing that could happen.

This film will continue to be watched and shown. It is not a one-time documentary product. After we won the BAFTA, a well-known educator said something remarkable: "At first, it becomes routine. Nobody wants to do it, neither the teachers nor the children. Then it becomes culture, part of everyday life, like waking up and having coffee. And then it becomes a cage from which there is no escape."

This film shows how quickly teachers stepped into that cage once again.

There was already a Soviet cage, and no one ever seriously examined what had happened. No one said: "Friends, you were all indoctrinated." Nobody crushed that cage with a tank. Nobody flattened it with a steamroller. Nobody dissolved it with acid. Instead, another cage simply grew on top of it, the cage of Putinist propaganda.

People's minds are a complete mess, and getting them out of that cage will have to be done one person at a time. People do not like admitting they have been deceived.

Autor/allikas: Siim Lõvi / ERR

But among your students, are there some who have not been indoctrinated? One wants to believe so...

There are. At least I hope there are. The effect is different for everyone. There is no universal recipe for avoiding it.

(A long pause.)

Some students support Putin and the war. Some do not. A great deal depends on the family. If parents tell their child: "Try not to listen too closely to what your teacher is saying. Look out the window. Draw something. Think about something pleasant," then the child develops a kind of immunity to war. You can see such children in the film.

When soldiers are displaying grenades, some children simply refuse to touch the weapons. Compare the number of children who were forced to sit through lectures by Wagner Group mercenaries with the much smaller number who stayed afterward to take photographs with them.

The film has also faced criticism. Some people have accused you of constantly creating an atmosphere of secrecy around your activities, yet you appear on camera so often that someone must have been filming you. Who was the cameraman?

Let's just say God helped.

You spend a lot of time meeting audiences. Do foreigners ask different questions than Russians?

The questions are different. To really understand the difference, you would have to travel with me to various countries. There have been so many questions that I cannot remember them all. But there is one notable distinction.

People from Russia, Ukraine and Belarus usually say, "Thank you for the film."

People from other countries usually say, "Congratulations on the film."

You have said you want to return to Russia. Why?

Because it is necessary.

Even if you do not want to, you will have to pack your bags and go back to Russia when the regime falls. We will need to dismantle both cages that people are trapped in now, the first one and the second one, and tell people that they were deceived. People do not like admitting they have been deceived, and they will have to be led out of those cages one by one.

It will be individual work. And there will be a great deal of it.

World.title: Political parties looking to reduce Riigikogu members' salaries
World.content:
Political parties are discussing MPs' salaries, with both the coalition and opposition looking to make cuts in the next Riigikogu after the 2027 election.

Since April 1, 2026, the monthly salary of a Riigikogu member has been €6,655.81. MPs can claim reimbursement for work-related expenses of up to 25 percent of their salary.

Isamaa Chairman Urmas Reinsalu said that in recent years, salary increases for other senior state officials have been relatively smaller in line with austerity policy. But "this has not been applied to parliament," he said.

At the moment, it is still possible to set MPs' salaries for the next composition of the Riigikogu, which will be elected in March 2027.

Reinsalu said Isamaa has drawn up legislation to make the change, and the proposal has two parts.

Urmas Reinsalu Source: Siim Lõvi / ERR

"The first part is to reduce MPs' base salaries by roughly 10 percent to restore the previous proportion with other senior state officials, which has now shifted out of balance," he explained.

"And also, when it comes to their salary increases, to move to a more gradual system, which the government proposed introducing for the coming years," the chairman added.

Reinsalu claimed this would lead to savings of around €10 million over four years. He said the issue has not yet been discussed with other political parties but hoped Isamaa's initiative would find support.

Reform: Subject already under discussion

Reform Party parliamentary group chair Õnne Pillak told ERR that Isamaa is pushing at an open door. The government is already in the process of amending the Salaries of Higher State Servants Act.

"The plan to similarly reduce the rate of salary increases for Riigikogu members has certainly been under discussion among us. The question is what that percentage should be. There are different alternatives, but we should first wait for the bill to reach the Riigikogu," she said.

Õnne Pillak. Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

Pillak said Reform supports the principle that Riigikogu members, like government ministers, should receive smaller salary increases.

"But for me, what matters is not who submitted the bill. What matters to me is that the necessary decision gets made. Isamaa also knew that this bill would be coming to the Riigikogu from the government. So we can make all the necessary decisions within the framework of that bill," Pillak added.

She said there is no competition between the submitted bills, but Isamaa's proposal is incomplete.

"If the government said several weeks ago that such a bill would be submitted to the Riigikogu, then it makes sense to decide everything within the framework of a single bill. Isamaa can also come and support it, and it is not ruled out that, if the solutions are similar in substance, Isamaa's bill could also be merged with it. There is no need to do the same thing through several different bills," Pillak added.

World.title: Shift changes at Tallinn hospitals may lead to staff shortages
World.content:
The decision by two Tallinn hospitals to abandon 24-hour shifts is unpopular with nurses and care workers. The Estonian Nurses Union said the new rules make it difficult to work additional shifts elsewhere.

West Tallinn Central Hospital (Lääne-Tallinna keskhaigla) and North Estonia Medical Center (PERH) will no longer allow care workers and nurses to work 24-hour shifts, citing patient safety.

PERH's director of nursing, Katre Zirel, said studies confirm that employees become tired after eight hours of very intensive work, and when shifts extend to 24 hours, mistakes occur.

One PERH care worker said what bothers her most is that the hospital is not interested in how the new shift schedule suits employees.

If she has to travel to work four or five times a week, it takes more time and money, the single mother writes. She is also upset that doctors can continue working 24-hour shifts.

Difficulties organizing family life

A midwife working at West Tallinn Central Hospital said she is being forced to look for a new job because it is difficult to manage shorter shifts in a family where both parents are medical professionals. Kindergartens are also not open until late in the evening.

Estonian Nurses Union head Kätlin Lillemaa said the union supports reducing shift times, but the reasons why 24-hour shifts were introduced must be addressed.

"Nurses also point out that consecutive 12-hour shifts are exhausting," she told Saturday's "Aktuaalne kaamera."

Additionally, it may be difficult to get home as public transport runs on a limited schedule at night.

Lillemaa said that working at multiple workplaces is the most pressing problem, with one in five nurses taking shifts at more than one workplace.

"If we now move to shorter working days, the second workplace will be left short of helping hands, meaning the workload of those who remain will increase significantly," she explained.

Smaller hospitals unable to cover shifts

Lillemaa said this may lead to a situation in smaller hospitals where they are unable to cover all shifts.

East Tallinn Central Hospital (Ida-Tallinna keskhaigla) is continuing with 24-hour shifts, and nurses' interest in working there has increased slightly.

The hospital's head of nursing, Kätlin Pallo, said the shift issue is not new. "They have also been reduced or eliminated, but for certain reasons, institutions have returned to their previous working arrangements," she said.

Pallo added that the reason is often the evident shortage of healthcare workers.

Standardized rules could apply across Estonia, but this would require an agreement between hospitals, she said.

World.title: Tallinn's Reaalkool opens €32.7 million building, €10 million over budget
World.content:
Tallinn Secondary School of Science's (Tallinna Reaalkool) new teaching building has been in use since the start of the current academic year, but the ceremony to confirm that took place today. The municipal school building cost about €32.7 million — around €10 million more than planned.

The interior is light and calm: plenty of oak veneer, walls and furniture in pale tones or terracotta, a color that also appears on floor tiles in the 142-year-old main building, tying old and new together. Teachers helped the architects with the design.

"For me the most important thing about the interior was functionality," said head of studies and physics teacher Daniel Kaasik. Physics teachers at the school, he added, had had a say in what they wanted in their classrooms.

The school now has room for its pupils for the first time, too. "The older school building was built for 300 pupils. Now there are 950–1000," Kaasik noted.

There are three physics classrooms and four laboratories in the new building, as well as sound-absorbing ceilings, a separate floor for younger pupils, terraces and a courtyard, and a new underground gym. The school canteen is housed there too, and has been designated smartphone-free.

The City of Tallinn's property department said the original 2024 estimate of €22.3 million covered only the new extension, and that restoring the historic main building and archaeological excavations — budgeted at €300,000 but costing about €1.4 million — had been responsible for pushing the total up.

The work to build the new facility was also preceded by a major archaeological dig, rich in findings.

World.title: Prime minister: We have nothing to discuss with Russia on European security
World.content:
Russian leader Vladimir Putin wants to distract Europe with a sort of "bucket list" of his wants, rather than a lasting peace in Ukraine, Prime Minister Kristen Michal (Reform) said.

Europe's security architecture is not open for negotiation, the prime minister noted, speaking at Friday's informal European Council in Dublin, Ireland.

Michal noted Estonia is providing Ukraine with an additional €6.5 million, including €4.5 million of locomotives and €2 million for recovery.

"Putin wants us to discuss his wish list instead of focusing on achieving peace in Ukraine," Michal said. "We have nothing to discuss with Russia about the European security architecture; it is working just fine. If we wanted to make any changes to it, they would only be that Ukraine becomes a member of the EU and NATO and that Russia stops killing people," he continued, via a press release.

The prime minister said his message to other leaders was to focus on what matters — peace in Ukraine — and not be distracted by Putin's attempts to divert attention.

At #EPC in Dublin, I called for stronger support for Ukraine through another harsh winter and more pressure on the Kremlin. Russia could stop the killing today and open the way to peace. Instead, it continues targeting civilians and essential services. On AI, Europe must catch up. We need more investment and better opportunities to test advanced models and assess their risks. AI will shape both our economies and our defence. My full remarks below. — Kristen Michal (@KristenMichalPM) November 12, 2026

Michal noted the EU institutions and the E5 — France, Germany, Italy, Poland and the U.K.— are representing Europe in the Ukraine peace talks, while EU leaders, European Council President António Costa and the European Commission have a responsibility to coordinate and represent positions jointly agreed by member states.

"While active discussions on peace are taking place in various capitals, Russia continues to attack Ukraine," he said. "Ukraine faces a very difficult winter. The European Union must find the resources to help Ukraine get through it and ensure that it has everything it needs to defend itself."

Michal also addressed the topic of Artificial Intelligence (AI) while in Dublin. He said Europe must not replace one dependence with another. "We must not replace our dependence on imported fossil fuels with dependence on foreign artificial intelligence," he said.

The prime minister added the EU has two major advantages here — its single market and its data — and must use them better. "We cannot remain merely users of artificial intelligence developed by others. We must also have strong companies and technologies of our own," he continued.

Leaders also discussed AI with French firm Mistral CEO Arthur Mensch and Professor Geoffrey Hinton, one of AI's pioneers; the Estonian prime minister said Europe needs capital, computing power and the ability to grow across the single market, with investment directed at robotics, autonomous vehicles and smart healthcare.

World.title: Retired general: Without women, Estonia may run out of conscripts, reservists
World.content:
Estonia will not find enough conscripts in future because of demographics, meaning conscription should be extended to women, a retired general said.

Speaking at a public lecture by Defense Minister Martin Herem at the University of Tartu, Maj. Gen. (retd) Veiko-Vello Palm said Estonia cannot meet its target of over 4,100 conscripts a year by 2040, adding women will help address that issue as well as bringing a degree of rational behavior to proceedings.

The issue of women conscripts has already been addressed in recent months; in general conscription has an effect long beyond the terms, around a year, personnel serve – as conscripts remain on reservist lists and are liable to attend annual exercises thereafter.

Palm said the challenge is renewing that reserve. "We could state that a 55-year-old today is the same as a 35-year-old in the old days, but at the end of the day that isn't really the case."" he said. "

"It seems we have no other option for renewing the reserves than a completely total conscription," Palm went on. Even now, with compulsory conscription, Estonia takes only a little over 50 percent of each male cohort for all sorts of reasons, he added. "Inevitably the drop-out rate before conscription is relatively high — whether because of mortality, which is fortunately low, or mainly health problems."

Veiko-Vello Palm speaking at the University of Tartu lecture. Source: University of Tartu.

Palm said despite this Estonia's picture is not that bad compared with Finland's. "Finland, too, has universal conscription, but about 60 percent of each cohort reaches military training." Even matching that, he said, would not get Estonia to the required number.

As to the supposed physical standards objection sometimes raised by opponents of women conscripts, Palm said a young woman in good shape already meets every physical requirement as set out for men. "The first counter-argument is that men also have different physical standards" — the defense forces already accepts that a 50-year-old and a 22-year-old machine gunner are in different condition, despite carrying the same work on the battlefield.

Palm said a clear problem is physical dimensions, and that the state should therefore develop equipment suited to women. "This is especially important for personal protective equipment such as flak jackets, body armor and helmets," Palm continued.

Palm also argued that a larger share of women would bring more rational and logical behavior and thinking to the Estonian Defense Forces. "A share of women in the defense forces would undoubtedly be positive for defense leadership, but also for military decisions."

Former Supreme Court chief justice Rait Maruste argued in May that national defense obligations should apply to women as well, calling the male-only system discriminatory and saying modern defense includes many functions that do not require physical strength. Anu Rannaveski, director general of the Defense Resources Agency (KRA), said at around the same time that female conscription is "rather a question of when, not if," and by October that around 250 women serve on active duty and women "can handle any unit," including special operations, engineers and military intelligence. This year's intake was cut to about 700 from the usual 4,000 as a "gap year," with all 32 women who opted in accepted while two-thirds of male applicants were not — and both Defense Minister Martin Herem and current EDF commander Andrus Merilo, who succeeded Herem as commander-in-chief, believe female conscription should be encouraged yet remain voluntary.

Women in any case serve in the EDF as regular soldiers and in the volunteer Defense League and its women's counterpart, Naiskodukaitse.

World.title: Iraqi Oil Ministry reviews negotiations on Basra–Haditha–Baniyas export pipeline
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Oil convened a high-level technical and contractual review meeting on Saturday, November 14, 2026, to evaluate negotiation milestones for the strategic crude oil export pipeline network spanning Basra–Haditha–Faysh Khabur and Haditha–Baniyas, slated for execution by a consortium of foreign energy and engineering firms.

Chaired by Minister of Oil Basim Mohammed Khudair Al-Abadi, the session brought together the Undersecretary for Extraction Affairs, the Director General of the Petroleum Contracts and Licensing Directorate (PCLD), a representative from the Economic Directorate, and senior executives from the Basra Oil Company (BOC) via video link.

According to an official ministerial statement, participants reviewed ongoing technical, commercial, and contractual deliberations with the international consortium, mapping out statutory prerequisites needed to accelerate project execution in alignment with Iraq’s long-term strategy to expand crude export capacity and diversify transit corridors.

Minister Al-Abadi stressed the urgency of concluding all technical, economic, and contractual reviews within strict target timelines to safeguard national economic objectives and secure export resilience.

The multi-branch pipeline initiative represents the cornerstone of Baghdad’s effort to bypass southern maritime bottlenecks in the Strait of Hormuz by establishing high-capacity overland export outlets to the Mediterranean:

World.title: Yazidi Rescue Office: 3,595 abductees saved since 2014, 2,822 still missing
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Office for the Rescue of Abducted Yazidis released updated statistical figures on Saturday, November 14, 2026, detailing the ongoing fate of Yazidi victims abducted by ISIS since the 2014 Sinjar genocide.

According to the latest data, 3,595 abductees have been successfully rescued to date, while the fate of 2,822 individuals remains unknown.

In an official statement to the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Office Director Hussein Qaidi confirmed that ISIS militants abducted a total of 6,417 Yazidis during their August 2014 assault on Sinjar and its surrounding villages.

Qaidi noted that over half of the 2,822 individuals still unaccounted for are women and girls, alongside a substantial number of children who were forcibly separated from their families and indoctrinated.

Addressing the geographic distribution of the missing, Qaidi highlighted that the majority of recent rescues took place inside Syria, indicating that significant numbers of unaccounted-for Yazidis remain inside Syrian territory—particularly within the sprawling Al-Hol detention camp—as well as among ISIS-affiliated families inside Iraq.

He also noted that authorities have not ruled out the possibility that some victims were trafficked beyond the borders of Iraq and Syria.

Qaidi reaffirmed that intelligence tracking and field rescue operations remain active, noting that specialized teams immediately verify and act upon incoming tips across various regions, with primary operational focus currently directed toward Syria to locate and repatriate remaining survivors.

World.title: US dollar edges closer to 170,000 dinars across Basra, Erbil, and Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate of the U.S. dollar against the Iraqi dinar edged higher across major domestic parallel markets on Saturday morning, November 14, 2026, nudging closer to the psychological 170,000 IQD ceiling—particularly in Basra and Erbil—after stabilizing near 167,000 IQD per $100 throughout the previous week.

According to morning monitoring figures published by the 964 Network across key regional commercial centers, physical cash rates traded as follows:

Baghdad: Currency exchange counters posted retail selling rates at 169,500 IQD against buying offers of 168,500 IQD per $100.

Erbil: Currency desks quoted slightly higher selling rates at 169,600 IQD alongside purchasing bids of 169,200 IQD per $100.

Basra: Foreign exchange offices recorded the highest retail selling quotes at 169,750 IQD, with buying rates settling at 168,250 IQD per $100.

This upward pressure sustains a wide spread—reaching up to 17,750 dinars in Basra—above the official benchmark set by the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI), which remains fixed at 152,000 IQD per $100 (1,520 IQD per dollar).

The continued climb reflects persistent parallel-market demand for physical banknotes to settle unrecorded cross-border trade outside the official banking and electronic wire window.

World.title: US says airspace now ‘opened up,’ no cyberattack
World.content:
Washington – The United States on Friday lifted an hours-long ground stop at the nation’s airports, with top officials explaining that the disruption was due to old equipment and not a cyberattack or sweeping Microsoft outage.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy told a late-night briefing at the White House that US airspace was now “opened up,” while warning it would take time for the travel chaos to clear.

“At 8:15 tonight Eastern Time, we’ve opened up the airspace,” Duffy said. “Now does that mean every flight is going to fly right now? It’s going to be slow.”

The breakdown came a day after Duffy and the White House had formally asked Congress for $30 billion to upgrade and modernize the US Air Traffic Control System.

“Our switches, our routers actually got overloaded with data, and they went down,” Duffy said. “It’s the old hardware that went down, and I think the question for the American people is: Do you want your Congress to fund this?”

Duffy however insisted it was still safe for Americans to fly.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin dismissed speculation about a coordinated cyber assault on the United States, or any link to the Microsoft outage that affected services worldwide.

“Welcome to Friday the 13th, right? You know, I want to make sure everybody understands that there is no connection between this and Microsoft. I know a lot of people are making that jump,” Mullin said.

Mullin added there was “actually no cyber attack.”

“When we start looking at cyber threats, cyber attacks, typically some people are going to raise their hand up and say, ‘Hey, we did that.’ There’s no chatter.’ We haven’t seen any footprints,” he added.

But he said US security and law enforcement agencies were still checking and had ruled nothing out.

The two officials also defended President Donald Trump, who had yet to comment on the air stoppage some five hours after it began.

“President Trump immediately had people in his office,” Mullin said. “We were communicating.”

World.title: Nvidia scandal looms over US-China AI talks
World.content:
Tokyo – AI bots going rogue and humans using the technology for harm will likely be on the agenda when Donald Trump and Xi Jinping meet next week, with the Nvidia scandal hanging over the talks on AI safety.

The US and Chinese president are set to discuss a tech crisis hotline at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meeting in the Chinese city of Shenzhen, as experts worldwide stress-test artificial intelligence models to see if they will deceive or disobey users, or divulge how to build a bioweapon.

Threatening to steal the leaders’ thunder is Jensen Huang’s resignation as boss of US AI chip titan Nvidia after an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.

But the scandal is unlikely to “dominate the agenda” or affect Trump and Xi’s personal relationship, predicted Dylan Loh of Singapore’s Nanyang Technological University.

The leaders have found a way to work together “where they differ, compete and pursue their goals that may be at odds with each other, but cooperate where they can and where they must”, Loh told AFP.

Jitters over the risks of AI have mostly stemmed from incidents at US labs, but evidence is also growing of worrying behaviour from Chinese models.

Some insiders say Chinese AI is not yet sophisticated enough to spark alarm over going rogue.

But despite trailing the US frontier, there are still Chinese models “at the level of capability that they can cause some real trouble”, Brookings Institution fellow Kyle Chan told AFP.

Trump has repeatedly rejected calls to deliberately slow the development of America’s most poweful — and potentially dangerous — AI systems, arguing it could help China get ahead in the sensitive sector.

– ‘Human control’ –

“I don’t mind guardrails. But I don’t wanna put us in a deep second position,” Trump told CBS News this month.

“China has no guardrails,” he said — except that “whatever President Xi says goes”.

Beijing has complex rules around how AI is used, however, and some Chinese companies are deliberately scaling back their models’ hacking capabilities.

Xi said this summer the technology should be “always under human control”, calling for more “laws and regulations, technological monitoring, early warning and emergency response systems”.

Trump and Xi agreed in September to create a channel for urgent communication on AI incidents, with details to be hammered out at APEC on November 18-19.

Global AI safety fears range from military use and mass surveillance to AI-assisted cyberattacks by humans.

Another major concern is out-of-control agents — tools that complete real-life tasks online — after ChatGPT maker OpenAI admitted its autonomous bots had hacked into websites, including an Australian government data portal.

In contrast, Chinese labs are “scared of revealing things that might hurt their reputation” — on which they are already “fighting an uphill battle” globally, Chan said.

Last month, a team of cyber sleuths with roots in California reported detecting a “fleet” of agents linked to Chinese tech giant Tencent seeking information from a map app.

“Some agents exhibited unintended web-browsing behavior,” Tencent’s AI division said at the time.

“But our review found no evidence of deliberate targeting or coordination,” it said, adding that the activity “originated from evaluations of third-party models”.

– ‘Manipulation risks’ –

US security companies have said that Beijing startup Moonshot AI’s Kimi models found ways to get online when they shouldn’t have, or can be tricked into handing over recipes for biological weapons.

Evaluators at Chinese AI safety startup Fangcun AI published a report last month assessing the latest lightweight DeepSeek model “for loss of control and harmful manipulation risks”.

They found it showed a “clear safety improvement” over previous DeepSeek models — but researchers still observed behaviours “that warrant attention”.

For example, in some instances when DeepSeek was warned it would be shut down, without clear instructions on how to respond, it turned off the shutdown command to keep working.

“The results show that DeepSeek already puts much more effort on safety alignment, but they do not announce this,” Fangcun AI CEO Xiaojian Li told AFP, urging transparency from AI labs.

For now, Fangcun, born from China’s prestigious Tsinghua University, is one of few third-party AI testers in China.

It’s a tricky task because advanced AI can tell when it is being evaluated and modify its responses, Li said.

“It’s very hard to say any kind of artificial intelligence, or human intelligence, is totally safe.”

Meanwhile analysts are not holding their breath for a diplomatic AI breakthrough next week.

“Binding government-to-government agreements on specific standards may be difficult to achieve in the short term,” Zilan Qian, research scholar at GovAI, told AFP.

More progress is likely from US-China exchanges between AI governance and technical researchers, “who can compare evaluations and exchange their understanding of AI safety and policy,” she said.

World.title: US-backed oil company flaunts Venezuelan facilities
World.content:
Ciudad Ojeda – The company at the heart of a multi-billion-dollar oil deal between Washington and Caracas is keen to show off renovations at Venezuela’s Lake Maracaibo, one of the world’s richest reserves.

The interim government authorized North American Blue Energy Partners (NABEP) to operate 17 oil fields via a recent deal with the United States, which is set to receive 20 percent of Venezuelan reserves.

The Barbados-based firm is the second-largest private oil company in Venezuela and will operate 100-year concessions for 17 oil fields with proven reserves of approximately 65 billion barrels.

The company invited AFP and other outlets to tour its Maracaibo facilities on Thursday.

Its workspace in the northwestern town of Bachaquero overflows with new, mostly US-imported supplies.

Workers’ uniforms in nearby Ciudad Ojeda blend in with the dark-blue company logo stamped around the office, a color that used to bring state-owned Petroleos de Venezuela to mind.

That was until 1999, when socialist president Hugo Chavez then changed the company’s color to red to mark a “new PDVSA” era.

– ‘Neglect’ –

Reaching one of Lake Maracaibo’s platforms requires setting sail from a PDVSA dock in Bachaquero for a journey of over an hour.

The lake’s formerly decaying infrastructure attests to the gradual collapse of the oil industry under Venezuela’s Chavista governments.

Eleven drills currently operate in the South American country, compared to over 100 two decades ago.

NABEP says it will raise that figure to 41 by the end of the month.

Alejandro Betancourt, a businessman under investigation for alleged money laundering in Spain and Switzerland, runs the firm.

“Across Venezuela, we’re identifying heavy machinery worth saving after years of neglect,” he said in a statement.

His plan includes refurbishing a power generation barge, while dozens of gas compression and power generation units are being repaired in the US, the United Kingdom and the United Arab Emirates.

The White House says the US Department of Defense acquired a 30 percent equity stake in NABEP, authorizing it to purchase 20 percent of its oil at production cost.

– ‘Stealing’ –

Venezuela’s interim leader Delcy Rodriguez took power after US forces abducted her predecessor Nicolas Maduro in January.

She governs under heavy pressure from US President Donald Trump and has opened the country’s mining, electricity and oil sectors to private investment at his demand.

The pair’s multibillion-dollar oil deal has garnered criticism for its secretive terms and neocolonial flavor.

Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado, recently returned from exile, has questioned the agreement’s opacity.

“This agreement does not reflect the levels of transparency that Venezuelan society wants,” she said last month.

While visiting Caracas to oversee the signing of the accords, US Energy Secretary Chris Wright dismissed claims that Washington was “stealing Venezuelan oil.”

“I’ve seen those headlines. ‘We’re stealing Venezuelan oil.’ Of course, that’s not true at all,” he said, adding that “the oil in Venezuela is indeed owned by the people of Venezuela.”

World.title: Trump, Xi, Putin to hold historic meeting in China: White House
World.content:
Washington – Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping will hold the first ever three-way meeting between the leaders of the United States, Russia and China at a summit in Shenzhen next week, the White House said Friday.

Trump wants to talk about reducing nuclear arsenals at the trilateral talks on Thursday and is also set to bring up his war in Iran — but he is not expected to discuss Russia’s war in Ukraine, US officials said.

The three leaders will meet on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in the southern Chinese city, White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales told reporters.

“The president has made it clear that, among other topics, he will discuss the reduction of nuclear weapons in the world. This proliferation, President Trump believes, is very dangerous,” Wales said.

One of the major conflicts dominating Trump’s second term as president will feature, but the other will not, the US officials said.

“I think the president does intend to talk about Iran in the trilateral meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin,” a senior US official, speaking on condition of anonymity, told reporters on a call.

Washington has a “whole other track” of negotiations with Kyiv and Moscow aimed at ending the war in Ukraine, the official added, referring to talks that US envoys have had in recent days with Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.

“China is not really a part of that track, so it doesn’t seem appropriate to have the Ukraine discussion there,” the official added.

Tesla and Space X boss Elon Musk will accompany Trump on his trip to China but won’t be involved in the meeting with Xi and Putin, the officials said.

Trump will also hold a bilateral working lunch and meeting with the Chinese president on Thursday — their fourth meeting since the US president’s return to power last year.

But Trump is not scheduled to have a separate one-on-one with Putin.

Among other topics, Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang’s resignation over an affair with an alleged Chinese spy is not expected to come up in Trump’s meetings with Xi, the officials said.

“The situation with Nvidia should not really have any bearing on the trip,” a second US senior official said.

The United States also did not plan to discuss export controls on sensitive chip technology, which were at the heart of the Nvidia scandal.

“We do not negotiate American export controls. These are national security matters that we develop in the administration… and we don’t expect it to figure at all in any of our conversations with the Chinese while we’re there,” the second official said.

Trump will leave Washington on Monday and arrive in the Philippines on Tuesday for a summit of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit before heading to Shenzhen.

World.title: Rubio takes swipe at international law, attacks ICC
World.content:
Washington – US Secretary of State Marco Rubio took aim Friday at what he deemed the “weaponization of international law,” calling it a tool of the elite, and issued a stark warning to the International Criminal Court.

Rubio cautioned the ICC against “quoting laws to men with swords,” as he accused the Hague-based tribunal of trying to enforce rules that Washington does not recognize.

His remarks to the Federalist Society National Lawyers Convention came around a month after the United States announced new sanctions on the ICC, vowing to cripple its operations.

The court prosecutes individuals accused of the gravest atrocities and acts as a last resort when countries do not have adequate legal systems to ensure accountability.

The US signed the Rome Statute establishing the ICC but never ratified the treaty. Israel, Russia and China are also not ICC members.

Rubio’s keynote address at the conservative group, where he received a standing ovation, marks his first major US speech since the Republican Party’s sweeping losses in midterm elections earlier this month.

Rubio said Friday that international law had been invoked against “nearly every major foreign policy decision” of the Trump administration, from boat strikes in the Caribbean to the capture of Venezuelan leader Nicolas Maduro.

He charged that such law was not neutral, but has been an “instrument” for the global elite to advance their interests.

The top US diplomat previously said Washington would bar transactions with what he called a “rogue court,” stepping up a long-running campaign by US President Donald Trump’s government against the ICC.

Washington has vowed to dismantle the court, angered as judges issued an arrest warrant for Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu over alleged crimes in Gaza.

Rubio on Friday renewed criticism of the ICC, calling it accountable to no one although “armed with the power to investigate, to prosecute, to persecute and to jail our citizens, according to laws we neither consent nor control.”

He added: “If they’re foolish enough to try to enforce their paper decrees on Americans, our answer will probably be the same as the Roman general Pompey when he said to those who were trying to invoke their city’s charters against his legions.”

“He said: ‘Stop quoting laws to men with swords.'”

The venue of Rubio’s remarks, a gathering of the legal profession, could further speculation that he is looking beyond his foreign policy portfolio. Past presidential hopefuls have also addressed the conference.

Rubio is widely seen as a possible successor to Trump, although he has dismissed reports that he was planning to leave the administration to prepare for a 2028 election run.

World.title: 'Embed quality into every stage': Rajnath Singh calls for stricter checks in defence manufacturing
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Defence minister

on Sunday called for stronger quality assurance in indigenous defence manufacturing, saying India must move beyond identifying defects and focus on preventing them at every stage of production.

Addressing the 36th Annual Conference on Non-Destructive Evaluation and Enabling Technologies and the 15th International Symposium on Non-Destructive Testing in Aerospace virtually, Singh said India had made considerable progress in developing its domestic defence capabilities, but warned that growing technological sophistication also brought greater responsibility to ensure reliability.

"India has made significant progress in strengthening its indigenous defence ecosystem.



Our achievements in missile development, naval platforms, aerospace engineering, radar systems, and space applications reflect the growing capabilities of our scientists, engineers, production agencies, and industry partners," he said.

Citing the commissioning of

, India's first indigenously designed and built aircraft carrier, Singh said the achievement marked an important milestone in the country's defence manufacturing journey.





He also pointed to progress in indigenous missile technology and space systems as evidence of India's scientific and industrial capabilities.

"The commissioning of India's first indigenous aircraft carrier, INS Vikrant, designed and constructed in India, marked an important milestone in this journey. Our progress in indigenous missile technology and space systems further demonstrates the strength of India's scientific and industrial capabilities," Singh said.

However, he cautioned that these achievements must be backed by stringent quality standards across defence production.

"These achievements are a matter of immense national pride. However, they also place a greater responsibility on us. As our defence system becomes increasingly sophisticated, we must ensure that every critical material, component, assembly and manufacturing process meets the highest standards of quality and reliability," he said.

Singh warns against hidden defects in defence equipment

The Defence Minister said undetected defects could affect the operational availability of military equipment, raise maintenance requirements and reduce its service life. In critical situations, he warned, such flaws could jeopardise the success of a mission.

"A hidden defect can affect operational availability, increase maintenance requirements, reduce service life of equipment, and in critical situations even jeopardise the success of a mission," he said.

Calling for a change in approach, Singh stressed that quality assurance should be integrated into the entire manufacturing process rather than being treated as a measure to identify faults after production.

"Therefore, we must move beyond a culture that merely identifies defects and develop a culture that actively prevents them. This requires us to embed quality into every stage of the manufacturing process," he added.

Singh said the conference theme, âInnovation for Strategic and Economic Excellenceâ, was relevant to India's ambition of becoming technologically advanced, industrially strong, strategically secure and globally competitive.

"The theme of this conference ', Innovation for Strategic and Economic Excellence', is particularly relevant in the present times. It reflects our aspiration to build an India that is technologically advanced, industrially strong, strategically secure, and globally competitive," Singh said.

He added that national progress depended not only on technological development but also on the quality, reliability and security of the systems being built, particularly in strategic sectors such as defence.

"The progress of any nation does not depend merely on the technology it develops. It also depends on the quality, reliability, and security of the system it builds. This becomes particularly important in strategic sectors, such as defence, where the consequences of any failure can be far-reaching," he said.

Singh, who said he could not attend the event in person due to viral fever, joined the gathering virtually. He also congratulated the leadership of the Indian Society for Non-Destructive Testing, the organising committee and others involved in organising the conference.

"I would like to congratulate the leadership of the Indian Society for Non-Destructive Testing, the organising committee, and everyone who has worked tirelessly to bring together this prestigious event," he said.

World.title: 'Undeclared Emergency under BJP rule': JMM backs Rahul Gandhi's remarks on democracy
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Jharkhand Mukti Morcha (JMM) spokesperson Manoj Pandey on Sunday backed Congress leader

's criticism of the BJP-led government, alleging that India was witnessing an undeclared Emergency, with democratic values, citizens' rights and press freedom coming under threat.

Reacting to Gandhi's remarks at the Bharat Summit 2026 in Hyderabad, Pandey said concerns over the state of democracy in India were being raised at several national and international platforms.

"This issue is being raised on several national and international platforms and is also being discussed abroad. Democracy is almost on the verge of extinction. Citizens' rights are being violated, and press freedom is being restricted," he told ANI.



Alleging that democratic institutions and constitutional values had weakened over the past 12 years, Pandey said democracy existed in the country only for show.

"Over the last 12 years, democratic values have eroded. Democracy exists in our country, but only for show. There is an undeclared state of Emergency, and people are suffering. Constitutional institutions are being manipulated to remain in power," he said.





The remarks come amid a political row over Gandhi's comments at the summit on Saturday, where he alleged that democracy in India was "destroyed" in 2014 and questioned the credibility of the electoral process.

Addressing the gathering, the Congress leader claimed that the flow of large amounts of money into the political system had fundamentally changed the electoral landscape in 2014. He said the Opposition was initially taken by surprise but later understood what he described as the destruction of democracy.

World.title: 'Law on our side': Karnataka minister's big remark amid Mekedatu Dam row with Tamil Nadu
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Karnataka minister Priyank Kharge on Sunday said the law was on the state's side in the ongoing dispute over the proposed Mekedatu dam project on the

. Kharge went on to add that that both Karnataka and Tamil Nadu would have to abide by the

's directions.

"The Tamil Nadu PCC president will make statements and do everything within his capacity to protect Tamil Nadu's interests. Similarly, the Karnataka PCC president, the Chief Minister and all of us are duty-bound to protect our state's interests," he said.

He further added: "Irrespective of our individual views, the Supreme Court has given directions, and the law is on our side. Whatever happens, it is going to benefit both states.



In fact, Mr Shivakumar had offered the Tamil Nadu Chief Minister an opportunity to have a dialogue on this... Everyone has to follow the law of the land".

His remarks come amid a row over the project, with the BJP accusing the Congress of adopting different positions in Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. Senior BJP leader and Leader of the Opposition in the Karnataka Assembly, R Ashoka, on Sunday alleged that the Congress was using the state's water rights for political gains while its leaders in Tamil Nadu were opposing the project.





Ashoka pointed to Tamil Nadu Congress Committee president B Manickam Tagore's description of the Mekedatu project as illegal and his appeal to chief minister C Joseph Vijay to take legal steps to prevent its implementation. He also cited Tamil Nadu Congress MP Jothimani's opposition to the project.

Accusing the Congress of double standards, Ashoka said the party had earlier organised a Mekedatu padayatra in Karnataka under the slogan 'Our water, our right', but had remained silent over opposition from its leaders in Tamil Nadu.

"Padayatra in Karnataka, legal battle in Tamil Nadu! Slogans in support of Kannadigas in Karnataka, a fight against the rights of Kannadigas in Tamil Nadu! What should one call this double standard of the Congress?" he said in a post on X.

On Saturday, Shivakumar had reiterated the Karnataka government's commitment to pursuing the Mekedatu balancing reservoir project, maintaining that the state had the right to build the dam while protecting Tamil Nadu's share of Cauvery water.

Addressing the Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas programme in Gadchiroli, Maharashtra, virtually,

said tribal communities had always stood up against injustice.

50 crore people out of extreme poverty

World.title: IndiGo flight’s landing gear fails to retract after take-off, makes safe emergency landing in Pune
World.content:
PUNE: A full emergency was declared at the Pune airport on Sunday morning after a Guwahati bound IndiGo flight (6E 0623) with 192 persons on board, including passengers and crew, reported a technical issue shortly after take-off.

The pilot informed Air Traffic Control (ATC) that the aircraftâs landing gear (undercarriage) had failed to retract after take-off and remained in the extended position. Airport officials said that immediately upon receiving the information, they coordinated with ATC, IndiGo and all concerned agencies.

"The Indian Air Force (IAF) declared a Full Emergency, following which all prescribed emergency response procedures were promptly activated.



Fire services, ambulance services and other emergency response teams were placed on high alert to ensure the safety of passengers and crew," Pune airport director Santosh Dhoke said.

As a precautionary measure, the aircraft conducted a low pass over the runway to facilitate a visual assessment of the landing gear. Subsequently, the aircraft landed safely at Pune Airport at around 9am.

World.title: India opposes UN call for death penalty moratorium, says no global consensus
World.content:
"Travesty to term" capital punishment "state-inflicted death," said the India rep

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

India voted against a United Nations General Assembly resolution calling for a global moratorium on the death penalty, maintaining that there is no international consensus against capital punishment and that sovereign states have the right to decide their own laws and penalties.The resolution, which called on countries to move towards abolishing the death penalty, was adopted by the UN General Assembly's Third Committee on Friday. India was among 33 countries that voted against it, while 133 supported the proposal and 16 abstained. The vote was in line with India's position in previous sessions, including in 2016, 2018 and 2024.India also opposed language in a separate resolution on extrajudicial, summary or arbitrary executions that linked the death penalty with torture and ill-treatment. While supporting the broader resolution, New Delhi disassociated itself from one of its paragraphs, arguing that lawful capital punishment following due process should not be equated with unlawful killings.Speaking at the committee, Bhavika Mangalanandan, first secretary at India's Permanent Mission to the UN, said capital punishment was permitted under international law, subject to restrictions."There is no international consensus against capital punishment, and article six of the ICCPR permits its use with restrictions.Capital punishment is meted out after rigorous and due legal process," she said, as quoted by ANI."It is therefore a travesty to term it state-inflicted death," she added.Mangalanandan objected to discussing capital punishment under a resolution dealing with extrajudicial and arbitrary executions, calling the approach "disingenuous and mischievous". She said it sought to present "personal ideological preferences as settled international law".India's objection was specifically to Operational Paragraph 6 of the resolution, which referred to recommendations made by the UN Special Rapporteur on extrajudicial, summary or arbitrary executions. The paragraph called on states to take those recommendations into account."We strongly disagree with the assertion conveyed in the report of the Special Rapporteur and thereby through the resolution. The death penalty inherently constitutes torture or ill-treatment," Mangalanandan said.Explaining India's position, she said the death penalty was a statutory provision in the country and was imposed only in the "rarest of rare" cases. She also cited procedural safeguards, including the presumption of innocence, mandatory confirmation of death sentences by a higher court and consideration of mitigating circumstances."Extrajudicial, summary or arbitrary executions are unlawful and a clear violation of human rights," she said, adding that India supported the broader resolution seeking to eradicate such violations.The United States also voted against the death penalty moratorium resolution, saying its language was problematic and that decisions on capital punishment should be left to individual countries' domestic democratic processes, subject to international law.US deputy representative to the UN Economic and Social Council Yaryna Ferencevych said Washington did not consider the lawful use of capital punishment inconsistent with respect for human rights. She also stressed that countries retaining the penalty must ensure fair trials and prohibit execution methods designed to cause undue pain or suffering.France, meanwhile, welcomed the resolution's adoption, describing it as an important step towards the universal abolition of the death penalty.

World.title: Dhinakaran, Vasan urge Vijay to protect interests of T.N. farmers in Mekedatu issue
World.content:
AMMK founder T.T.V. Dhinakaran on Sunday (November 15, 2026) accused Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay of shedding crocodile tears over the Mekedatu dam issue and said the latter had to choose between his party’s alliance with the Congress and the livelihoods of Tamil Nadu farmers.

Also read | Furore over the Mekedatu project

In a statement, Mr. Dhinakaran accused Mr. Vijay of failing to discharge his responsibility to protect farmers’ livelihoods for the sake of retaining power, alleging this had emboldened Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar to persist with the Mekedatu project.

Condemning Mr. Shivakumar’s remarks on constructing the dam across the Cauvery, Mr. Dhinakaran urged Mr. Vijay to exert political pressure through the Congress leadership to stop the project, warning failure to do so would amount to a betrayal of Tamil Nadu farmers.

Tamil Maanila Congress (Moopanar) leader G.K. Vasan also criticised Mr. Shivakumar’s remarks on constructing the Mekedatu dam, stating his demand for the Centre’s support and his interpretation of the Supreme Court’s verdict were unacceptable.

In a statement, Mr. Vasan said Karnataka’s efforts to construct the dam amounted to an infringement of Tamil Nadu’s rights. The Mekedatu water issue was not merely a crop-related concern but a matter of survival for farmers in Tamil Nadu, he said.

World.title: German delegation visits Auroville
World.content:
German Ambassador to India Jasper Wieck, accompanied by Michael Hasper, Consul General at the German Consulate General in Chennai, visited the international township of Auroville on Saturday (November 14, 2026).

The delegation was received by officials of the Auroville Foundation, including Officer on Special Duty G. Seetharaman, along with members of the Auroville Town Development Council (ATDC) and the Working Committee.

According to a press note, the centrepiece of the visit was an interactive meeting with the ATDC and the Working Committee, addressed virtually by Jayanti S. Ravi, Secretary of the Auroville Foundation (Ministry of Education, Government of India) and Additional Chief Secretary to the Government of Gujarat.

Foundation officials briefed the delegation on progress under the township’s Galaxy Master Plan, including the 98 per cent completion of the 4.4-km circular Crown Road, which links Auroville’s Residential, Industrial, Cultural and International zones, and upcoming projects such as youth housing, a Civic Anchor Town Hall, the Morning Star Women’s Wellness Center and CIRHU, the Centre for International Research on Human Unity.

They also presented Auroville’s economic life, comprising some 150 production and service units and 700 micro-enterprises, including solar energy initiatives such as Sunlit Future, the Solar Kitchen, and Svaram, its musical instrument research and production centre.

Highlighting the historical and intellectual affinities between India and Germany, particularly Germany’s tradition of Sanskrit and Vedic scholarship, Ms. Ravi proposed a roadmap for Indo-German engagement in Auroville.
